Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Dīghanikāye

The Long Discourses

Mahāvaggaṭīkā

The Subcommentary on the Great Chapter

1. Mahāpadānasuttavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Great Discourse on the Lineage

Pubbenivāsapaṭisaṃyuttakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse Connected with Past Lives

1. Yathājātānaṃ [P 2.0001][V 2.0001][M 2.0001] karerirukkhānaṃ ghanapattasākhāviṭapehi maṇḍapasaṅkhepehi sañchanno padeso “karerimaṇḍapo”ti adhippeto. Dvāreti dvārasamīpe. Dvāre ṭhitarukkhavasena aññatthāpi samaññā atthīti dassetuṃ “yathā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kathaṃ pana bhagavā mahāgandhakuṭiyaṃ avasitvā tadā karerikuṭikāyaṃ vihāsīti? Sāpi buddhassa bhagavato vasanagandhakuṭi evāti dassento “antojetavane”tiādimāha. Salaḷāgāranti devadārurukkhehi katagehaṃ. Pakatibhattassa pacchatoti bhikkhūnaṃ pākatikabhattakālato pacchā, ṭhitamajjhanhikato uparīti attho. Piṇḍapātato paṭikkantānanti piṇḍapātabhojanato apetānaṃ. Tenāha “bhattakicca”ntiādi.

1. A place covered by the dense foliage, branches, and boughs of naturally grown kareri trees, which are reckoned as pavilions, is intended by the term 'kareri pavilion.' 'At the gate' means near the gateway. To show that the designation also exists elsewhere on account of trees standing at a gate, the words 'just as,' etc., are stated. But how is it that the Blessed One, having dwelt in the Great Fragrant Cell, then resided in the Kareri Hut? To show that this too was a fragrant dwelling chamber of the Blessed Buddha, he says 'inside Jeta's Grove,' etc. 'A pine house' means a house made from devadāru trees. 'After the regular meal' means after the bhikkhus' normal mealtime; the meaning is, after midday has passed. 'Of those who have returned from the alms round' means of those who have finished their meal from the alms round. Hence he says 'the meal duties,' etc.

Maṇḍalasaṇṭhānā [V 2.0002] māḷasaṅkhepena katā nisīdanasālā “maṇḍalamāḷa”nti adhippetāti āha “nisīdanasālāyā”ti. Pubbenivāsapaṭisaṃyuttāti ettha pubba-saddo atītavisayo, nivāsa-saddo kammasādhano, khandhavinimutto ca nivasitadhammo natthi, khandhā ca santānavaseneva pavattantīti āha “pubbenivutthakkhandhasantānasaṅkhātena pubbenivāsenā”ti. Yojetvāti [M 2.0002] visayabhāvena yojetvā. Pavattitāti kathitā. Dhammūpasaṃhitattā dhammato anapetāti dhammī. Tenāha “dhammasaṃyuttā”ti.

A seating hall made in a circular shape, reckoned as an upper-storied pavilion, is intended by 'circular pavilion'; thus he says 'of the seating hall.' Herein, in 'connected with past lives,' the word 'pubba' refers to the past. The word 'nivāsa' is an active noun. And there is no dwelt-in state apart from the aggregates, and the aggregates proceed only by way of a continuum; thus he says 'by the past dwelling, which is designated as the continuum of previously dwelt-in aggregates.' 'Having connected' means having connected it as an object. 'Was set forth' means was spoken. Because it is conjoined with the Dhamma and not apart from the Dhamma, it is a 'Dhamma talk.' Hence he says 'connected with the Dhamma.'

Udapādīti [P 2.0002] paduddhāro, tassa uppannā jātāti iminā sambandho. Taṃ panassā uppannākāraṃ pāḷiyaṃ saṅkhepatova dassitaṃ, vitthārato dassetuṃ “aho acchariya”ntiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha ke anussaranti, ke nānussarantīti padadvaye paṭhamaṃyeva sappapañcanaṃ, na itaranti tadeva puggalabhedato, kālavibhāgato, anussaraṇākārato, opammato niddisantena “titthiyā anussarantī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Aggappattakammavādinoti sikhāppattakammavādino “atthi kammaṃ atthi kammavipāko”ti (paṭi. ma. 1.234) evaṃ kammassakatāñāṇe ṭhitā tāpasaparibbājakā. Cattālīsaṃyeva kappe anussarantīti brahmajālādīsu (dī. ni. 1.33) bhagavatā tathā paricchijja vuttattā. Tato paraṃ na anussarantīti tathāvacanañca diṭṭhigatopaṭṭhakassa tesaṃ ñāṇassa paridubbalabhāvato.

'It arose' is the citation of the word; its connection is with 'its arising, its birth.' But the manner of its arising is shown only concisely in the Pāli text; to show it in detail, the passage beginning 'Oh, how wonderful!' is introduced. Therein, in the two phrases 'some recollect, some do not recollect,' the first is with proliferation, not the other. Thus, by indicating it with distinctions of persons, divisions of time, the manner of recollection, and by simile, it is said, 'The adherents of other teachings recollect,' etc. 'Those who are proponents of kamma that has reached the highest point' means ascetics and wanderers who have reached the pinnacle of the doctrine of kamma, established in the knowledge of kamma as one's own, holding: 'There is kamma, there is the result of kamma.' They recollect only forty eons, because it was stated so, having been delimited by the Blessed One, in such texts as the Brahmajāla Sutta. That they do not recollect beyond that is stated because of the extreme weakness of their knowledge, which is obstructed by the grip of views.

Sāvakāti mahāsāvakā tesañhi kappasatasahassaṃ pubbābhinīhāro. Pakatisāvakā pana tato ūnakameva anussaranti. Yasmā “kappānaṃ lakkhādhikaṃ ekaṃ, dve ca asaṅkhyeyyānī”ti kālavasena evaṃ parimāṇo yathākkamaṃ aggasāvakapaccekabuddhānaṃ puññañāṇābhinīhāro, sāvakabodhipaccekabodhipāramitāsambharaṇañca, tasmā vuttaṃ “dve aggasāvakā…pe… kappasatasahassañcā”ti. Yadi bodhisambhārasambharaṇakālaparicchinno tesaṃ tesaṃ ariyānaṃ abhiññāñāṇavibhavo, evaṃ sante buddhānampissa saparicchedatā āpannāti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “buddhānaṃ pana ettakanti paricchedo natthi, yāvatakaṃ ākaṅkhanti, tāvatakaṃ anussarantī”ti “yāvatakaṃ neyyaṃ, tāvatakaṃ ñāṇa”nti (mahāni. 156; cūḷani. 85; paṭi. ma. 3, 5) vacanato. Sabbaññutaññāṇassa viya hi buddhānaṃ abhiññāñāṇānampi savisaye paricchedo nāma natthi, tasmā yaṃ [P 2.0003] yaṃ ñātuṃ icchanti, te taṃ taṃ jānanti eva. Atha vā satipi kālaparicchede karuṇūpāyakosallapariggahādinā sātisayattā mahābodhisambhārānaṃ paññāpāramitāya pavattiānubhāvassa paricchedo nāma natthi, kuto tannimittakānaṃ abhiññāñāṇānanti vuttaṃ “buddhānaṃ…pe… natthī”ti.

'Disciples' means the great disciples, for their initial aspiration was made a hundred thousand eons ago. Ordinary disciples, however, recollect for a shorter period. Because 'one incalculable and a hundred thousand eons' and 'two incalculable eons' are the respective time periods for the aspiration for merit and knowledge of the chief disciples and paccekabuddhas, and for the accumulation of the perfections for the enlightenment of a disciple and the enlightenment of a paccekabuddha, therefore it is said: 'The two chief disciples… and a hundred thousand eons.' Anticipating the objection, 'If the power of the direct knowledges of the various noble ones is limited by the time spent accumulating the requisites for enlightenment, in that case it would follow that even for the Buddhas there is a limitation,' he says: 'But for the Buddhas there is no limitation such as "only this much"; they recollect as much as they wish,' in accordance with the statement: 'As far as the knowable extends, so far their knowledge extends.' For just as the omniscience of the Buddhas has no limitation within its own domain, so too their direct knowledges have no limitation. Therefore, whatever they wish to know, that they know. Alternatively, even if there is a limitation of time, because of the excellence of the great requisites for enlightenment due to their being embraced by compassion, skill in means, etc., there is no limitation to the powerful influence of the perfection of wisdom in its operation. How then could there be a limitation for the direct knowledges that are its sign? Hence it is said: 'For the Buddhas… there is none.'

Khandhapaṭipāṭiyāti [V 2.0003][M 2.0003] yathāpaccayaṃ anupubbapavattamānānaṃ khandhānaṃ anupubbiyā. Khandhappavattinti vedanādikkhandhappavattiṃ. Tesañhi anubhavanādiākāraggahaṇamassa sātisayaṃ, taṃ saññābhave tattha tattha anussaraṇavasena gahetvā gacchantā ekavokārabhave alabhantā “na passantī”ti vuttā, jāle patitā viya sakuṇā, macchā viya cāti adhippāyo. Kuṇṭhā viyāti dandhā viya. Paṅguḷā viyāti pīṭhasappino viya. Diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhantīti adhiccasamuppannikadiṭṭhiṃ gaṇhanti. Yaṭṭhikoṭihetukaṃ gamanaṃ yaṭṭhikoṭigamanaṃ khandhapaṭipāṭiyā amuñcanato.

'By the sequence of aggregates' means by the succession of the aggregates that proceed in sequence according to conditions. 'The occurrence of the aggregates' means the occurrence of the aggregates beginning with feeling. For them, the grasping of the modes of experiencing and so on is excellent. Taking this up by way of recollection here and there in the realm of perception, but not finding it in the one-constituent existence, they are said 'not to see.' The intention is that they are like birds fallen into a net, or like fish. 'Like the blunted' means like the slow. 'Like the lame' means like those who move by shuffling on their buttocks. 'They adopt a view' means they adopt the view of fortuitous origination. Walking that has the tip of a staff as its cause is 'stick-tip-walking,' because of not letting go of the sequence of aggregates.

Evaṃ santepīti kāmaṃ buddhasāvakāpi asaññabhave khandhappavattiṃ na passanti, evaṃ santepi te buddhasāvakā asaññabhavaṃ laṅghitvā parato anussaranti. “Vaṭṭe”tiādi tathā tesaṃ anussaraṇākāradassanaṃ. Buddhehi dinnanaye ṭhatvāti “yattha pañcakappasatāni rūpappavattiyeva, na arūpappavatti, so asaññabhavo”ti evaṃ sammāsambuddhehi desitāyaṃ dhammanettiyaṃ ṭhatvā. Evañhi antarā cutipaṭisandhiyo apassantā parato anussaranti seyyathāpi āyasmā sobhitoti (theragā. aṭṭha. 1.2.164 sobhitattheragāthāvaṇṇanā). So kira pubbenivāse ciṇṇavasī hutvā anupaṭipāṭiyā attano nibbattaṭṭhānaṃ [P 2.0004] anussaranto yāva asaññabhave attano acittakapaṭisandhi tāva addasa, tato paraṃ pañcakappasataparimāṇe kāle cutipaṭisandhiyo adisvā avasāne cutiṃ disvā “kiṃ nāmeta”nti āvajjayamāno nayavasena “asaññabhavo bhavissatī”ti niṭṭhaṃ agamāsi. Atha naṃ bhagavā taṃ kāraṇaṃ aṭṭhuppattiṃ katvā pubbenivāsaṃ anussarantānaṃ aggaṭṭhāne ṭhapesi. “Cutipaṭisandhiṃ oloketvā”ti idaṃ cutipaṭisandhivasena tesaṃ ñāṇassa saṅkamanadassanaṃ, tena sabbaso bhave anāmasitvā gantuṃ na sakkontīti dasseti.

This being so, although the Buddha's disciples do not see the occurrence of the aggregates in the realm of non-perception, still, having leapt over the realm of non-perception, they recollect beyond it. The words 'In the round,' etc., show their manner of recollection. 'Standing in the method given by the Buddhas' means standing in the guideline of the Dhamma taught by the Perfectly Self-Enlightened Buddhas thus: 'That is the realm of non-perception where for five hundred eons there is only the occurrence of form, not the occurrence of non-form.' For thus, without seeing the death and rebirth-linking in between, they recollect beyond, just like the Venerable Sobhita. He, it seems, having gained mastery over the recollection of past lives, while recollecting in sequence the places where he had been reborn, saw up to his own mind-less rebirth-linking in the realm of non-perception. Beyond that, not seeing any death and rebirth-linking for a period of five hundred eons, at the end he saw a death and, reflecting, 'What is this?', he came to the conclusion by inference: 'It must have been the realm of non-perception.' Then the Blessed One, having made that the occasion for a discourse, placed him in the foremost position among those who recollect past lives. 'Having looked at the death and rebirth-linking': this shows the transition of their knowledge by way of death and rebirth-linking. By this he shows that they are unable to proceed without touching upon existence in some way.

Taṃ tadeva passantīti yathā nāma saradasamaye ṭhitamajjhanhikavelāya caturatanike gehe cakkhumato purisassa rūpagataṃ supākaṭameva hotīti lokasiddhametaṃ, siyā pana tassa sukhumataratirohitādibhedassa rūpagatassa agocaratā. Na tveva buddhānaṃ ñātuṃ icchitassa ñeyyassa agocaratā, atha kho taṃ ñāṇālokena obhāsitaṃ hatthatale āmalakaṃ viya supākaṭaṃ suvibhūtameva hoti [M 2.0004] tathā ñeyyāvaraṇassa suppahīnattā. Tenāha “buddhā pana attanā vā parehi vā diṭṭhakatasutaṃ, sūriyamaṇḍalobhāsasadisa”nti ca ādi.

'They see that very thing.' Just as for a man with sight in a house adorned with the four gems at midday in the autumn season, a visible form is very plain—this is established in the world. But there might be an inability to perceive that visible form if it is of a more subtle, concealed, or other such kind. For the Buddhas, however, no knowable object that they wish to know is beyond their range. Rather, illuminated by the light of knowledge, it becomes very plain and distinct, like a myrobalan fruit on the palm of the hand, because the obstruction to the knowable has been completely abandoned. Hence he says: 'But for the Buddhas, what is seen, done, or heard by themselves or by others is like the light of the sun's disk,' etc.

Tathā sāvakā ca paccekabuddhā cāti. Ettha tathā-saddena “attanā diṭṭhakatasutameva anussarantī”ti [V 2.0004] idaṃ upasaṃharati, tena sappadesameva nesaṃ anussaraṇaṃ, na nippadesanti nidasseti.

'Likewise the disciples and the paccekabuddhas.' Here, with the word 'likewise,' he connects this with the statement 'they recollect only what has been seen, done, and heard by themselves.' By this he shows that their recollection is partial, not complete.

Khajjopanakaobhāsasadisaṃ ñāṇassa ativiya appānubhāvatāya. Sāvakānanti ettha pakatisāvakānaṃ pākatikapadīpobhāsasadisaṃ. Mahāsāvakānaṃ (theragā. aṭṭha. 2.21 vaṅgīsettharagāthāvaṇṇanāya vitthāro) mahāpadīpobhāsasadisaṃ. Tenāha visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 2.402) “ukkāpabhāsadisa”nti. Osadhitārakobhāsasadisanti [P 2.0005] ussannā pabhā etāya dhīyati, osadhīnaṃ vā anubalappadāyakattā “osadhī”ti evaṃ laddhanāmāya tārakāya pabhāsadisaṃ. Saradasūriyamaṇḍalobhāsasadisaṃ sabbaso andhakāravidhamanato. Apaṭubhāvahetuko visayaggahaṇe cañcalabhāvo khalitaṃ, kuṇṭhibhāvahetuko visayassa anabhisamayo paṭighāto. Āvajjanapaṭibaddhamevāti āvajjanamattādhīnaṃ, āvajjitamatte eva yathicchitassa paṭivijjhanakanti attho. Sesapadadvayepi eseva nayo.

'Like the light of a firefly': this is due to the very slight power of the knowledge. Here, regarding 'of the disciples': for ordinary disciples, it is like the light of an ordinary lamp; for the great disciples (as elaborated in the commentary on the verses of the Elder Vaṅgīsa), it is like the light of a great lamp. Hence it is said in the Visuddhimagga: 'like the light of a torch.' 'Like the light of the morning star': this is like the light of the star so named (osadhi) either because a bright light is sustained by it, or because it gives strength to medicinal herbs. 'Like the light of the autumn sun's disk': this is because of completely dispelling the darkness. 'Stumbling' (khalitaṃ) is unsteadiness in grasping the object, caused by a lack of sharpness. 'Impingement' (paṭighāto) is the non-comprehension of the object, caused by bluntness. 'Bound only to adverting' means dependent only on adverting; the meaning is the penetration of the desired object at the very moment of adverting to it. This same method applies to the remaining two terms as well.

Asaṅgaappaṭihataṃ pavattamānaṃ bhagavato ñāṇaṃ lahutarepi visaye, garutare ca ekasadisamevāti dassetuṃ “dubbalapattapuṭe”tiādinā upamādvayaṃ vuttaṃ. Dhammakāyattā bhagavato guṇaṃ ārabbha pavattā “bhagavantaṃyeva ārabbha uppannā”ti vuttaṃ. Taṃ sabbampīti taṃ yathāvuttaṃ sabbampi pubbenivāsapaṭisaṃyuttaṃ kathaṃ. Titthiyānaṃ, sāvakānañca pubbenivāsānussaraṇaṃ bhagavato pubbenivāsānussaraṇassa hīnudāharaṇadassanavasenettha kathitaṃ. Evañhi bhagavato mahantabhāvo visesato pakāsito hotīti. Saṅkhepatoti samāsato. Yattakopi pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa pavattibhedo attano ñāṇassa visayabhūto, taṃ sabbaṃ tadā yathākathitaṃ te bhikkhū saṅkhipitvā “itipī”ti āhaṃsu. Tassa ca anekākāratāya āmeḍitavacanaṃ, pi-saddo sampiṇḍanattho, “iti kho bhikkhave sappaṭibhayo bālo”tiādīsu (ma. ni. 3.124; a. ni. 3.1) viya ākārattho iti-saddoti dassento “evampī”ti tadatthamāha.

To show that the Blessed One's knowledge proceeds without attachment or impediment and is exactly the same in lighter and in heavier domains, the two similes beginning with 'a weak leaf-container' are stated. Because the Blessed One is the Dhamma-body, the praise that arises concerning his qualities is said to have 'arisen only in dependence on the Blessed One.' 'All of that' means the entire discourse connected with the recollection of past lives as stated above. The recollection of past lives by the sectarians and the disciples is mentioned here by way of showing an inferior example to the Blessed One's recollection of past lives. For in this way the Blessed One's greatness is especially revealed. 'In brief' means concisely. Whatever variety in the operation of the knowledge of recollecting past lives fell within the range of their own knowledge, the bhikkhus condensed all of that as it was then explained and said, 'Thus indeed...' The repetition of the word is because of its manifold aspects. The word 'pi' is for summing up. To show that the word 'iti' has the sense of manner, just as in such passages as 'Thus, bhikkhus, the fool is fraught with peril...' (MN 129; AN 3.1), he states its meaning as 'evampī' ('in this way too').

2-3. Vuttamevāti [M 2.0005] ettha ca idha pāṭhe yaṃ vattabbaṃ tena pāṭhena sādhāraṇaṃ, taṃ vuttamevāti adhippetaṃ, na asādhāraṇaṃ apubbapadavaṇṇanāya adhikatattāti taṃ dassento [P 2.0006] “ayameva hi viseso”tiādimāha. “Assosī”ti idaṃ savanakiccanipphattiyā vuttaṃ saddaggahaṇamukhena tadatthāvabodhassa siddhattā. Tattha pana pāḷiyaṃ “imaṃ saṃkhiyadhammaṃ viditvā” icceva (dī. ni. 1.2) vuttaṃ. Ime bhikkhū mama guṇe thomenti, kathaṃ? Mama pubbenivāsañāṇaṃ ārabbhāti yojanā. Nipphattinti kiccanipphattiṃ, tena kātabbakiccasiddhanti attho. Noti pucchāvācī [V 2.0005] nu-iti iminā samānattho nipātoti vuttaṃ “iccheyyātha nū”ti. Nanti bhagavantaṃ. “Yaṃ bhagavā”ti ettha yaṃ-saddena kiriyāparāmasanabhūtena “dhammiṃ kathaṃ katheyyā”ti evaṃ vuttaṃ. Dhammikathākaraṇaṃ parāmaṭṭhaṃ “etassā”ti padassa atthoti āha “etassa dhammikathākaraṇassā”ti, ādaravasena pana taṃ dvikkhattuṃ vuttaṃ.

2–3. Here, 'vuttamevāti' ('it has already been said') is intended to mean that what is to be said in this text is common to that other text, not what is uncommon, which would be excessive due to the explanation of a new word. To show this, he says, 'For this is the distinction,' and so on. 'Assosī' ('he heard') is said with regard to the accomplishment of the act of hearing, since the understanding of its meaning is achieved by way of grasping the sound. But in the Pāli text there, it is just said: 'having known this doctrine in brief' (DN 1). The construction is: 'These bhikkhus are praising my qualities. How? In connection with my knowledge of past lives.' 'Nipphattiṃ' means the accomplishment of the task; the meaning is that the task to be done has been achieved. It is said that the particle 'no' is an interrogative synonymous with 'nu,' as in 'iccheyyātha nū.' 'Naṃ' refers to the Blessed One. In 'Yaṃ bhagavā,' the word 'yaṃ' refers to the action, so what is said is: 'that the Blessed One might give a Dhamma talk.' He says, 'of this act of giving a Dhamma talk,' because the giving of a Dhamma talk is what is referred to by the word 'etassa.' It is said twice out of respect.

4. Suṇāthāti ettha iti-saddo ādiattho, pakārattho vā, etena “manasi karothā”ti padaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Sotāvadhānaṃ sotassa odahanaṃ, sussūsāti attho. Chinnaṃ upacchinnaṃ vaṭumaṃ saṃsāravaṭṭaṃ etesanti chinnavaṭumakā, sammāsambuddhā, aññe ca khīṇāsavā, idha pana sammāsambuddhā adhippetā. Tesañhi sabbaso anussaraṇaṃ itaresaṃ avisayo. Tenāha “aññesaṃ asādhāraṇa”nti. Paccattavacane dissati yaṃ-saddo kammatthadīpanato. Upayogavacane dissati yaṃ-saddo pucchanakiriyāya kammatthadīpanato. Tanti ca upayogavacanameva pucchati-saddassa dvikammakabhāvato. Yanti yena kāraṇenāti ayamettha atthoti āha “karaṇavacane dissatī”ti. Bhummeti daṭṭhabboti yathā yaṃ-saddo na kevalaṃ paccattaupayogesu eva, atha kho karaṇepi dissati, evaṃ idha bhummeti daṭṭhabbo. Dasasahassilokadhātunti jātikkhettabhūtaṃ dasasahassacakkavāḷaṃ. Unnādento uppajji [P 2.0007] anekacchariyapātubhāvapaṭimaṇḍitattā buddhuppādassa.

4. In 'Suṇātha' ('Listen!'), the word 'iti' has the sense of 'and so on' or of manner; by this it includes the phrase 'attend closely' ('manasi karotha'). 'Sotāvadhānaṃ' is the application of the ear; the meaning is the desire to hear. 'Chinnaṃ' means cut off, severed; 'vaṭumaṃ' means the round of saṃsāra. Thus 'chinnavaṭumakā' are those for whom the round is cut off, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones and other arahants. Here, however, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones are intended. For their recollection in all respects is beyond the range of others. Hence it is said: 'uncommon to others.' The word 'yaṃ' is seen in the accusative case indicating the object. It is seen in the dative of reference indicating the object of the action of asking. And 'taṃ' is also the dative of reference because the word 'pucchati' is a ditransitive verb. 'Yaṃ' here means 'for which reason'; hence he says: 'it is seen in the instrumental case.' It should be understood as being in the locative ('bhumma'): just as the word 'yaṃ' is seen not only in the accusative and dative of reference but also in the instrumental, so here it should be understood as being in the locative. 'Dasasahassilokadhātu' means the ten-thousandfold world-system, the ten thousand world-spheres that are the birth-field. 'Resounding' means it arose, because the arising of a Buddha is adorned with the manifestation of many wonders.

Kālassa bhaddatā nāma tattha sattānaṃ guṇavibhūtiyā, buddhuppādaparamā ca guṇavibhūtīti tabbahulatā yassa kappassa bhaddatāti āha “pañcabuddhuppādapaṭimaṇḍitattā sundarakappe”ti, tathā sārabhūtaguṇavasena “sārakappe”ti[M 2.0006]. “Imaṃ kappaṃ thomento evamāhā”ti vatvā imassa kappassa tathā thometabbatā anaññasādhāraṇāti dassetuṃ “yato paṭṭhāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha yato paṭṭhāyāti yato pabhuti abhinīhāro katoti manussattādiaṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato abhinīhāro pavattito. Saṃsārassa anādibhāvato imassa bhagavato abhinīhārato puretaraṃ uppannā sammāsambuddhā anantā aparimeyyāti tehi uppannakappe nivattento “etasmiṃ antare”ti āha. Kāmaṃ dīpaṅkarabuddhuppāde ayaṃ bhagavā abhinīhāramakāsi, tassa pana bhagavato nibbatti imassa abhinīhārato purimatarāti vuttaṃ “amhākaṃ…pe… nibbattiṃsū”ti.

The auspiciousness of an eon is due to the flourishing of qualities in the beings there, and the supreme flourishing of qualities is the arising of a Buddha. The auspiciousness of an eon in which that is abundant is why he says: 'in the beautiful eon,' because it is adorned with the arising of five Buddhas, and similarly, 'in the essence eon,' on account of its essential qualities. Having said, 'Praising this eon, he spoke thus,' to show that the praiseworthiness of this eon is not shared by any other, he says, 'from when,' and so on. Therein, 'from when' means from when the aspiration was made, that is, the aspiration endowed with the eight factors beginning with human status was undertaken. Since saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning, before the aspiration of this Blessed One, infinite, immeasurable Perfectly Enlightened Ones had arisen. Excluding the eons in which they arose, he says, 'in this interval.' Although this Blessed One made his aspiration at the time of the Buddha Dīpaṅkara's arising, the final Nibbāna of that Blessed One occurred before this aspiration; thus it is said, 'our... passed away.'

Asaṅkhyeyyakappapariyosāneti mahākappānaṃ asaṅkhyeyyapariyosāne. Esa nayo ito paresupi. “Ito tiṃsakappasahassānaṃ uparī”ti etena padumuttarassa bhagavato, sumedhassa ca bhagavato antare ekūnasattatikappasahassāni buddhasuññāni ahesunti dasseti. “Ito aṭṭhārasannaṃ kappasahassānaṃ uparī”ti iminā sujātassa bhagavato, atthadassissa ca bhagavato antare [V 2.0006] ekenūnāni dvādasakappasahassāni buddhasuññāni ahesunti dasseti. “Ito catunavute kappe”ti iminā dhammadassissa bhagavato, siddhatthassa ca bhagavato antare chādhikanavasatuttarāni sattarasakappasahassāni buddhasuññāni ahesunti dasseti. “Ekatiṃse kappe”ti iminā vipassissa bhagavato, sikhissa ca bhagavato antare saṭṭhi kappāni buddhasuññāni ahesunti dasseti. Te sabbepi padumuttarassa bhagavato oraṃ sumedhādīhi uppannakappehi saddhiṃ samodhāniyamānā satasahassā kappā honti, yattha mahāsāvakādayo (theragā. aṭṭha. 2.21 vaṅgīsattheragāthāvaṇṇanā) vivaṭṭū panissayāni [P 2.0008] kusalāni sambhariṃsu. Buddhasuññepi loke paccekabuddhā uppajjitvā tesaṃ purisavisesānaṃ puññābhisandābhibuddhiyā paccayā honti. “Evamaya”ntiādi vuttamevatthaṃ nigamanavasena vadati.

‘At the end of an incalculable eon’ means at the conclusion of an incalculable number of great eons. This same method applies to the subsequent cases. By ‘thirty thousand eons ago from this one,’ he shows that between the Blessed One Padumuttara and the Blessed One Sumedha there were sixty-nine thousand eons void of Buddhas. By ‘eighteen thousand eons ago from this one,’ he shows that between the Blessed One Sujāta and the Blessed One Atthadassī there were eleven thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine eons void of Buddhas. By ‘ninety-four eons ago from this one,’ he shows that between the Blessed One Dhammadassī and the Blessed One Siddhattha there were seventeen thousand nine hundred and six eons void of Buddhas. By ‘thirty-one eons ago,’ he shows that between the Blessed One Vipassī and the Blessed One Sikhī there were sixty eons void of Buddhas. All these, when combined with the eons in which Sumedha and others arose after the Blessed One Padumuttara, amount to one hundred thousand eons, during which the great disciples and others accumulated wholesome deeds that are a basis for turning away from the cycle of existence. Even in a world void of Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas arise and become a condition for the growth and increase of the store of merit of those special persons. ‘Thus this…’ and so on states the meaning already explained by way of a conclusion.

“Kiṃ paneta”ntiādi pubbanimittavibhāvanatthāya āraddhaṃ. Tattha etanti buddhānaṃ uppajjanaṃ. Kappasaṇṭhānakālasminti vivaṭṭakappassa saṇṭhahanakāle. Ekamasaṅkhyeyyanti saṃvaṭṭaṭṭhāyiṃ sandhāyāha. Ekaṅgaṇaṃ hutvā ṭhiteti pabbatarukkhagacchādīnaṃ, meghādīnañca abhāvena vivaṭaṃaṅgaṇaṃ hutvā ṭhite. Lokasannivāseti [M 2.0007] bhājanalokena sannivisitabbaṭṭhāne. Vīsati yaṭṭhiyo usabhaṃ. “Usabhamattā, dve usabhamattā”tiādinā paccekaṃ mattā-saddo yojetabbo. Yojanasahassamattā hutvāti patamānāva udakadhārā yojanasahassamattaṃ ākāsaṭṭhānaṃ pharitvā pavattiyā yojanasahassamattā hutvā. Yāva avinaṭṭhabrahmalokāti yāva ābhassarabrahmalokā, yāva subhakiṇhabrahmalokā, yāva vehapphalabrahmalokāti attho.

The passage beginning ‘But what is this?’ is introduced for the purpose of explaining the preliminary signs. Herein, ‘this’ means the arising of the Buddhas. ‘At the time of the eon’s formation’ means at the time of the establishment of the evolving eon. ‘One incalculable’ refers to the period the eon remains in dissolution. ‘When it stood as a single open space’ means when it stood as an open space due to the absence of mountains, trees, thickets, clouds, and so on. ‘In the world-settlement’ means in the place to be settled by the receptacle world. Twenty rods make an usabha. The word ‘measure’ should be connected with each term, as in ‘a measure of an usabha, two measures of an usabha,’ and so on. ‘Having become a thousand yojanas in measure’ means: the falling streams of water, by pervading a space of a thousand yojanas as they fall, become a thousand yojanas in measure as they flow. ‘Up to the undestroyed Brahma worlds’ means up to the Ābhassara Brahma world, up to the Subhakiṇha Brahma world, and up to the Vehapphala Brahma world.

Vātavasenāti saṭṭhisahassādhikanavayojanasatasahassubbedhassa sandhārakavātamaṇḍalassa vasena. Mahābodhipallaṅkoti mahābodhipallaṅkappadesamāha. Tassa pacchā vināso, paṭhamaṃ saṇṭhahanañca dhammatāvasena veditabbaṃ. Tatthāti tasmiṃ padese. Pubbanimittaṃ hutvāti buddhappādassa pubbanimittaṃ hutvā. Pubbanimittasannissayo hi gaccho nissitavohārena tathā vutto. Tenāha “tassā”tiādi. Kaṇṇikābaddhāni hutvāti ābaddhakaṇṇikā viya hutvā. Suddhāvāsabrahmāno attamanā…pe… gacchantīti yojanā. Vehapphalepi subhakiṇhe saṅgahetvā “nava brahmalokā”ti vuttaṃ. Tathā hi te [P 2.0009] catutthiṃyeva viññāṇaṭṭhitiṃ bhajanti. Nikkhamantesūti mahābhinikkhamanaṃ abhinikkhamantesu. Abhijāti panettha jātibhāvasāmaññena gabbhokkantiyāva saṅgahitā. Nimīyati anumīyati phalaṃ etenāti nimittaṃ, kāraṇaṃ. Ñāpakampi hi kāraṇaṃ disvā tassa abyabhicārībhāvena phalaṃ siddhameva katvā gaṇhi, yathā taṃ asito isi abhijātiyaṃ mahāpurisassa lakkhaṇāni disvā tesaṃ abyabhicārībhāvena buddhaguṇe siddhe eva katvā gaṇhi, evaṃ [V 2.0007] pana gayhamānaṃ tannimittakaṃ phalaṃ tadānubhāvena siddhaṃ viya voharīyati tabbhāve bhāvato. Tenāha “tesaṃ nimittānaṃ ānubhāvenā”tiādi. Tathā cāha bhagavā “so tena lakkhaṇena samannāgato…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati, buddho samāno kiṃ labhatī”ti (dī. ni. 3.202, 204) ca evamādi. Imamatthanti pañca buddhā imasmiṃ kappe uppajjissantīti imamatthaṃ yāthāvato jāniṃsu.

By the power of the wind: this is by the power of the supporting wind-circle that is nine hundred and sixty thousand yojanas in height. The great Bodhi seat: this refers to the place of the great Bodhi seat. Its later destruction and its initial establishment should be understood as occurring by natural law. There: in that place. Having become a prior sign: having become a prior sign of the Buddha’s appearance. For a plant that is a basis for prior signs is so called by a dependent designation. Therefore, it is said, ‘of that,’ and so on. Having bound pericarps: like having bound pericarps. The Suddhāvāsa Brahmas, delighted… and so on… go: this is the connection. Including the Vehapphala and Subhakiṇha realms, it is said, ‘nine Brahma worlds.’ For they resort only to the fourth station of consciousness. When departing: when undertaking the great renunciation. Here, noble birth is included by the generality of the state of birth, even up to conception in the womb. A sign (nimitta) is a cause (kāraṇa), because the result is inferred (nimīyati) or deduced (anumīyati) by means of it. For having seen a cause, which is also a means of knowledge, one takes the result as certainly accomplished because of its infallibility, just as the sage Asita, having seen the marks of a great man at his noble birth, took the Buddha’s qualities as certainly accomplished because of their infallibility. But when taken thus, the result based on that sign is spoken of as if accomplished by its power, because it exists when that cause exists. Therefore, it is said, ‘by the power of those signs,’ and so on. And thus the Blessed One said: ‘Endowed with that mark… what does he obtain as a king, what does he obtain as a Buddha?’ (Dī. Ni. 3.202, 204) and so on. This meaning: they accurately knew this meaning, that five Buddhas will arise in this eon.

Jātiparicchedādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Ascertainment of Birth, etc.

5-7. Kappaparicchedavasenāti [M 2.0008] “ito so ekanavute kappe”tiādinā yattha yattha kappe te te buddhā uppannā, tassa tassa kappassa paricchindanavasena parijānanavasena. “Idaṃ ta”nti hi niyametvā paricchijja jānanaṃ paricchindanaṃ paricchedo. Parittanti ittaraṃ. Lahukanti sallahukaṃ, āyuno adhippetattā rassanti vuttaṃ hoti. Tenāha “ubhayametaṃ appakasseva vevacana”nti.

5-7. By way of defining the eon: this means by way of defining and fully knowing each eon in which those Buddhas arose, as in the phrase, ‘from this, the ninety-first eon,’ etc. For defining, which is to delimit and know by determining, ‘this is that,’ is definition. Limited means insignificant. Light means very light; because the intended meaning is lifespan, it is said to be short. Therefore, it is said, ‘both of these are synonyms for “small”.’

“Appaṃ vā bhiyyo”ti avisesajotanaṃ “vīsaṃ vā tiṃsaṃ vā”tiādinā aniyamitavaseneva yathālābhato [P 2.0010] vavatthapetvā ayañca nayo apacuroti dassento “evaṃ dīghāyuko pana atidullabho”ti āha. Idaṃ taṃ visesavavatthāpanaṃ puggalesu pakkhipitvā dassento “tattha visākhā”tiādimāha.

‘Whether little or much’: this indiscriminate expression is determined based on whatever is available, without specifying an amount like ‘twenty or thirty.’ Showing that this way is not common, he said, ‘But such a long-lived person is exceedingly rare.’ Placing this specific determination among individuals, he showed it by saying, ‘There, Visākhā,’ and so on.

Yadi evaṃ kasmā amhākaṃ bhagavā tattakampi kālaṃ na jīvi, nanu mahābodhisattā carimabhave ativiyauḷāratamena puññābhisaṅkhārena paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhantīti? Saccametanti. Tattha kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ “vipassīādayo panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha abhijātiyā mettāṭhānatāya abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇassa mettāpubbabhāgatā. Tadanuguṇañhi tesaṃ visesato paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ. Tassa visesato bahulaṃ khemavitakkūpanissayatāya somanassasahagatatā, anaññasādhāraṇaparopadesarahitañāṇavisesūpanissayatāya ñāṇasampayuttatā, asaṅkhārikatā ca veditabbā, asaṅkhyeyyaṃ āyu ādhāravisesato, nissayavisesato, paṭipakkhadūrībhāvato, pavattiākāravisesato ca aparimeyyānubhāvatāya kāraṇassa. Tattha cirataraṃ kālaṃ santānassa pāramitāparibhāvitatā ādhāravisesatā. Alobhajjhāsayādiāsayasampadā nissayavisesatā. Lābhamacchariyādipāpadhammavikkhambhanaṃ paṭipakkhadūrībhāvo. Sabbasattānaṃ sakalavaṭṭadukkhanissaraṇatthāya āyūhanā pavattiākāraviseso veditabbo.

If this is so, why did our Blessed One not live even for that long? Surely, the great bodhisattas in their final existence take rebirth with an extremely vast and sublime accumulation of merit. This is true. To explain the reason, it is said, ‘But Vipassī and others…’ Here, due to their noble birth and their being established in loving-kindness, the consciousness formed by their volitional activities is preceded by loving-kindness. For their rebirth-consciousness is especially in accordance with this. Due to its being strongly supported by thoughts of security, it is accompanied by joy. Because of its being supported by a special knowledge that is not shared by others and is free from reliance on others’ teachings, it is associated with wisdom. It should also be understood as unprompted. Their immeasurable lifespan is due to the special base, the special support, the removal of opposing factors, and the distinctive mode of activity—all because of the immeasurable power of the cause. Here, the special base is the fact that the stream of consciousness has been cultivated by the perfections over a very long time. The special support is the excellence of their disposition, such as an attitude free from greed. The removal of opposing factors is the suppression of evil qualities like stinginess regarding gains. The distinctive mode of activity should be understood as striving for the liberation of all beings from the entire round of suffering.

Ayañca [V 2.0008] nayo sabbesaṃ mahābodhisattānaṃ carimabhavābhinibbattakakammāyūhane sādhāraṇoti tassa phalenāpi ekasadiseneva bhavitabbanti [M 2.0009] āha “iti sabbe buddhā asaṅkhyeyyāyukā”ti, asaṅkhyeyyakālāvatthānāyukāti attho. Asaṅkhyeyyāyukasaṃvattanasamatthaṃ paricitaṃ kammaṃ hoti, buddhā pana tadā manussānaṃ [P 2.0011] paramāyuppamāṇānurūpameva kālaṃ ṭhatvā parinibbāyanti tato paraṃ ṭhatvā sādhetabbapayojanābhāvato, dhammatāvesāti vā veditabbā. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana tato paraṃ pana aṭṭhānassa “utubhojanavipattiyā”ti (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.5) kāraṇaṃ vuttaṃ, “taṃ lokasādhāraṇaṃ loke jātasaṃvuddhānaṃ tathāgatānaṃ na hotī”ti na sakkā vattuṃ. Tathā hi nesaṃ rogakilamathādayo hontiyeva. Utubhojanavasenāti asampannassa, sampannassa ca utuno, bhojanassa ca vasena yathākkamaṃ āyu hāyatipi vaḍḍhatipi. Āyūti ca paramāyu adhippetaṃ. Tattha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ brahmajālādiṭīkāyaṃ (dī. ni. ṭī. 1.40) vuttameva.

This method is common to all great Bodhisattas in accumulating the kamma that produces their final existence, and so by its fruit, they must be similar in one respect. Thus it is said: 'All Buddhas are of immeasurable lifespan,' meaning they have a lifespan that lasts for an immeasurable period. The kamma capable of producing an immeasurable lifespan has been accumulated. However, the Buddhas then pass into Parinibbāna after dwelling for a time corresponding to the maximum lifespan of humans at that time, because beyond that there is no purpose to be achieved. Or this is to be understood as their nature. In the commentary, however, the reason given for not remaining beyond that is 'due to failure of climate and food.' It cannot be said that this, being common to the world, does not apply to the Tathāgatas who are born and fully awakened in the world; for they too experience illness, fatigue, and the like. 'By means of climate and food' refers to the lifespan decreasing or increasing, respectively, depending on whether one lacks or possesses suitable climate and food. Here, 'lifespan' means the maximum lifespan. As for what should be said on this matter, it has already been stated in the subcommentary to the Brahmajāla Sutta.

Idāni tamatthaṃ samudāgamato paṭṭhāya dassetuṃ “tattha yadā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Dhamme niyuttā dhammikā, na dhammikā adhammikā, hiṃsādiadhammapasutā. Adhammikameva hoti issarajanānaṃ anuvattanena, paresaṃ diṭṭhānugatiāpajjanena ca. Uṇhavalāhakā devatāti uṇhautuno paccayabhūtameghamālāsamuṭṭhāpakā devaputtā. Tesaṃ kira tathā cittuppādasamakālameva yathicchitaṭṭhānaṃ uṇhaṃ pharamānā valāhakamālā nātibahalā ito cito nabhaṃ chādentī vitanoti. Esa nayo sītavalāhakavassavalāhakāsu. Abbhavalāhakā pana devatā sītuṇhavassehi vinā kevalaṃ abbhapaṭalasseva samuṭṭhāpakā veditabbā. Tāsanti ettha “mittā”ti padaṃ ānetvā yojanā. Kāmaṃ heṭṭhā vuttā sattavidhāpi devatā cātumahārājikāva tā pana tena tena visesena vatvā idāni tadaññe paṭhamabhūmike kāmāvacaradeve sāmaññato gaṇhanto “cātumahārājikā”ti āha. Tāsaṃ adhammikatāyāti rājūnaṃ adhammikabhāvamūlakena uparājādiadhammikabhāvaparamparābhatena tāsaṃ devatānaṃ adhammikabhāvena. Visamaṃ candimasūriyā pariharantīti [P 2.0012] bahvābādhatādi aniṭṭhaphalūpanissayabhūtassa yathāvuttaadhammikatāsaññitassa sādhāraṇassa pāpakammassa balena visamaṃ vāyantena vāyunā pīḷiyamānā candimasūriyā sineruṃ parikkhipantā visamaṃ parivattanti yathāmaggena nappavattantīti[M 2.0010]. Assidaṃ yathā candimasūriyānaṃ visamaparivattanaṃ visamavātasaṅkhobhahetukaṃ, evaṃ utuvassādivisamappavattīti dassetuṃ “vāto yathāmaggena na vāyatī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Devatānanti sītavalāhakadevatādidevatānaṃ. Tenāha “sītuṇhabhedo utū”tiādi. Tasmiṃ asampajjanteti tasmiṃ yathāvutte vassabījabhūte utumhi yathākālaṃ sampattiṃ anupagacchante.

Now, to show that meaning beginning from its source, it is said: 'Therein, when…' Those devoted to the Dhamma are righteous (dhammikā); those not devoted are unrighteous (adhammikā), being intent on unrighteousness such as harming. Unrighteousness arises from following powerful people and adopting the views of others. The deities of the hot clouds are the divine beings who produce masses of clouds that are the condition for the hot season. It is said that at the very moment their thought arises, a not-too-thick mass of clouds, spreading heat as they wish, covers the sky here and there. This same principle applies to the deities of cold clouds and rain clouds. However, the deities of mere clouds should be understood as producing only a layer of clouds, without cold, heat, or rain. Here, the word 'friends' should be supplied and connected with 'of them' (tāsaṃ). Although the seven kinds of deities mentioned below are all of the realm of the Four Great Kings, having spoken of them with their specific distinctions, he now speaks generally of the other sense-sphere devas of that first plane by saying 'the Four Great Kings.' By their unrighteousness: by the unrighteousness of those deities, which is brought about by a succession of unrighteousness from viceroys and others, rooted in the unrighteousness of the kings. 'The moon and sun move unevenly': oppressed by wind that blows unevenly due to the force of common unwholesome kamma—the aforesaid unrighteousness which is a basis for undesirable results such as much disease—the moon and sun, encircling Mount Sineru, revolve unevenly, not proceeding on their proper path. To show that just as the uneven revolution of the moon and sun is caused by the disturbance of an uneven wind, so too is the irregular occurrence of the seasons and rains, it is said: 'the wind does not blow along its proper path,' and so on. Of the deities: of the deities of the cold clouds, etc. Therefore, it is said: 'The season is the distinction between cold and heat,' and so on. When that does not succeed: when that season, which is the basis for rain and seeds as stated, does not attain its proper fulfillment in due time.

“Na [V 2.0009] sammā devo vassatī”ti saṅkhepato vuttamatthaṃ vivaranto “kadācī”tiādimāha. Tattha kadāci vassatīti kadāci avassanakāle vassati. Kadāci na vassatīti kadāci vassitabbakāle na vassati. Katthaci vassati, katthaci na vassatīti padesamāha. “Vassantopī”tiādi “kadāci vassati, kadāci na vassatī”ti padadvayasseva atthavivaraṇaṃ. Vigatagandhavaṇṇarasādīti ādi-saddena nirojataṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Ekasmiṃ padeseti bhattapacanabhājanassa ekapasse. Uttaṇḍulanti pākato ukkantataṇḍulaṃ. Tīhākārehīti sabbaso apariṇataṃ, ekadesena pariṇataṃ, dupariṇatañcāti evaṃ tīhākārehi. Paccati pakkāsayaṃ upagacchati. Appāyukāti ettha “dubbaṇṇā cā”tipi vattabbaṃ. Evaṃ utubhojanavasena āyu hāyati hetumhi aparikkhīṇepi paccayassa paridubbalattā.

'The deity does not rain properly': Elaborating on the meaning stated in brief, he says 'sometimes,' etc. Here, 'sometimes it rains' means it rains at a time when it should not rain. 'Sometimes it does not rain' means it does not rain at a time when it should rain. 'In some places it rains, in some places it does not rain': he speaks of a region. The words 'Even when it rains,' etc. are an explanation of the meaning of the two phrases 'sometimes it rains' and 'sometimes it does not rain.' 'Devoid of fragrance, color, and taste': by the word 'etc.' he includes its being without nutritional essence. 'In one place': on one side of a cooking pot. 'Overcooked rice': rice that has passed the point of being properly cooked. 'In three ways': that is, completely uncooked, partially cooked, and badly cooked. 'It cooks': it approaches the state of being cooked. 'Short-lived': here, 'and of poor complexion' should also be stated. Thus, on account of the season and food, lifespan declines because of the extreme weakness of the supporting condition, even when the cause has not been exhausted.

“Yadā panā”tiādi sukkapakkhassa attho vuttavipariyāyena veditabbo.

'But when,' etc.: The meaning for the bright fortnight should be understood in the way opposite to what has been stated.

Vaḍḍhitvā [P 2.0013] vaḍḍhitvā parihīnanti veditabbaṃ. Kasmā? Na hi ekasmiṃ antarakappe aneke buddhā uppajjanti, eko eva pana uppajjatīti. Idāni tamatthaṃ vitthārato dassetuṃ “katha”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Cattāri ṭhatvāti accantasaṃyoge upayogavacanaṃ. Yaṃyaṃāyuparimāṇesūti yattakayattakaparamāyuppamāṇesu. Tesampīti buddhānaṃ. Taṃ tadeva āyuparimāṇaṃ hoti, tattha kāraṇaṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva.

It should be understood as having increased and increased and then declined. Why? Because in a single intermediate eon not many Buddhas arise, but only one arises. Now, to show this meaning in detail, the words 'how,' etc., are stated. 'Having stood for four': this is a locative expressing an absolute connection. 'For whatever life spans': for whatever maximum life spans there may be. 'For them too': for the Buddhas. That very life span is theirs; the reason for this has already been stated below.

Jātiparicchedādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā

The explanation of the section on birth and so on is concluded.

Bodhiparicchedavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Section on Enlightenment

8. Mūleti [M 2.0011] mūlāvayavassa samīpe. Taṃ pana tassā heṭṭhāpadeso hotīti āha “pāṭalirukkhassa heṭṭhā”ti. Taṃdivasanti attanā jātadivase, taṃdivasanti vā taṃ bhagavato abhisambodhidivase. So kira bodhirukkho sālakalyāṇī viya pathaviyā abbhantare eva puretaraṃ vaḍḍhento abhisambodhidivase pathaviṃ ubbhijjitvā uṭṭhito ratanasataṃ ucco, tāvadeva ca vitthato hutvā nabhaṃ pūrento aṭṭhāsi. Ayampi kiretassa rukkhabhāvena viya aññehi vemattatā. Ghanasaṃhatanāḷavaṇṭatāya kaṇṇikabaddhehi viya pupphehi. Ekasañchannāti pupphānaṃ nirantaratāya [V 2.0010] ekajjhaṃ sañchannā, tattha tattha nibaddha…pe… samujjalanti tahaṃ tahaṃ olambitakusumadāmehi ceva tahaṃ tahaṃ khittamālāpiṇḍīhi ca ito cito vippakiṇṇavividhavaṇṭamuttapupphehi ca sammadeva ujjalaṃ. Aññamaññaṃ sirīsampattānīti aññamaññassa siriyā sobhāya sampannāni. Buddhaguṇavibhavasirinti sammāsambuddhehi abhigantabbaguṇavibhūtisobhaṃ. Paṭivijjhamānoti adhigacchanto.

8. 'At the root': near the root-part. But since that is its lower part, he says 'beneath the Pāṭali tree.' 'On that day': on the day of his own birth, or 'on that day' means on the day of the Blessed One's full enlightenment. It is said that this Bodhi tree, like the Sālakalyāṇī, having grown earlier deep within the earth, on the day of full enlightenment broke through the earth and arose. It stood a hundred ratanas high and, having become just as wide, it stood filling the sky. This, it is said, is its distinction from other trees by its very nature as a tree. With flowers as if bound to the pericarp because of their dense, compact stalks and stems. 'Completely covered': covered all together because the flowers are uninterrupted. 'Fastened here and there…pe…radiantly bright': it was truly radiant with garlands of flowers hanging here and there, with clusters of garlands tossed here and there, and with various stalk-released flowers scattered about hither and thither. 'Endowed with mutual splendor': endowed with the beauty of each other's glory. 'The splendor of the Buddha's qualities and majesty': the glorious beauty of the qualities and powers to be realized by the Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones. 'Penetrating': attaining.

Setambarukkhoti setavaṇṇaphalo ambarukkho. Tadevāti [P 2.0014] pāṭaliyā vuttappamāṇameva. Ekatoti ekapasse. Surasānīti sumadhurarasāni.

'The Setamba tree': a mango tree with white-colored fruit. 'The very same': the very same measure as stated for the Pāṭali tree. 'On one side': on one side only. 'Of excellent flavor': of very sweet flavor.

Ekova pallaṅkoti ekova pallaṅkappadeso. So so rukkho “bodhī”ti vuccati bujjhanti etthāti katvā.

'Only one seat': only one seating place. Each respective tree is called 'Bodhi' because 'they awaken (bujjhanti) there.'

Sāvakayugaparicchedavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Section on the Pair of Disciples

9. Sāvakaparicchedeti sāvakayugaparicchede. “Khaṇḍatissa”nti dvepi ekajjhaṃ gahetvā ekattavasena vuttanti āha “khaṇḍo ca tisso cā”ti, buddhānaṃ sahodaro, vemātikopi vā jeṭṭhabhātā na hotīti “ekapitiko kaniṭṭhabhātā”ti vuttaṃ. Avasesehi puttehi. “Paññāpāramiyā matthakaṃ patto”ti vatvā tassa matthakappattaṃ guṇavisesaṃ dassetuṃ “sikhinā bhagavatā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

9. In the section on the disciples means in the section on the pair of disciples. Regarding ‘Khaṇḍatissa’: since both are taken together and spoken of as one, he says, ‘Khaṇḍa and Tissa.’ He is a uterine brother of the Buddha; since he is not an elder brother, nor even a half-brother by a different mother, it is said, ‘a younger brother of the same father.’ With the remaining sons. Having said, ‘He reached the peak of the perfection of wisdom,’ to show the special quality of his attainment of the peak, the words ‘by the Blessed One Sikhi,’ etc., are stated.

Uttaroti uttamo. Puna uttaroti theraṃ nāmena vadati. Pāranti parakoṭimatthakaṃ. Paññāvisayeti paññādhikāre. Pavattiṭṭhānavasena hi pavattiṃ vadati.

Uttara means the highest. Again, Uttara: he addresses the elder by name. The far shore means the ultimate limit, the peak. In the domain of wisdom means in the sphere of wisdom. For he speaks of its occurrence by way of its underlying condition.

Sāvakasannipātaparicchedavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Section on the Assembly of Disciples

10. Uposathanti [M 2.0012] āṇāpātimokkhaṃ. Dutiyatatiyesūti dutiye, tatiye ca sāvakasannipāte. Eseva nayoti caturaṅgikataṃ atidisati. Abhinīhārato paṭṭhāya vatthuṃ kathetvā pabbajjā dīpetabbā, sā pana yasmā manorathapūraṇiyaṃ aṅguttaraṭṭhakathāyaṃ (a. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.211) vitthārato āgatā, tasmā tattha vuttanayeneva veditabbāti.

10. Uposatha means the Pātimokkha of command. In the second and third means in the second and third assemblies of disciples. This is the method: he applies this to the four-factored assembly. Having related the story beginning from the aspiration, the going forth should be explained. But since this has come down in detail in the Manorathapūraṇī, the commentary to the Aṅguttara Nikāya, it should be understood by the method stated there.

Upaṭṭhākaparicchedavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Section on the Attendant

11. Nibaddhupaṭṭhākabhāvanti [V 2.0011] ārambhato paṭṭhāya yāva parinibbānā niyataupaṭṭhākabhāvaṃ. Aniyatuupaṭṭhākā pana bhagavato paṭhamabodhiyaṃ bahū ahesuṃ. Tenāha “bhagavato hī”tiādi. Idāni ānandatthero yena kāraṇena satthu nibaddhupaṭṭhākabhāvaṃ upagato, yathā ca upagato, taṃ dassetuṃ “tattha ekadā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Ahaṃ iminā maggena gacchāmī”ti āha anayabyasanāpādakena kammunā codiyamāno[P 2.0015]. Atha naṃ bhagavā tamatthaṃ anārocetvāva khemaṃ maggaṃ sandhāya “ehi bhikkhu iminā gacchāmā”ti āha. Kasmā panassa bhagavā tamatthaṃ nārocesīti? Ārocitepi asaddahanto nādiyissati. Tañhi tassa hoti dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyātiti. Teti te gamanaṃ, “ta”nti vā pāṭho.

11. The state of being a permanent attendant means the state of being a regular attendant from the beginning until the Parinibbāna. However, in the early period of his Buddhahood, the Blessed One had many non-regular attendants. Therefore, it is said, 'For the Blessed One,' etc. Now, to show for what reason the Venerable Ānanda undertook the role of permanent attendant to the Teacher, and how he did so, it is said, 'On one occasion,' etc. Being urged on by an action that causes misfortune and ruin, he said, 'I will go by this path.' Then the Blessed One, without informing him of that matter and referring to a safe path, said, 'Come, bhikkhu, let us go by this way.' But why did the Blessed One not inform him of that matter? Because even if it were told, he, not believing, would not accept it, and that would be for his long-term harm and suffering. Teti means 'your going'; alternatively, the reading is 'ta'.

Anvāsattoti anubaddho, upadduto vā. Dhammagāravanissito saṃvego dhammasaṃvego “amhesu nāma tiṭṭhantesu bhagavatopi īdisaṃ jāta”nti. “Ahaṃ upaṭṭhahissāmī”ti vadanto dhammasenāpati atthato evaṃ vadanto nāma hotīti “ahaṃ bhante tumhe”tiādi vuttaṃ. Asuññāyeva me sā disāti asuññāyeva mama sā disā. Tattha kāraṇamāha “tava ovādo buddhānaṃ ovādasadiso”ti.

Anvāsatto means followed closely, or afflicted. Dhammasaṃvego is a sense of spiritual urgency based on reverence for the Dhamma, that is, the thought: ‘Even while we are present, such a thing has happened to the Blessed One!’ When the General of the Dhamma said, ‘I will attend upon you,’ he was in effect speaking thus, hence it is said, ‘Venerable sir, I will attend upon you,’ etc. Asuññāyeva me sā disā means ‘that direction is indeed not empty for me.’ He states the reason for this: ‘Your advice is like the advice of the Buddhas.’

Vasituṃ na dassatīti ekagandhakuṭiyaṃ vāsaṃ na labhissatīti adhippāyo. Parammukhā desitassāpi dhammassāti suttantadesanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Abhidhammadesanā panassa parammukhāva pavattā pageva yācanāya. Tassā vācanāmaggopi sāriputtattherappabhavo. Kasmā? So niddesapaṭisambhidā viya [M 2.0013] therassa bhikkhuto gahitadhammakkhandhapakkhiyo. Apare pana “dhammabhaṇḍāgāriko paṭipāṭiyā tikadukesu devasikaṃ katokāso bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ pucchi, bhagavāpissa pucchitapucchitaṃ nayadānavasena vissajjesi. Evaṃ abhidhammopi satthārā parammukhā desitopi therena sammukhā paṭiggahitova ahosī”ti vadanti. Sabbaṃ vīmaṃsitvā gahetabbaṃ.

`He will not allow to dwell` means he would not get to stay in the same fragrant chamber; this is the intention. `Of the Dhamma taught even in his absence` is said with reference to the teaching of the Suttas. The Abhidhamma teaching, however, was given in his absence, let alone upon his asking. Moreover, its oral tradition originated from the Venerable Sāriputta. Why? Because, like the Niddesa and the Paṭisambhidā, it belongs to the collection of Dhamma aggregates received by the elder from that bhikkhu. Others, however, say: 'The Treasurer of the Dhamma, having found the opportunity daily, questioned the Blessed One in sequence on the triads and dyads, and the Blessed One answered each and every question by way of bestowing the method. Thus, although the Abhidhamma was taught by the Teacher in his absence, it was received by the elder face-to-face.' All this should be investigated before being accepted.

Aggupaṭṭhākoti upaṭṭhāne sakkaccakāritāya aggabhūto upaṭṭhāko. Thero hi upaṭṭhākaṭṭhānaṃ laddhakālato paṭṭhāya bhagavantaṃ duvidhena udakena, tividhena dantakaṭṭhena, pādaparikammena, gandhakuṭipariveṇasammajjanenāti evamādīhi kiccehi upaṭṭhahanto “imāya nāma velāya satthu idaṃ nāma laddhuṃ vaṭṭati, idaṃ nāma kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti cintetvā [P 2.0016] taṃ taṃ nipphādento mahatiṃ daṇḍadīpikaṃ gahetvā ekarattiṃ gandhakuṭipariveṇaṃ nava vāre anupariyāyati. Evaṃ hissa ahosi [V 2.0012] “sace me thinamiddhaṃ okkameyya, bhagavati pakkosante paṭivacanaṃ dātuṃ nāhaṃ sakkuṇeyya”nti, tasmā sabbarattiṃ daṇḍadīpikaṃ hatthena na muñcati. Tena vuttaṃ “aggupaṭṭhāko”ti.

The foremost attendant means the attendant who is foremost because of his respectful service. For from the time the Elder received the position of attendant, he served the Blessed One with duties such as providing two kinds of water and three kinds of tooth-sticks, washing his feet, and sweeping the fragrant chamber and its precincts. Thinking, ‘At this particular time the Teacher should receive this particular thing, and this particular thing should be done,’ and accomplishing each task accordingly, he would take a large torch-staff and walk around the fragrant chamber and its precincts nine times during a single night. For this was his thought: ‘If sloth and torpor should overcome me, I might not be able to answer when the Blessed One calls.’ Therefore, he did not release the torch-staff from his hand all night long. Hence it is said, ‘the foremost attendant.’

12. Pitumātujātanagaraparicchedo pitumukhena āgatattā “pitiparicchedo”ti vutto.

12. The section on the native city of his father and mother is called ‘the Father’s Section’ because it is presented from the father’s perspective.

Vihāraṃ pāvisīti gandhakuṭiṃ pāvisi. Ettakaṃ kathetvāti kappaparicchedādinavavārapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ vipassīādīnaṃ sattannaṃ buddhānaṃ pubbenivāsapaṭisaṃyuttaṃ ettāvatā desanaṃ desetvā. Kasmā panettha bhagavā vipassīādīnaṃ sattannaṃyeva buddhānaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ kathesi, na buddhavaṃsadesanāyaṃ (bu. vaṃ. 64 gāthādayo) viya pañcavīsatiyā buddhānaṃ, tato vā pana bhiyyoti? Anadhikārato, payojanābhāvato ca. Buddhavaṃsadesanāyañhi (bu. vaṃ. 75) –

`He entered the dwelling` means he entered the fragrant chamber. `Having spoken this much` means having delivered a discourse of this extent, one connected with the past abodes of the seven Buddhas beginning with Vipassī and adorned with the nine sections beginning with the Section on the Aeon. But why did the Blessed One here recount the past abodes of only the seven Buddhas beginning with Vipassī, and not, as in the Buddhavaṃsa discourse, those of the twenty-five Buddhas, or even more? Because it was not the proper occasion and there was no purpose. For in the Buddhavaṃsa discourse it is said:

“Kīdiso te mahāvīra, abhinīhāro naruttama;

Kamhi kāle tayā vīra, patthitā bodhimuttamā”ti. ādinā –

'O great hero, supreme among men, what was your aspiration? At what time, O hero, did you aspire to the supreme enlightenment?' and so on.

Pavattaṃ taṃ pucchaṃ adhikāraṃ aṭṭhuppattiṃ katvā yassa sammāsambuddhassa pādamūle attanā mahābhinīhāro kato, taṃ dīpaṅkaraṃ bhagavantaṃ ādiṃ katvā yesaṃ catuvīsatiyā buddhānaṃ santikā bodhiyā laddhabyākaraṇo hutvā tattha tattha pāramiyo pūresi, tesaṃ paṭipattisaṅkhāto pubbenivāso, attano ca paṭipatti kathitā, idha pana tādiso adhikāro natthi[M 2.0014], yena dīpaṅkarato paṭṭhāya, tato vā pana purato buddhe ārabbha pubbenivāsaṃ katheyya. Tasmā na ettha buddhavaṃsadesanāyaṃ viya pubbenivāso vitthārito. Yasmā ca buddhānaṃ desanā nāma desanāya bhājanabhūtānaṃ puggalānaṃ ñāṇabalānurūpā, na attano ñāṇabalānurūpā, tasmā tattha aggasāvakānaṃ, mahāsāvakānaṃ, (theragā. aṭṭha. 2.21 vaṅgīsattheragāthāvaṇṇanā) tādisānañca [P 2.0017] devabrahmānaṃ vasena desanā vitthāritā. Idha pana pakatisāvakānaṃ, tādisānañca devatānaṃ vasena pubbenivāsaṃ kathento sattannameva buddhānaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ kathesi. Tathā hi ne bhagavā palobhanavasena samuttejetuṃ sappapañcatāya kathāya desanaṃ matthakaṃ apāpetvāva gandhakuṭiṃ pāvisi. Tathā ca imissā eva desanāya anusārato āṭānāṭiyaparitta- (dī. ni. 3.275) desanādayo pavattā.

There, having made that question the topic and the reason for the story, he recounted his own practice and the past abodes—known as their practice—of those Buddhas, beginning with the Blessed One Dīpaṅkara, at whose feet he himself had made the great aspiration, and of the twenty-four Buddhas from whom he had received the prediction to enlightenment while fulfilling the perfections in various places. Here, however, there is no such topic whereby he would recount past abodes concerning the Buddhas starting from Dīpaṅkara or even from before him. Therefore, the account of past abodes is not elaborated here as it is in the Buddhavaṃsa discourse. And since the teaching of the Buddhas is in accordance with the intellectual capacity of the persons who are vessels for the teaching, not in accordance with his own intellectual capacity, the teaching there was elaborated for the sake of the chief disciples, the great disciples, and such devas and brahmās. Here, however, recounting past abodes for the sake of ordinary disciples and such devatās, he spoke of the past abodes of only seven Buddhas. Indeed, in order to entice and rouse them, the Blessed One entered the fragrant chamber without bringing the diversified discourse to its conclusion. And so, in accordance with this very teaching, discourses such as the Āṭānāṭiya Protection came about.

Apicettha [V 2.0013] bhagavā attano suddhāvāsacārikāvibhāviniyā uparidesanāya saṅgahatthaṃ vipassīādīnaṃ eva sattannaṃ sammāsambuddhānaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ kathesi. Tesaṃyeva hi sāvakā tadā ceva etarahi ca suddhāvāsabhūmiyaṃ ṭhitā, na aññesaṃ parinibbutattā. “Siddhatthatissaphussānaṃ kira buddhānaṃ sāvakā suddhāvāsesu upapannā upapattisamanantarameva imasmiṃ sāsane upakādayo viya arahattaṃ adhigantvā nacirasseva parinibbāyiṃsu, na tattha tattha yāvatāyukaṃ aṭṭhaṃsū”ti vadanti. Tathā yesaṃ sammāsambuddhānaṃ paṭivedhasāsanaṃ ekaṃsato nicchaye na ajjāpi dharati, na antarahitaṃ, te eva kittento vipassīādīnaṃyeva bhagavantānaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ imasmiṃ sutte kathesi veneyyajjhāsayavasena. Apubbācarimaniyamo pana aparāparaṃ saṃsaraṇakasattavāsavasena ekissā lokadhātuyā icchitoti na tenetaṃ virujjhatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Nirantaraṃ matthakaṃ pāpetvāti abhijātito paṭṭhāya yāva pātimokkhuddeso yāva tā buddhakiccasiddhi, tāva matthakaṃ sikhaṃ pāpetvā. Na tāva kathitoti yojanā.

Moreover, the Blessed One here recounted the past abodes of only the seven Perfectly Self-Enlightened Buddhas beginning with Vipassī in order to gather his audience for the higher teaching that reveals his own journeying in the Pure Abodes. For only their disciples, both in the past and at present, are established in the plane of the Pure Abodes; not the disciples of other Buddhas, as they have attained parinibbāna. They say: 'It seems the disciples of the Buddhas Siddhattha, Tissa, and Phussa, having been reborn in the Pure Abodes, attained arahantship immediately after rebirth—like Upaka and others in this Dispensation—and attained parinibbāna not long after, not remaining there for their full lifespan.' Likewise, praising only those Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones whose teaching of penetration certainly still exists today and has not disappeared, he recounted in this sutta the past abodes of only the Blessed Ones beginning with Vipassī, in accordance with the disposition of those to be trained. However, it should be understood that this does not contradict the principle of 'not before, not after,' which is held to apply to a single world-system on account of the dwelling of beings who wander repeatedly in saṃsāra. `Reaching the summit without interruption` means: from birth up to the recitation of the Pātimokkha, that is, up to the fulfillment of the Buddha's duties, having brought it to the summit, the peak. The connection is: 'it has not yet been told.'

Tantinti dhammatantiṃ, pariyattinti attho. Puttaputtamātuyānavihāradhanavihāradāyakādīnaṃ sambahulānaṃ atthānaṃ vibhāvanavasena pavattavāro sambahulavāro.

`The tradition` means the tradition of the Dhamma; the meaning is the textual teaching. The 'Section of Numerous Matters' is the section that proceeds by way of explaining numerous matters, such as son, grandson, mother, vehicle, monastery, wealth, donor of a monastery, and so on.

Sambahulavāravaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Section of Numerous Matters

Kāmañcāyaṃ [M 2.0015] pāḷiyaṃ anāgato, aṭṭhakathāsu āgatattā pana ānetvā [P 2.0018] dīpetabboti taṃ dīpento “sabbabodhisattānañhī”tiādimāha. Kulavaṃso kulānukkamo. Paveṇīti paramparā. “Kasmā”ti puttuppattiyā kāraṇaṃ pucchitvā taṃ vissajjento “sabbaññubodhisattānañhī”tiādimāha, tena tesaṃ jātanagarādi paññāyamānaṃ ekaṃsato manussabhāvasañjānanatthaṃ icchitabbaṃ, aññathā yathādhippetabuddhakiccasiddhi eva na siyāti dasseti, yato mahāsattānaṃ carimabhave manussaloke eva pātubhāvo, na aññattha.

Although this passage is not found in the Pāḷi, since it is found in the commentaries it should be presented and explained. Explaining it, he says: 'Indeed, for all Bodhisattas...' and so on. `Kulavaṃso` means family lineage, succession of the family. `Paveṇī` means tradition. Having asked 'Why?' regarding the reason for the birth of a son, he answers by saying: 'Indeed, for the omniscient Bodhisattas...' and so on. By this he shows that their being known by their birth-city and so on is to be desired for the sake of recognizing their human state with certainty; otherwise the intended accomplishment of a Buddha's duties would not be possible, since the great beings appear in their final existence only in the human world, not elsewhere.

Sambahulaparicchedavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Section of Numerous Matters

Candādīnaṃ sobhāvisesaṃ raheti cajāpetīti rāhu, rāhuggaho, idha pana rāhu viyāti rāhu. Bandhananti ca anatthuppattiṭṭhānataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tathā mahāsattena vuttavacanameva gahetvā kumārassa “rāhulo”ti nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Athāti nipātamattaṃ. Rocinīti rocanasīlā, ujjalarūpāti [V 2.0014] attho. Rucaggatīti rucaṃ pabhātaṃ āgatibhūtā, ga-kārāgamaṃ katvā vuttaṃ. Itthiratanabhāvato manussaloke sabbāsaṃ itthīnaṃ bimbapaṭicchannabhūtāti bimbā.

Because he abandons and causes to be abandoned the special beauty of the moon and others, he is Rāhu, the seizer. Here, however, it is 'like Rāhu,' thus Rāhu. And 'a fetter' is said with reference to its being a basis for the arising of misfortune. Thus, taking the very words spoken by the Great Being, they gave the prince the name 'Rāhula.' `Atha` is merely a particle. `Rocinī` means 'of shining nature'; the meaning is 'of radiant form.' `Rucaggatī`: she is the arrival of light, of dawn; it is stated with the insertion of the augment `ga`. Because she was a jewel among women, in the human world she was like a reflection that outshone all other women; thus, Bimbā.

Jhānā vuṭṭhāyāti pādakajjhānato uṭṭhāya.

“Having emerged from jhāna” means having risen from the foundational jhāna.

Aṭṭhaṅgulubbedhāti aṭṭhaṅgulappamāṇabahalabhāvā. Cūḷaṃsena chādetvāti tiriyabhāgena ṭhapanavasena sabbaṃ vihāraṭṭhānaṃ chādetvā. Suvaṇṇayaṭṭhiphālehīti phālappamāṇāhi suvaṇṇayaṭṭhīhi. Suvaṇṇahatthipādānīti pakatihatthipādaparimāṇāni suvaṇṇakhaṇḍāni. Vuttanayenevāti cūḷaṃseneva. Suvaṇṇakaṭṭīhīti suvaṇṇakhaṇḍehi. Salakkhaṇānanti lakkhaṇasampannānaṃ sahassārānaṃ.

“Eight fingers thick” means having a thickness of the measure of eight fingers. “Covered with small sections” means covering the entire monastery site by placing them transversely. “With golden rod-ploughshares” means with golden rods the size of ploughshares. “Golden elephant feet” means pieces of gold the size of natural elephant feet. “In the same way” means just as with the small sections. “With golden planks” means with pieces of gold. “With auspicious marks” means of thousand-spoked wheels endowed with auspicious marks.

Bodhipallaṅkoti abhisambujjhanakāle nisajjaṭṭhānaṃ. Avijahitoti [P 2.0019] buddhānaṃ tathānisajjāya anaññatthabhāvībhāvato apariccatto. Tenāha “ekasmiṃyeva ṭhāne hotī”ti. Paṭhamapadagaṇṭhikāti pacchime sopānaphalake ṭhatvā ṭhapiyamānassa dakkhiṇapādassa patiṭṭhahanaṭṭhānaṃ. Taṃ pana yasmā daḷhaṃ thiraṃ kenaci abhejjaṃ hoti, tasmā “padagaṇṭhī”ti vuttaṃ. Yasmiṃ [M 2.0016] bhūmibhāge idāni jetavanamahāvihāro, tattha yasmiṃ ṭhāne purimānaṃ sabbabuddhānaṃ mañcā paññattā, tasmiṃyeva padese amhākampi bhagavato mañco paññattoti katvā “cattāri mañcapādaṭṭhānāni avijahitāneva hontī”ti vuttaṃ. Mañcānaṃ pana mahantakhuddakabhāvena mañcapaññāpanapadesassa mahantāmahantatā appamāṇaṃ, buddhānubhāvena pana so padeso sabbadā ekappamāṇoyeva hotīti “cattāri mañcapādaṭṭhānāni avijahitāneva hontī”ti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vihāropi na vijahito yevāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Purimaṃ vihāraṭṭhānaṃ na pariccajatīti hi attho.

“The seat of awakening” is the place of sitting at the time of full enlightenment. “Unforsaken” means not given up, because the Buddhas' sitting thus is not liable to be elsewhere. Therefore he said: “It is in one place only.” “The first foot-knot” is the place where the right foot is placed when one is standing on the last plank of the staircase. And since it is firm, stable, and unbreakable by anyone, it is called a “foot-knot.” In that region of ground where the Jetavana Great Monastery is now, in the very place where the couches of all previous Buddhas were prepared, the couch of our Blessed One too was prepared; thus it is said: “The four places for the couch-legs are indeed unforsaken.” But due to the couches being large and small, the size of the spot for preparing the couch could be of any measure; however, through the Buddha's power that spot is always of one and the same measure. Thus it should be understood that it is said: “The four places for the couch-legs are indeed unforsaken.” The monastery too is indeed not forsaken; here too this is the method. For the meaning is that the former monastery site is not given up.

Visiṭṭhā mattā vimattā, vimattāva vemattaṃ, visadisatāti attho. Pamāṇaṃ āroho. Padhānaṃ dukkarakiriyā. Rasmīti sarīrappabhā.

“Vimattā” is a distinguished measure. “Vemattaṃ” is just “vimattā”; the meaning is dissimilarity. “Measure” is height. “Striving” is the practice of austerities. “Rays” means the radiance of the body.

“Sattānaṃ pākatikahatthena chahattho majjhimapuriso, tato tiguṇaṃ bhagavato sarīrappamāṇanti bhagavā aṭṭhārasahattho”ti vadanti. Apare pana bhaṇanti “manussānaṃ pākatikahatthena catuhattho majjhimapuriso, tato tiguṇaṃ bhagavato sarīrappamāṇanti bhagavā dvādasahattho upādinnakarūpadhammavasena, samantato pana byāmamattaṃ byāmappabhā pharatīti upari chahatthaṃ abbhuggato, bahalatarappabhā rūpena saddhiṃ aṭṭhārasahattho hotī”ti.

They say: “An average person is six cubits tall measured by a being's natural cubit, and the Blessed One's body is three times that size; therefore the Blessed One is eighteen cubits tall.” But others say: “An average person is four cubits tall measured by a human's natural cubit, and the Blessed One's body is three times that size, making the Blessed One twelve cubits tall in terms of the material phenomena produced by clinging. However, his fathom-wide radiance pervades for a fathom all around; and having risen six cubits above, he is eighteen cubits tall with his thicker radiance together with his form.”

Addhaniyanti [V 2.0015] dīghakālaṃ.

“Addhaniya” means lasting a long time.

Ajjhāsayapaṭibaddhanti bodhisambhārasambharaṇakāle tathāpavattajjhāsayādhīnaṃ, tathāpavattapatthanānurūpaṃ vipulaṃ, vipulatarañca [P 2.0020] hotīti attho. Svāyamattho cariyāpiṭakavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Ettha ca yasmā sarīrappamāṇaṃ, padhānaṃ, sarīrappabhā ca buddhānaṃ visadisāti idha pāḷiyaṃ anāgatā, tasmā tehi saddhiṃ vemattatāsāmaññena āyukulānipi idha āharitvā dīpitāni. Paṭividdhaguṇesūti adhigatasabbaññuguṇesu. Nanu ca bodhisambhāresu, veneyyapuggalaparimāṇe ca vemattaṃ natthīti? Saccaṃ natthi, tadubhayaṃ pana buddhaguṇaggahaṇena gahitameva hotīti na uddhaṭaṃ. Yadaggena hi sabbabuddhānaṃ buddhaguṇesu vemattaṃ natthi, tadaggena nesaṃ sambodhisambhāresupi vemattaṃ natthīti. Kasmā? Hetuanurūpatāya phalassa[M 2.0017], ekanteneva veneyyapuggalaparimāṇe vemattabhāvo vibhāvito. Mahābodhisattānañhi hetuavatthāyaṃ sambhatūpanissayindriyaparipākā veneyyapuggalā carimabhave arahattasampattiyā paripositāni kamalavanāni sūriyarasmisamphassena viya tathāgataguṇānubhāvasamphassena vibodhaṃ upagacchantīti dīpesuṃ aṭṭhakathācariyā.

“Bound to disposition”: the meaning is that during the accumulation of the provisions for awakening, it is dependent on the disposition that has so arisen, and it becomes vast, and still vaster, in accordance with the aspiration that has so arisen. This meaning should be understood in the same way as explained in the commentary on the Cariyāpiṭaka. Here, because the physical size, striving, and radiance of the Buddhas are dissimilar, and these are not mentioned in the Pāḷi, therefore, along with these, differences in lifespan and clan are also introduced here by way of their commonality of difference. “In those who have penetrated the qualities” means in those who have attained the qualities of omniscience. But is there not no difference in the provisions for awakening or in the measure of trainable individuals? It is true that there is none. However, both are included by the taking up of the Buddha’s qualities, so they are not singled out. For in the supreme respect that there is no difference in the Buddha’s qualities among all Buddhas, in that same respect there is also no difference in their provisions for awakening. Why? Because the result corresponds to the cause. A difference in the measure of trainable individuals, however, has certainly been shown. For the commentary masters have explained that in the causal stage of the great bodhisattvas, the trainable individuals—whose faculties have been brought to maturity by the accumulated supporting conditions, nurtured in their final existence for the attainment of arahantship—awaken through contact with the power of the Tathāgata’s qualities, like lotus ponds touched by the sun’s rays.

Nidhikumbhoti cattāro mahānidhayo sandhāya vadati. Jāto cāti. Ca-saddena katamahābhinīhāro cāti ayampi attho saṅgahitoti daṭṭhabbo. Vuttaṃ hetaṃ buddhavaṃse –

“A pot of treasure”: this is said with reference to the four great treasures. “And born”: it should be understood that with the word `ca`, this meaning is also included: “and having made the great resolution.” For this has been said in the Buddhavaṃsa:

“Tārāgaṇā virocanti, nakkhattā gaganamaṇḍale;

Visākhā candimāyuttā, dhuvaṃ buddho bhavissatī”ti. (bu. vaṃ. 65);

“The hosts of stars shine, the constellations in the circle of the sky; Visākhā is conjoined with the moon—certainly, he will become a Buddha.” (Bv 2.65)

“Eteneva ca sabbabuddhānaṃ visākhānakkhatteneva mahābhinīhāro hotī”ti ca vadanti.

And they also say: “It is precisely in conjunction with the Visākhā constellation that the great resolution of all Buddhas occurs.”

13. Ayaṃ [P 2.0021] gatīti ayaṃ pavatti pavattanākāro, aññe pubbenivāsaṃ anussarantā iminā ākārena anussarantīti attho, yasmā cutito paṭṭhāya yāva paṭisandhi, tāva anussaraṇaṃ ārohanaṃ atītaatītataraatītatamādijātisaṅkhāte pubbenivāse ñāṇassa abhimukhabhāvena pavattīti katvā. Tasmā paṭisandhito paṭṭhāya yāva cuti, tāva anussaraṇaṃ orohanaṃ pubbenivāse paṭimukhabhāvena ñāṇassa pavattīti āha “pacchāmukhaṃ ñāṇaṃ pesetvā”ti. Cutigantabbanti yaṃ panidaṃ cutiyā ñāṇagatiyā gantabbaṃ, taṃ gamanaṃ bujjhananti attho. Garukanti bhāriyaṃ dukkaraṃ. Tenāha “ākāse padaṃ dassento viyā”ti. Aparampi kāraṇanti [V 2.0016] chinnavaṭumānussaraṇaṃ pacchāmukhaṃ ñāṇaṃ pesanato aparaṃ acchariyabbhutakāraṇaṃ. Yatrāti paccattatthe, nāmāti acchariyatthe nipāto, hi-saddo anatthako. Tenāha “yo nāma tathāgato”ti. Evañca katvā “yatrā”ti nipātavasena visuṃ yatra-saddaggahaṇaṃ samatthitaṃ hoti. Papañcenti sattasantānaṃ saṃsāre vitthārentīti papañcaṃ. Kammavaṭṭaṃ vuccatīti kilesavaṭṭassa papañcaggahaṇena, vipākavaṭṭassa dukkhaggahaṇena gahitattā. Pariyādinnavaṭṭeti sabbaso khepitavaṭṭe. “Maggasīlena phalasīlenā”ti vatvā tayidaṃ maggaphalasīlaṃ lokiyasīlapubbakaṃ, buddhānañca [M 2.0018] lokiyasīlampi lokuttarasīlaṃ viya anaññasādhāraṇaṃ evāti dassetuṃ “lokiyalokuttarasīlenā”ti vuttaṃ. Samādhipaññāsupi eseva nayo. Samādhipakkhāti samādhi ca samādhipakkhā ca samādhipakkhā, ekadesasarūpekaseso daṭṭhabbo. Tenāha “maggasamādhinā”tiādi, “vihāro gahito vā”ti ca. Samādhipakkhā nāma vīriyasatiādayo.

13. “This is the way”: this is the process, the mode of proceeding. The meaning is that others who recollect past lives recollect in this manner, because from death up to rebirth-linking, the recollection is an ascent, with knowledge proceeding forwards into past lives designated as past, more past, and most past. Therefore, from rebirth-linking up to death, the recollection is a descent, with knowledge proceeding backwards into past lives; hence it is said, “having sent knowledge backwards.” “To be gone to by death”: the meaning is that one understands that going which is to be gone to by the knowledge-course of death. “Difficult” means weighty, hard to do. Therefore he said: “like showing a footprint in the sky.” “Another reason”: another wonderful and marvelous reason apart from sending knowledge backwards to recollect a severed continuity. “Yatra” is in the reflexive sense; “nāma” is a particle in the sense of wonder; the word “hi” is meaningless. Therefore he says: “who indeed is the Tathāgata.” And by this, the separate taking of the word “yatra” as a particle is justified. “They proliferate”: they extend the continuity of beings in saṃsāra, thus they are “proliferations.” The round of kamma is meant, since the round of defilements is included by the term “proliferation” and the round of results is included by the term “suffering.” “Whose round is consumed”: whose round is exhausted in every way. Having said “by the virtue of the path and the virtue of the fruit,” to show that this virtue of path and fruit is preceded by mundane virtue, and that for Buddhas even mundane virtue is unique like supramundane virtue, it is said “by mundane and supramundane virtue.” In regard to concentration and wisdom too, this is the method. “The side of concentration”: concentration and things on the side of concentration are “the side of concentration”; this should be seen as an ellipsis of one of two similar forms. Therefore he says, “by the concentration of the path,” etc., and “or the abiding is included.” Things on the side of concentration are energy, mindfulness, and so on.

Sayanti attanā. Nīvaraṇādīhīti nīvaraṇehi ceva tadekaṭṭhehi ca pāpadhammehi, vitakkavicārādīhi ca. “Vimuttattā [P 2.0022] vimuttīti saṅkhyaṃ gacchantī”ti iminā vimutti-saddassa kammasādhanataṃ āha aṭṭhasamāpattiādivisayattā tassa. Vimuttattāti ca “vikkhambhanavasena vimuttattā”tiādinā yojetabbaṃ. Tassa tassāti aniccānupassanādikassa. Paccanīkaṅgavasenāti pahātabbapaṭipakkhaaṅgavasena. Paṭippassaddhante uppannattāti kilesānaṃ paṭippassambhanaṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ, so eva anto pariyosānabhāvato, tasmiṃ sādhetabbe nibbattattā, taṃtaṃmaggavajjhakilesānaṃ paṭippassambhanavasena pavattattāti attho. Kilesehi nissaṭatā, apagamo ca nibbānassa tehi vivittattā evāti āha “dūre ṭhitattā”ti.

They are so called in themselves. "By the hindrances, etc." means by the hindrances and by those unwholesome states associated with them, and by initial and sustained thought, etc. "Because of being liberated, they are reckoned as 'liberation'"—this explains the objective derivation of the word 'liberation' as it is the object of the eight attainments, etc. And "because of being liberated" should be connected with "because of being liberated by way of suppression," etc. "Of that, of that" refers to the contemplation of impermanence, etc. "By way of opposing factors" means by way of factors that are the opposing limbs to what is to be abandoned. "Because of arising in the pacified" means the pacification of defilements is called 'pacified'; that itself is the end because it is the final state; because it is produced when that is to be achieved, and because it proceeds by way of the pacification of the defilements to be abandoned by the respective paths—this is the meaning. The escape from and removal of defilements is precisely Nibbāna's seclusion from them; thus he says, "because of standing far away."

16. Dhammadhātūti dhammānaṃ sabhāvo, atthato cattāri ariyasaccāni. Suppaṭividdhāti suṭṭhu paṭividdhā savāsanānaṃ sabbesaṃ kilesānaṃ pajahanato. Evañhi sabbaññutā, dasabalañāṇādayo cāti sabbe buddhaguṇā bhagavatā adhigatā ahesuṃ. Arahattaṃ dhammadhātūti keci. Sabbaññutañāṇanti apare. Dvīhi padehīti dvīhi vākyehi. Ābaddhanti paṭibaddhaṃ taṃmūlakattā uparidesanāya. Devacārikakolāhalanti attano devaloke cārikāyaṃ suddhāvāsadevānaṃ kutūhalappavattiṃ dassento suttantapariyosāne (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.91) vicāressati, atthato vibhāvessatīti yojanā. Ayaṃ desanāti “ito so bhikkhave”tiādinā (dī. ni. 2.4) vitthārato pavattitadesanamāha. Nidānakaṇḍetiādito desitaṃ uddesadesanamāha. Sā hi imissā desanāya nidānaṭṭhāniyattā tathā vuttā.

16. "The element of phenomena" is the nature of phenomena; in meaning, it refers to the four noble truths. "Well penetrated" means thoroughly penetrated because of abandoning all defilements along with their latent tendencies. For thus omniscience, the knowledge of the ten powers, and so on—all the qualities of the Buddha—were attained by the Blessed One. Some say the element of phenomena is arahantship; others say it is the knowledge of omniscience. "By two clauses" means by two statements. "Connected" means linked because it is the basis of the subsequent teaching. "The commotion of the divine procession" refers to showing the curiosity arising among the pure abode deities during their procession in their own divine world—as will be discussed and explained in detail at the end of the sutta (Dī.A. 2.91). This is the meaning to be construed. "This teaching" refers to the detailed teaching given starting with "From this, monks," etc. (Dī. 2.4). "From the chapter on the introduction," etc., refers to the summary teaching given. For that is called so because it serves as the introduction to this teaching.

Bodhisattadhammatāvaṇṇanā

An Exposition of the Bodhisatta's Nature

17. “Vipassīti [V 2.0017] tassa nāma”nti vatvā tassa anvatthataṃ dassetuṃ “tañca kho”tiādi vuttaṃ. Vividhe attheti tirohitavidūradesagatādike nīlādivasena [M 2.0019] nānāvidhe, tadaññe ca indriyagocarabhūte te ca yathūpagate, vohāravinicchaye cāti nānāvidhe atthe. Passanakusalatāyāti dassane nipuṇabhāvena. Yāthāvato [P 2.0023] ñeyyaṃ bujjhatīti bodhi, so eva sattayogato bodhisattoti āha “paṇḍitasatto bujjhanakasatto”ti. Sucintitacintitādinā pana paṇḍitabhāve vattabbameva natthi. Yadā ca panānena mahābhinīhāro kato, tato paṭṭhāya mahābodhiyaṃ ekantaninnattā bodhimhi satto bodhisattoti āha “bodhisaṅkhātesū”tiādi.
