Maggañāṇapadaṭṭhānañhi sabbaññutañāṇaṃ, sabbaññutañāṇapadaṭṭhānañca maggañāṇaṃ “bodhī”ti vuccati. “Sato sampajāno”ti iminā catutthāya gabbhāvakkantiyā okkamīti dasseti. Catasso hi gabbhāvakkantiyo idhekacco gabbho mātukucchiyaṃ okkamane, ṭhāne, nikkhamaneti tīsu ṭhānesu asampajāno hoti, ekacco paṭhame ṭhāne sampajāno, na itaresu, ekacco paṭhame, dutiye ca ṭhāne sampajāno, na tatiye, ekacco tīsupi ṭhānesu sampajāno hoti. Tattha paṭhamā gabbhāvakkanti lokiyamahājanassa vasena vuttā, dutiyā asītimahāsāvakānaṃ (theragā. aṭṭha. 2.21 vaṅgīsattheragāthāvaṇṇanāya vitthāro) vasena, tatiyā dvinnaṃ aggasāvakānaṃ, paccekabuddhānañca vasena. Te kira kammajavātehi uddhaṃpādā adhosirā anekasataporise papāte viya yonimukhe khittā tāḷacchiggaḷena hatthī viya sambādhena yonimukhena nikkhamantā mahantaṃ dukkhaṃ pāpuṇanti, tena nesaṃ “mayaṃ nikkhamāmā”ti sampajaññaṃ na hoti. Catutthā sabbaññubodhisattānaṃ vasena. Te hi mātukucchimhi paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhantāpi pajānanti, tattha vasantāpi pajānanti, nikkhamanakālepi pajānanti. Na hi te kammajavātā uddhaṃpāde adhosire katvā khipituṃ sakkonti, dve hatthe pasāritvā akkhīni ummīletvā ṭhitakāva nikkhamantīti. Ñāṇena paricchinditvāti pubbabhāge pañcamahāvilokanañāṇehi ceva “idāni cavāmī”ti cutiparicchindanañāṇena ca aparabhāge “idha mayā paṭisandhi gahitā”ti paṭisandhiparicchindanañāṇena ca paricchijja jānitvā.

17. Having said, 'Vipassī was his name,' to show its etymological meaning, 'and that indeed,' etc., was said. 'In various meanings' means in various objects, such as those that are concealed, distant, in other regions, and so on; those that are of various kinds by way of blue, etc.; others that are objects of the sense faculties as they have come to be; and in matters of conventional judgment. 'By skill in seeing' means by proficiency in seeing. 'He awakens to what is to be known as it really is,' thus it is enlightenment (bodhi). He, because of his connection with a being (satta), is a Bodhisatta. Thus it is said, 'a wise being, an awakening being.' But regarding his state of wisdom, with such things as 'well-considered thoughts,' there is nothing more to be said. And when he made the great aspiration, from then on, being solely inclined toward great enlightenment, he was attached (satto) to enlightenment (bodhi), thus a Bodhisatta. Thus it is said, 'in what is reckoned as enlightenment,' etc. For the knowledge of the path is the proximate cause of omniscient knowledge, and omniscient knowledge is the proximate cause of the knowledge of the path; this is called 'enlightenment.' 'Mindful and fully aware'—by this it is shown that he entered the womb by the fourth way of entering the womb. For there are four ways of entering the womb: one being is not fully aware at the three stages of entering the mother’s womb, abiding there, and emerging; another is fully aware at the first stage but not the others; another is fully aware at the first and second stages but not the third; and another is fully aware at all three stages. Here, the first way of entering the womb is described in terms of ordinary people. The second is in terms of the eighty great disciples (as detailed in the commentary on the Theragāthā). The third is in terms of the two chief disciples and the Paccekabuddhas. For it is said that they, propelled by karmic winds with their feet up and heads down, are cast into the opening of the womb as if into an abyss of many hundreds of men's depth; emerging through the constricted womb-opening like an elephant through a keyhole, they experience great suffering. Thus they have no full awareness that 'we are emerging.' The fourth way is in terms of the omniscient Bodhisattas. For they are aware when taking relinking in the mother’s womb, they are aware while abiding there, and they are aware at the time of emerging. The karmic winds are not able to cast them out with feet up and heads down; rather, they emerge with their two hands stretched out and their eyes open, as if standing. 'Having delimited by knowledge' means having known by delimiting, in the earlier phase, with the five great investigations and with the knowledge that delimits death—'Now I am passing away'—and in the later phase, with the knowledge that delimits relinking—'Here relinking has been taken by me.'

Pañcannaṃ [P 2.0024] mahāpariccāgānaṃ, ñātatthacariyādīnañca satipi pāramiyā pariyāpannabhāve sambhāravisesabhāvadassanatthaṃ visuṃ gahaṇaṃ. Tattha aṅgapariccāgo, nayanapariccāgo, attapariccāgo, rajjapariccāgo, puttadārapariccāgoti ime [M 2.0020] pañca mahāpariccāgā. Tatthāpi kāmaṃ aṅgapariccāgādayopi dānapāramīyeva, tathāpi pariccāgavisesabhāvadassanatthañceva sudukkarabhāvadassanatthañca [V 2.0018] mahāpariccāgānaṃ visuṃ gahaṇaṃ. Tato eva ca aṅgapariccāgatopi visuṃ nayanapariccāgaggahaṇaṃ, pariccāgabhāvasāmaññepi rajjapariccāgaputtadārapariccāgaggahaṇañca kataṃ. Ñātīnaṃ atthacariyā ñātatthacariyā, sā ca kho karuṇāyanavasena. Tathā sattalokassa diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikaparamatthānaṃ vasena hitacariyā lokatthacariyā. Kammassakatāñāṇavasena, anavajjakammāyatanasippāyatanavijjāṭhānavasena, khandhāyatanādivasena, lakkhaṇattayāditīraṇavasena ca attano, paresañca tattha satipaṭṭhānena ñāṇacāro buddhacariyā, sā panatthato paññāpāramīyeva, ñāṇasambhāravisesatādassanatthaṃ pana visuṃ gahaṇaṃ. Buddhacariyānanti bahuvacananiddesena pubbayogapubbacariyādhammakkhānādīnaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Tattha gatapaccāgatavattasaṅkhātāya pubbabhāgapaṭipadāya saddhiṃ abhiññāsamāpattinipphādanaṃ pubbayogo. Dānādīsuyeva sātisayapaṭipatti pubbacariyā. “Yāva cariyāpiṭake saṅgahitā abhinīhāro pubbayogo, kāyādivivekavasena ekacariyā pubbacariyā”ti keci. Dānādīnañceva appicchatādīnañca saṃsāranibbānesu ādīnavānisaṃsānañca vibhāvanavasena, sattānaṃ bodhittaye patiṭṭhāpanaparipācanavasena [P 2.0025] ca pavattakathā dhammakkhānaṃ. Koṭiṃ patvāti paraṃ pariyantaṃ paramukkaṃsaṃ pāpuṇitvā. Sattamahādānānīti aṭṭhavassikakāle “hadayamaṃsādīnipi yācakānaṃ dadeyya”nti ajjhāsayaṃ uppādetvā dinnadānaṃ, maṅgalahatthidānaṃ, gamanakāle dinnaṃ sattasattakamahādānaṃ, maggaṃ gacchantena dinnaṃ assadānaṃ, rathadānaṃ, puttadānaṃ, bhariyādānanti imāni satta mahādānāni (cariyā. 79) datvā.

The five great renunciations, and the practice for the welfare of relatives, etc., are mentioned separately, even though they are included within the perfections, in order to show their status as a special accumulation. Herein, the five great renunciations are: the renunciation of limbs, the renunciation of eyes, the renunciation of one's own life, the renunciation of sovereignty, and the renunciation of sons and wives. Although the renunciation of limbs and so on are indeed the perfection of giving, nevertheless, the great renunciations are mentioned separately to show their status as a special kind of renunciation and to show how very difficult they are to perform. For this very reason, the renunciation of the eyes is mentioned separately from the renunciation of limbs; and despite the general nature of renunciation, the renunciation of the kingdom and of sons and wife are also mentioned separately. The practice for the welfare of relatives (ñātatthacariyā) is acting for the welfare of one's relatives, and this is by way of compassion. Similarly, the practice for the welfare of the world (lokatthacariyā) is acting for the benefit of the world of beings, with regard to their welfare in this life, in future lives, and their ultimate welfare. The conduct of a Buddha (buddhacariyā) is the practice of knowledge, with mindfulness established therein for oneself and others, by way of the knowledge of ownership of kamma; by way of the bases of blameless action, skills, and fields of knowledge; by way of the aggregates, sense bases, etc.; and by way of investigating the three characteristics, etc. This is in essence the perfection of wisdom, but it is mentioned separately to show its status as a special accumulation of knowledge. By the plural designation 'conducts of the Buddhas' (Buddhacariyānaṃ), the inclusion of previous endeavor, previous conduct, the teaching of the Dhamma, etc., should be understood. Herein, previous endeavor (pubbayogo) is the accomplishment of the superknowledges and meditative attainments, together with the preliminary practice consisting of the duty of going and returning. Previous conduct (pubbacariyā) is the surpassing practice in giving, etc. Some say: 'The aspiration included in the Cariyāpiṭaka is previous endeavor; solitary practice by way of seclusion of body, etc., is previous conduct.' The teaching of the Dhamma (dhammakkhānaṃ) is the discourse given by way of explaining the dangers in saṃsāra and the benefits in Nibbāna regarding giving, etc., and having few wishes, etc., and by way of establishing and maturing beings in the threefold enlightenment. 'Having reached the limit' means having attained the furthest boundary, the supreme excellence. Having given the seven great gifts: the gift given after forming the intention at the age of eight, 'I would give even my heart and flesh to supplicants'; the gift of the auspicious elephant; the seven-times-seven great gift given at the time of departure; the gift of a horse given while traveling on the road; the gift of a chariot; the gift of a son; and the gift of a wife (Cariyā. 79)—

“Idāneva me maraṇaṃ hotū”ti adhimuccitvā kālakaraṇaṃ adhimuttikālakiriyā, taṃ bodhisattānaṃyeva, na aññesaṃ. Bodhisattā kira dīghāyukadevaloke ṭhitā “idha ṭhitassa me bodhisambhārasambharaṇaṃ na sambhavatī”ti katvā tattha vāsato nibbindamānasā honti, tadā vimānaṃ pavisitvā akkhīni nimīletvā “ito uddhaṃ me jīvitaṃ nappavattatū”ti cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāya nisīdanti, cittādhiṭṭhānasamanantarameva maraṇaṃ hoti. Pāramīdhammānañhi [M 2.0021] ukkaṃsappavattiyā tasmiṃ tasmiṃ attabhāve abhiññāsamāpattīhi santānassa visesitattā attasinehassa tanubhāvena, sattesu ca mahākaruṇāya uḷārabhāvena adhiṭṭhānassa tikkhavisadabhāvāpattiyā bodhisattānaṃ adhippāyā samijjhanti. Citte, viya kammesu ca nesaṃ vasībhāvo, tasmā yattha upapannānaṃ pāramiyo sammadeva paribrūhanti. Vuttanayena kālaṃ katvā tattha upapajjanti. Tathā hi amhākaṃ mahāsatto imasmiṃyeva kappe nānājātīsu aparihīnajjhāno kālaṃ katvā brahmaloke nibbatto, appakameva kālaṃ tattha ṭhatvā tato cavitvā manussaloke nibbatto, pāramīsambharaṇapasuto ahosi. Tena vuttaṃ “bodhisattānaṃyeva, na [V 2.0019] aññesa”nti. “Ekenaattabhāvena antarena pāramīnaṃ sabbaso pūritattā”ti iminā payojanābhāvato tattha ṭhatvā adhimuttikālakiriyā [P 2.0026] nāma nāhosīti dasseti. Api ca tattha yāvatāyukaṭṭhānaṃ carimabhave anekamahānidhisamuṭṭhānapubbikāya dibbasampattisadisāya mahāsampattiyā nibbatti viya, buddhabhūtassa asadisadānādivasena anaññasādhāraṇalābhuppatti viya ca “ito paraṃ mahāpurisassa dibbasampattianubhavanaṃ nāma natthī”ti ussāhajātassa puññasambhārassa vasenāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ayañhettha dhammatā.

Having resolved, 'May my death occur right now,' the act of dying by resolution is called 'adhimuttikālakiriyā.' This is for Bodhisattas alone, not for others. It is said that when Bodhisattas are dwelling in a deva world of long-lived beings, thinking, 'While dwelling here, the accumulation of the requisites for enlightenment is not possible for me,' they become disenchanted with that abode. Then, entering their celestial mansion and closing their eyes, they sit down having made the resolution, 'Henceforth, may my life not continue.' Death occurs immediately after this mental resolution. For, due to the excellent development of their perfections in each existence, their mental continuum having been distinguished by the direct knowledges and meditative attainments, because of the attenuation of their self-love, and because of the sublimity of their great compassion for beings and the attainment of a sharp and clear resolve, the intentions of the Bodhisattas succeed. They have mastery over their minds and, as it were, over their kamma; therefore, they are reborn wherever their perfections are perfectly fulfilled. Having died in the way described, they are reborn there. Thus our Great Being, in this very eon, having died in various births without losing his jhāna, was reborn in the brahmā world. Having dwelt there for only a short time, he passed away from there and was reborn in the human world, intent on accumulating the perfections. Therefore it is said: 'This is for Bodhisattas alone, not for others.' By the words, 'Because the perfections have been completely fulfilled within a single existence,' it is shown that since it serves no purpose, there is no such thing as dying by resolution while dwelling there. Moreover, it should be understood that this is by the power of the accumulation of merit born of the zeal expressed as: 'Henceforth there is no more enjoyment of divine fortune for the Great Being.' This is just like the arising of great fortune similar to divine fortune in the final existence, where one dwells for the full lifespan, which is preceded by the emergence of many great treasures; and just like the arising of unparalleled gain for one who has become a Buddha through unequaled giving and so on. This is the natural principle here.

Manussagaṇanāvasena, na devagaṇanāvasena. Pubbanimittānīti cutiyā pubbanimittāni. Amilāyitvāti ettha amilātaggahaṇeneva tāsaṃ mālānaṃ vaṇṇasampadāyapi gandhasampadāyapi sobhāsampadāyapi avināso dassitoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Bāhirabbhantarānaṃ rajojallānaṃ lepassapi abhāvato devānaṃ sarīragatāni vatthāni sabbakālaṃ parisuddhappabhassarāneva hutvā tiṭṭhantīti āha “vatthesupi eseva nayo”ti. Neva sītaṃ na uṇhanti yassa sītassa paṭikāravasena adhikaṃ seviyamānaṃ uṇhaṃ, sayameva vā kharataraṃ hutvā abhibhavantaṃ sarīre sedaṃ uppādeyya, tādisaṃ neva sītaṃ, na uṇhaṃ hoti. Tasmiṃ kāleti yathāvuttamaraṇāsannakāle. Bindubinduvasenāti chinnasuttāya āmuttamuttāvaliyā nipatantā muttaguḷikā viya bindu bindu hutvā. Sedāti sedadhārā muccanti. Dantānaṃ khaṇḍitabhāvo khaṇḍiccaṃ. Kesānaṃ palitabhāvo pāliccaṃ. Ādi-saddena valittacataṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Kilantarūpo attabhāvo hoti, na pana khaṇḍiccapāliccādīti [M 2.0022] adhippāyo. Ukkaṇṭhitāti anabhirati. Sā natthi [P 2.0027] uparūpari uḷārauḷārānameva bhogānaṃ visesato duvijānanānaṃ upatiṭṭhahanato. Nissasantīti uṇhaṃ nissasanti. Vijambhantīti anabhirativasena vijambhanaṃ karonti.

By way of human reckoning, not by way of deva reckoning. 'Preliminary signs' means the preliminary signs of passing away. 'Unfaded': here, by the mention of 'unfaded,' it should be understood that the non-perishing of the perfection of color, the perfection of fragrance, and the perfection of beauty of those garlands is shown. Because of the absence of any stain from external and internal dust and dirt, the garments on the bodies of the devas always remain pure and radiant; thus he says, 'the same principle applies to their garments.' 'Neither cold nor hot' means there is neither such cold that heat would have to be used excessively as a remedy, nor such heat that, becoming very harsh and overpowering, would produce sweat on the body. 'At that time' means at the time of approaching death as described. 'Drop by drop' means like pearls from a broken string of pearls falling one by one. 'Sweat' means streams of sweat are released. 'Khaṇḍicca' is the state of having broken teeth. 'Pālicca' is the state of having grey hair. By the word 'etcetera,' wrinkled skin is included. The personal existence becomes weary in appearance; the meaning is not that there is broken teeth, grey hair, and so on. 'Discontent' means dissatisfaction. That does not exist because of the attendance of ever more sublime pleasures, which are especially difficult to discern. 'They pant' means they exhale hot breaths. 'They yawn' means they yawn out of dissatisfaction.

Paṇḍitā evāti buddhisampannā eva devatā. Yathā devatā sampatijātā “kīdisena puññakammena idha nibbattā”ti cintetvā “iminā nāma puññakammena idha nibbattā”ti jānanti, evaṃ atītabhave attanā kataṃ, aññadāpi vā ekaccaṃ puññakammaṃ jānantiyeva mahāpuññāti āha “ye mahāpuññā”tiādi.

'Wise indeed' means deities endowed with wisdom. Just as deities, as soon as they are born, think, 'By what kind of meritorious kamma were we reborn here?' and know, 'We were reborn here by this meritorious kamma,' so too, being of great merit, they know a certain meritorious kamma done by themselves in a past existence, or on another occasion. Thus he says, 'those who are of great merit,' etc.

Na paññāyanti ciratarakālattā paramāyuno. Aniyyānikanti na niyyānāvahaṃ sattānaṃ abhājanabhāvato. Sattā na paramāyuno honti nāma pāpussannatāyāti āha “tadā hi sattā ussannakilesā hontī”ti. Etthāha – kasmā sammāsambuddhā manussaloke eva uppajjanti, na devabrahmalokesūti? Devaloke tāva nuppajjanti brahmacariyavāsassa anokāsabhāvato, tathā anacchariyabhāvato[V 2.0020]. Acchariyadhammā hi buddhā bhagavanto, tesaṃ sā acchariyadhammatā devattabhāve ṭhitānaṃ na pākaṭā hoti yathā manussabhūtānaṃ, devabhūte hi sammāsambuddhe dissamānaṃ buddhānubhāvaṃ devānubhāvato loko dahati, na buddhānubhāvato, tathā sati “sammāsambuddho”ti nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, issaraguttaggāhaṃ na vissajjeti, devattabhāvassa ca cirakālādhiṭṭhānato ekaccasassatavādato na parimuccati. Brahmaloke nuppajjantīti etthāpi eseva nayo. Sattānaṃ tādisaggāhavinimocanatthañhi buddhā bhagavanto manussasugatiyaṃyeva uppajjanti, na devasugatiyaṃ. Manussasugatiyaṃ uppajjantāpi opapātikā na honti, sati ca opapātikūpapattiyaṃ vuttadosānativattanato, dhammaveneyyānaṃ dhammatantiyā ṭhapanassa [P 2.0028] viya dhātuveneyyānaṃ dhātūnaṃ ṭhapanassa icchitabbattā ca. Na hi opapātikānaṃ parinibbānato uddhaṃ sarīradhātuyo tiṭṭhanti. Manussaloke uppajjantāpi mahābodhisattā carimabhave manussabhāvassa pākaṭabhāvakaraṇāya pana dārapariggahampi karontā yāva puttamukhadassanā agāramajjhe tiṭṭhanti, paripākagatasīlanekkhammapaññādipāramikāpi na abhinikkhamantīti. Kiṃ vā etāya [M 2.0023] kāraṇacintāya “sabbabuddhehi āciṇṇasamāciṇṇā, yadidaṃ manussabhūtānaṃyeva abhisambujjhanā, na devabhūtāna”nti. Ayamettha dhammatā. Tathā hi tadattho mahābhinīhāropi manussabhūtānaṃyeva ijjhati, na devabhūtānaṃ.

They are not discerned because of the very long duration of the maximum lifespan. 'Non-liberating' means not leading to release because beings are not suitable vessels. Beings do not have the maximum lifespan because of the prevalence of evil; thus he says, 'For then beings have abundant defilements.' Here one might ask: Why do Sammāsambuddhas arise only in the human world and not in the deva and brahmā worlds? They do not arise in the deva world, for one thing, because it is not a suitable occasion for living the brahmacariya, and also because of the lack of the marvelous. The Blessed Buddhas are possessors of marvelous qualities, but this marvelous nature of theirs is not as manifest when they are in the deva state as it is when they are human beings. For the world considers the Buddha-power seen in a Sammāsambuddha in deva form to be deva-power, not Buddha-power. In that case, one does not resolve upon him as a 'Sammāsambuddha' and does not gain confidence; one does not relinquish the grasp of the creator-god doctrine; and one is not freed from a certain eternalist view because of the long duration of the deva state. The same principle applies to why they do not arise in the brahmā world. It is for the purpose of releasing beings from such a grasp that the Blessed Buddhas arise only in the human good destination, not in the deva good destination. Even when arising in the human good destination, they are not of spontaneous birth, for if they were of spontaneous birth, the faults mentioned would not be overcome, and because, just as the establishment of the teaching of the Dhamma for those to be trained by the Dhamma is desirable, so too is the establishment of the relics for those to be trained by the relics. For the bodily relics of those of spontaneous birth do not remain after their Parinibbāna. Even when arising in the human world, the Great Bodhisattas in their final existence, in order to make their human state manifest, take a wife and dwell in the home until they see the face of their son. Although their perfections of virtue, renunciation, wisdom, etc., have reached maturity, they do not go forth. But what is the use of this line of reasoning? 'It is the practice and custom of all Buddhas that they awaken to full enlightenment only as human beings, not as devas.' This is the natural principle here. For the great resolution for that purpose succeeds only for human beings, not for devas.

Kasmā pana sammāsambuddhā jambudīpe eva uppajjanti, na sesadīpesu? Keci tāva āhu “yasmā pathaviyā nābhibhūtā, buddhānubhāvasahitā acalaṭṭhānabhūtā bodhimaṇḍabhūmi jambudīpe eva, tasmā jambudīpe eva uppajjantī”ti, tathā “itaresampi avijahitaṭṭhānānaṃ tattheva labbhanato”ti. Ayaṃ panettha amhākaṃ khanti – yasmā purimabuddhānaṃ, mahābodhisattānaṃ, paccekabuddhānañca nibbattiyā sāvakabodhisattānaṃ sāvakabodhiyā abhinīhāro, sāvakapāramiyā sambharaṇaṃ, paripācanañca buddhakhettabhūte imasmiṃ cakkavāḷe jambudīpe eva ijjhati, na aññattha. Veneyyānaṃ vinayanattho ca buddhuppādoti aggasāvakamahāsāvakādi veneyyavisesāpekkhāya etasmiṃ jambudīpe eva buddhā nibbattanti, na sesadīpesu. Ayañca nayo sabbabuddhānaṃ āciṇṇasamāciṇṇoti. Tesaṃ uttamapurisānaṃ tattheva uppatti sampatticakkānaṃ viya aññamaññūpanissayato aparāparaṃ [P 2.0029] vattatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ, eteneva imaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ majjhe katvā iminā saddhiṃ cakkavāḷānaṃ dasasahassasseva khettabhāvo dīpito ito aññassa buddhānaṃ uppattiṭṭhānassa tepiṭake buddhavacane anupalabbhanato. Tenāha “tīsu dīpesu buddhā na nibbattanti, jambudīpeyeva nibbattantīti dīpaṃ passī”ti. Iminā nayena desaniyāmepi kāraṇaṃ nīharitvā vattabbaṃ.

But why do Sammāsambuddhas arise only in Jambudīpa and not in the other continents? Some say: 'Because the site of the Bodhimaṇḍa—not overcome by the earth, endowed with the Buddha's power, an immovable place—exists only in Jambudīpa, therefore they arise only in Jambudīpa.' And also: 'Because the other unabandoned sites are obtainable there.' This, however, is our preferred view: Because the arising of past Buddhas, Great Bodhisattas, and Paccekabuddhas, and the aspiration for the disciples' enlightenment by disciple-bodhisattas, the accumulation of the disciples' perfections, and their maturation succeed only in Jambudīpa within this world-system, which is a Buddha-field, and not elsewhere. And since the purpose of a Buddha's appearance is the training of those to be trained, with regard to the special disciples such as the chief disciples and great disciples, the Buddhas are born in this Jambudīpa, not in the other continents. And this is the practice and custom of all Buddhas. It should be understood that the arising of these supreme persons in that very place proceeds successively through mutual support, like the wheels of attainment. By this it is shown that the Buddha-field is just the ten-thousandfold world-system with this world-system at its center, because no other place for the arising of Buddhas is found in the word of the Buddha in the Tipiṭaka. Therefore he said: 'Buddhas do not arise in the three continents; they arise only in Jambudīpa,' and so he surveyed the continent. In this way, the reason should also be stated by extracting it in accordance with the fixed order of the teaching.

Idāni [V 2.0021] ca khattiyakulaṃ lokasammataṃ brāhmaṇānampi pūjanīyabhāvato. “Rājā pitā bhavissatī”ti kulaṃ passi pituvasena kulassa niddisitabbato.

And now the khattiya clan is esteemed by the world because it is venerable even to the brahmins. 'The king will be the father': he surveyed the clan because the clan is to be designated by way of the father.

“Dasannaṃ māsānaṃ upari satta divasānī”ti passi, tena attano antarāyābhāvaṃ aññāsi, tassā ca tusitabhave dibbasampattipaccanubhavanaṃ.

He saw, 'Seven days over and above ten months'; thereby he knew the absence of danger for himself, and her experience of divine fortune in the Tusita existence.

Tā devatāti dasasahassicakkavāḷadevatā. Kathaṃ pana tā devatā tadā bodhisattassa pūritapāramibhāvaṃ, kathaṃ cassa buddhabhāvaṃ jānantīti? Mahesakkhānaṃ [M 2.0024] devatānaṃ vasena, yebhuyyena ca tā devatā abhisamayabhāgino. Tathā hi bhagavato dhammadānasaṃvibhāge anekavāraṃ dasasahassacakkavāḷadevatāsannipāto ahosi.

Those deities are the deities of the ten-thousandfold world-system. But how did those deities know then of the Bodhisatta's fulfillment of the perfections, and how did they know of his Buddhahood? It was through the influence of the deities of great power, and for the most part, those deities were destined for realization. Indeed, during the Blessed One's distribution of the gift of Dhamma, there were gatherings of deities from the ten-thousandfold world-system on many occasions.

“Cavāmī”ti jānāti cutiāsannajavanehi ñāṇasahitehi cutiyā upaṭṭhitabhāvassa paṭisaṃviditattā. Cuticittaṃ na jānāti cuticittakkhaṇassa ittarabhāvato. Tathā hi taṃ cutūpapātañāṇassapi avisayova. Paṭisandhicittepi eseva nayo. Āvajjanapariyāyoti āvajjanakkamo. Yasmā ekavāraṃ āvajjitamattena ārammaṇaṃ nicchinituṃ na sakkā, tasmā taṃ evārammaṇaṃ dutiyaṃ, tatiyañca āvajjitvā nicchayati. Āvajjanasīsena cettha javanavāro gahito. Tenāha “dutiyatatiyacittavāre eva jānissatī”ti. Cutiyā puretaraṃ katipayacittavārato paṭṭhāya “maraṇaṃ me āsanna”nti [P 2.0030] jānanato “cutikkhaṇepi cavāmīti jānātī”ti vuttaṃ. Paṭisandhiyā pana apubbabhāvato paṭisandhicittaṃ na jānāti. Nikantiyā uppattito parato “asukasmiṃ me ṭhāne paṭisandhi gahitā”ti jānāti. Tasmiṃ kāleti paṭisandhiggahaṇakāle. Dasasahassilokadhātu kampatīti ettha kampanakāraṇaṃ heṭṭhā brahmajālavaṇṇanāyaṃ (dī. ni. ṭī. 1.149) vuttameva. Atthato panettha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ parato mahāparinibbānavaṇṇanāyaṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.171) āgamissati. Mahākāruṇikā buddhā bhagavanto sattānaṃ hitasukhavidhānatapparatāya bahulaṃ somanassikāva hontīti tesaṃ paṭhamamahāvipākacittena paṭisandhiggahaṇaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.17; dha. sa. aṭṭha. 498; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 4.200) vuttaṃ. Mahāsivattheropana yadipi mahākāruṇikā buddhā bhagavanto sattānaṃ hitasukhavidhānatapparāva, vivekajjhāsayā pana visaṅkhāraninnā sabbasaṅkhāresu ajjhupekkhanabahulāti pañcamamahāvipākacittena paṭisandhiggahaṇamāha.

“He knows, ‘I am passing away,’” because he has comprehended that the state of death is present by means of the death-proximate javanas accompanied by knowledge. He does not know the death-consciousness, because the moment of the death-consciousness is so brief. Indeed, it is beyond the range even of the knowledge of passing away and rebirth. The same method applies to the rebirth-linking consciousness. The ‘sequence of adverting’ is the order of adverting. Since the object cannot be ascertained by adverting to it only once, one ascertains it by adverting to that same object a second and a third time. Here, the javana process is taken under the heading of adverting. Therefore it is said: “He will know only in the second or third thought-process.” Because one knows, “My death is near,” starting from a few thought-processes before death, it is therefore said: “At the moment of death, he knows, ‘I am passing away.’” However, he does not know the rebirth-linking consciousness because of its unprecedented nature. After the arising of craving, he knows: “My rebirth-linking has been taken in such and such a place.” “At that time” means at the time of grasping rebirth-linking. “The ten-thousandfold world-system trembles”: the cause of the trembling here has been stated below in the subcommentary on the Brahmajāla Sutta (Dī. Ni. Ṭī. 1.149). What should be said here regarding the meaning will come later in the commentary on the Mahāparinibbāna Sutta (Dī. Ni. Aṭṭha. 2.171). The Blessed Ones, the Buddhas, are greatly compassionate and, being devoted to providing for the welfare and happiness of beings, are for the most part joyful. Thus it is said in the commentaries that they take rebirth-linking with the first great resultant consciousness (Dī. Ni. Aṭṭha. 2.17; Dha. Sa. Aṭṭha. 498; Ma. Ni. Aṭṭha. 4.200). The Elder Mahāsiva, however, says that although the Blessed Ones, the Buddhas, are greatly compassionate and devoted to providing for the welfare and happiness of beings, they are inclined toward seclusion, tend towards the unconditioned, and are largely equanimous towards all formations; therefore, he asserts that their rebirth-linking is taken by the fifth great resultant consciousness.

Pure puṇṇamāya sattamadivasato paṭṭhāyāti puṇṇamāya pure sattamadivasato paṭṭhāya, sukkapakkhe [V 2.0022] navamito paṭṭhāyāti attho. Sattame divaseti navamito sattame divase āsaḷhipuṇṇamāyaṃ. Idaṃ supinanti idāni vuccamānākāraṃ. Majjhimaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “anotattadahaṃ netvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Atha nesaṃ deviyo āgantvā manussamalaharaṇatthaṃ nhāpetvā”ti [M 2.0025] (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 4.200) vuttaṃ. Tattha nesaṃ deviyoti mahārājūnaṃ deviyo. Caritvāti gocaraṃ caritvā.

“Starting from the seventh day before the full moon” means beginning from the seventh day before the full moon, that is, from the ninth day of the bright fortnight. “On the seventh day” means on the seventh day from the ninth, which is the Āsāḷhī full moon day. “This dream” refers to the one whose nature is now being described. In the Commentary to the Middle-Length Discourses, however, it is said: “Having led her to Lake Anotatta, they stood to one side. Then their consorts came and bathed her to remove any human stain” (MN-a 4.200). There, “their consorts” means the consorts of the great kings. “Having roamed” means having wandered for pasture.

Haritūpalittāyāti haritena gomayena kataparibhaṇḍāya. “So ca kho purisagabbho, na itthigabbho, putto te bhavissatī”ti ettakameva [P 2.0031] te brāhmaṇā attano supinasatthanayena kathesuṃ. “Sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasissatī”tiādi pana devatāviggahena tamatthaṃ yāthāvato pavedesuṃ.

“Smeared with green” means made ready with fresh cow dung. “And that is a male in the womb, not a female; you will have a son”—this much only the brahmins said, in accordance with their science of dreams. However, as to “If he lives the household life,” and so on, the deities, in their own form, revealed its true meaning.

Dhammatāti ettha dhamma-saddo “jātidhammānaṃ bhikkhave sattāna”ntiādīsu (ma. ni. 1.131; 3.373; paṭi. ma. 1.33) viya pakatipariyāyo, dhammo eva dhammatā yathā devo eva devatāti āha “ayaṃ sabhāvo”ti, ayaṃ pakatīti attho. Svāyaṃ sabhāvo atthato tathā niyatabhāvoti āha “ayaṃ niyāmoti vuttaṃ hotī”ti. Niyāmo pana bahuvidhoti te sabbe atthuddhāranayena uddharitvā idhādhippetaniyāmameva dassetuṃ “niyāmo ca nāmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha kammānaṃ niyāmo kammaniyāmo. Esa nayo utuniyāmādīsu tīsu. Itaro pana dhammo eva niyāmo dhammaniyāmo, dhammatā.

Here, in the word dhammatā, the term dhamma is a synonym for nature (pakati), as in such passages as: “Bhikkhus, beings are subject to the nature of birth” (MN I 131, etc.). Dhamma itself is dhammatā (nature), just as deva (deity) is devatā (divinity); hence it is said, “This is its intrinsic nature,” meaning, this is its nature. Since that intrinsic nature is, in meaning, a state that is fixed in such a way, it is said, “This is called the fixed order.” But since the fixed order is of many kinds, in order to show only the fixed order intended here after having drawn out all the meanings by the method of extracting the meaning, it is said, “The fixed order, namely…,” and so on. Among them, the fixed order of kamma is kammaniyāma. The same method applies to the other three, such as the fixed order of seasons. The other one, however, is the fixed order that is Dhamma itself, the dhammaniyāma, dhammatā.

Kusalassa kammassa. Nisento tikhiṇaṃ karonto.

Of wholesome kamma. Sharpening, making keen.

Arūpādibhūmibhāgavisesavasena utuvisesadassanato utuvisesena sijjhamānānaṃ rukkhādīnaṃ pupphaphalādiggahaṇaṃ “tesu tesu janapadesū”ti visesetvā vuttaṃ. Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ kāleti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ vasantādikāle.

The taking of flowers, fruits, etc., from trees, etc., which are brought to fruition by specific seasons, is stated with the specification “in those various regions” because specific seasons are seen according to the specific divisions of the planes of existence, such as the formless plane. “At that particular time” means at that particular season, such as spring.

Madhurato bījato tittato bījatoti yojanā.

“From a sweet seed,” “from a bitter seed”—this is how it should be construed.

18. Vattamānasamīpe vattamāne viya voharitabbanti “okkamatī”ti vuttanti āha “okkanto hotīti ayamevattho”ti. Evaṃ hotīti evaṃ vuttappakārenassa sampajānanā hoti. Na okkamamāne paṭisandhikkhaṇassa duviññeyyatāya. Yathā ca vuttaṃ “paṭisandhicittaṃ na jānātī”ti. Dasasahassacakkavāḷapattharaṇena [P 2.0032] vā appamāṇo. Ativiya samujjalanabhāvena uḷāro[V 2.0023]. Devānubhāvanti devānaṃ pabhānubhāvaṃ. Devānañhi pabhaṃ so obhāso [M 2.0026] abhibhavati, na tesaṃ ādhipaccaṃ. Tenāha “nivatthavatthassā”tiādi.

18. Because one should speak of what is near the present as if it were the present, the present tense “he descends” is used. Hence it is said: “The meaning is simply that ‘he has descended.’” “It is thus” means that his clear comprehension occurs in the manner described. Not while he is descending, because the moment of rebirth-linking is difficult to discern. And as it was said: “He does not know the rebirth-linking consciousness.” Or it is “immeasurable” because it spreads throughout the ten-thousandfold world-system. It is “magnificent” because of its nature of blazing up exceedingly. “The power of the devas” means the power of the devas’ radiance. For that light surpasses the radiance of the devas, not their sovereignty. Therefore it is said: “of one wearing a garment,” etc.

Lokānaṃ lokadhātūnaṃ antaro vivaro lokantaro, so eva itthiliṅgavasena “lokantarikā”ti vutto. Rukkhagacchādinā kenaci na haññantīti aghā, asambādhā. Tenāha “niccavivaṭā”ti. Asaṃvutāti heṭṭhā, upari ca kenaci na pihitā. Tena vuttaṃ “heṭṭhāpi appatiṭṭhā”ti. Tattha pi-saddena yathā heṭṭhā udakassa pidhāyikā pathavī natthīti asaṃvutā lokantarikā, evaṃ uparipi cakkavāḷesu viya devavimānānaṃ abhāvato asaṃvutā appatiṭṭhāti dasseti. Andhakāro ettha atthīti andhakārā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na jāyati ālokassa abhāvato, na cakkhuno. Tathā hi “tena obhāsena aññamaññaṃ sañjānantī”ti vuttaṃ. Jambudīpe ṭhitamajjhanhikavelāyaṃ pubbavidehavāsīnaṃ atthaṅgamanavasena upaḍḍhaṃ sūriyamaṇḍalaṃ paññāyati, aparagoyānavāsīnaṃ uggamanavasena, evaṃ sesadīpesu pīti āha “ekappahāreneva tīsu dīpesu paññāyantī”ti. Ito aññathā pana dvīsu eva dīpesu ekappahārena paññāyantīti. Ekekāya disāya nava nava yojanasatasahassāni andhakāravidhamanampi imināva nayena daṭṭhabbaṃ. Pabhāya nappahontīti attano pabhāya obhāsituṃ anabhisambhunanti. Yugandharapabbatappamāṇe ākāse vicaraṇato “cakkavāḷapabbatassa vemajjhena vicarantī”ti vuttaṃ.

The opening between the worlds, the world-systems, is the world-interspace (lokantara); this is called lokantarikā in the feminine gender. Because they are not obstructed by anything such as trees or bushes, they are spacious (aghā), unconfined (asambādhā). Hence it is said they are “always open” (niccavivaṭā). They are “unenclosed” (asaṃvutā) because they are not covered by anything below or above. Therefore it is said: “unsupported also from below” (heṭṭhāpi appatiṭṭhā). Here the particle pi shows that just as the world-interspace is unenclosed below because there is no earth to contain the water, so too it is unenclosed and unsupported above because of the absence of celestial mansions as there are on the Cakkavāḷa mountains. There is darkness here, so they are called the “darknesses” (andhakārā). Eye-consciousness does not arise for lack of light, not for lack of the eye organ. For it is said: “By that light they recognize one another.” When it is midday in Jambudīpa, half the sun’s disc appears to the inhabitants of Pubbavideha as it is setting, and to the inhabitants of Aparagoyāna as it is rising; similarly in the other continents. Thus it is said: “They appear in three continents at a single stroke.” Alternatively, they appear in only two continents at a single stroke. The dispelling of darkness for nine hundred thousand yojanas in each direction should be understood in the same way. “They are not able with their radiance” means they are unable to illuminate with their own radiance. Because they travel in a space the size of the Yugandhara mountain, it is said: “They travel through the middle of the Cakkavāḷa mountain.”

Vāvaṭāti [P 2.0033] khādanatthaṃ gaṇhituṃ upakkamantā. Viparivattitvāti vivattitvā. Chijjitvāti mucchāpattiyā ṭhitaṭṭhānato muccitvā, aṅgapaccaṅgachedanena vā chijjitvā. Accantakhāreti ātapasantāpābhāvena atisītabhāvameva sandhāya accantakhāratā vuttā siyā. Na hi taṃ kappasaṇṭhahanaudakaṃ sampattikaramahāmeghavuṭṭhaṃ pathavisandhārakaṃ kappavināsakaṃ udakaṃ viya khāraṃ bhavituṃ arahati. Tathā hi sati pathavīpi vilīyeyya, tesaṃ vā pāpakammabalena petānaṃ udakassa pubbakheḷabhāvāpatti viya tassa udakassa tadā khārabhāvāpatti hotīti vuttaṃ “accantakhāre udake”ti.

“Engaged” means approaching to take it for the purpose of eating. “Having turned over” means having rolled over. “Being cut off” means being released from the place where one stood after having fallen into a faint, or being cut off by the severing of one’s limbs great and small. “Extremely caustic”: the extreme causticity might be spoken of with reference to the state of being excessively cold due to the absence of heat and torment. For that water should not be caustic like the world-contracting water, which is rained down by the great cloud that brings fortune, which supports the earth, and which destroys the eon. For if it were so, the earth itself would dissolve. Or, for those petas, by the power of their evil kamma, that water becomes caustic just as what was formerly water became spittle for them. Thus it is said: “in the extremely caustic water.”

Ekayāgupānamattampīti pattādibhājanagataṃ yāguṃ gaḷociādiuddharaṇiyā gahetvā pivanamattampi kālaṃ. Samantatoti sabbabhāgato chappakārampi.

“Even for the time it takes to drink a single portion of gruel” means for the time it takes to drink a portion of gruel from a bowl or other vessel, having taken it up with a ladle or the like. “From all around” means from all parts, in all six ways.

19. Catunnaṃ [M 2.0027] mahārājānaṃ vasenāti vessavaṇādicatumahārājabhāvasāmaññena.

19. “By the authority of the four great kings” refers to the common state of being the four great kings, beginning with Vessavaṇa.

Yathāvihāranti [V 2.0024] yathāsakaṃ vihāraṃ.

“According to their abiding” means to their own respective abodes.

20. Pakatiyāti attano pakatiyā eva. Tenāha “sabhāvenevā”ti. Parassa santike gahaṇena vinā attano sabhāveneva sayameva adhiṭṭhahitvā sīlasampannā. Bodhisattamātāpīti amhākaṃ bodhisattamātāpi. Kāladevilassāti yathā kāladevilassa santike aññadā gaṇhāti, bodhisatte pana…pe… sayameva sīlaṃ aggahesi, tathā vipassībodhisattamātāpīti adhippāyo.

20. “By nature” means by her own nature itself. Therefore it is said, “by intrinsic nature itself.” Without having received it from another, by her own intrinsic nature itself, she was established in and endowed with virtue. “The Bodhisatta’s mother” means our Bodhisatta’s mother. “Like Kāladevila” means: just as on another occasion she might receive it from Kāladevila, in the case of the Bodhisatta... she herself undertook the virtue. The meaning is that the mother of the Vipassī Bodhisatta did so similarly.

21. “Manussesū”ti idaṃ pakaticārittavasena vuttaṃ, “manussitthiyā nāma manussapurisesu purisādhippāyacittaṃ uppajjeyyā”ti. Bodhisattassa mātuyā pana devesupi tādisaṃ cittaṃ nuppajjateva. Yathā bodhisattassa ānubhāvena bodhisattamātu purisādhippāyacittaṃ nuppajjati, evaṃ tassa ānubhāveneva sā kenaci purisena anabhibhavanīyāti āha “pādā na vahanti dibbasaṅkhalikā viya bajjhantī”ti.

21. “Among humans”: this is said with regard to natural behavior, that is: “for a human woman, a mind with desire for a human man might arise.” But for the Bodhisatta’s mother, such a mind does not arise even in relation to gods. Just as through the Bodhisatta’s power a mind with desire for a man does not arise in the Bodhisatta’s mother, so too, by that same power, she cannot be overcome by any man. Hence it is said: “her feet do not carry her, as if bound by divine fetters.”

22. Pubbe [P 2.0034] “kāmaguṇūpasaṃhitaṃ cittaṃ nuppajjatī”ti vuttaṃ, puna “pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricāretī”ti ca vuttaṃ. Kathamidaṃ aññamaññaṃ na virujjhatīti āha “pubbe”tiādi. Vatthupaṭikkhepoti abrahmacariyavatthupaṭisedho. Tenāha “purisādhippāyavasenā”ti. Ārammaṇapaṭilābhoti rūpādipañcakāmaguṇārammaṇasseva paṭilābho.

22. Earlier it was said, “a mind connected with sensual pleasures does not arise,” and again it was said, “she enjoys herself, furnished and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure.” How is it that these do not contradict each other? To explain this, he says “earlier,” etc. “Rejection of the basis” is the rejection of the basis for unchastity. Therefore it is said, “by way of a mind intent on a man.” “Acquisition of the object” is the acquisition of the object of the five cords of sensual pleasure, such as forms, etc.

23. Kilamathoti khedo, kāyassa garubhāvakathinabhāvādayopi tassā tadā na honti eva. “Tirokucchigataṃ passatī”ti vuttaṃ. Kadā paṭṭhāya passatīti āha “kalalādikālaṃ atikkamitvā”tiādi. Dassane payojanaṃ sayameva vadati. Tassa abhāvato kalalādikāle na passati. Puttena daharena mandena uttānaseyyakena saddhiṃ. “Yaṃ taṃ mātū”tiādi pakaticārittavasena vuttaṃ. Cakkavattigabbhatopi hi savisesaṃ bodhisattagabbho parihāraṃ labhati puññasambhārassa sātisayattā, tasmā bodhisattamātā ativiya sappāyāhārācārā ca hutvā sakkaccaṃ pariharati. Sukhavāsatthanti bodhisattassa sukhavāsatthaṃ. Puratthābhimukhoti mātu [M 2.0028] purimabhāgābhimukho. Idāni tirokucchigatassa dissamānatāya abbhantaraṃ, bāhirañca kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ “pubbe katakamma”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Assāti deviyā. Vatthunti kucchiṃ. Phalikaabbhapaṭalādino viya bodhisattamātukucchitacassa patanubhāvena ālokassa vibandhābhāvato yathā bodhisattamātā kucchigataṃ bodhisattaṃ passati, kiṃ evaṃ bodhisattopi mātaraṃ, aññañca purato ṭhitaṃ rūpagataṃ passati, noti āha “bodhisatto panā”tiādi. Kasmā [V 2.0025] pana sati cakkhumhi, āloke ca na passatīti āha “na hi antokucchiyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppajjatī”ti. Assāsapassāsā viya hi tattha cakkhuviññāṇampi na uppajjati tajjassa samannāhārassa abhāvato.

23. “Weariness” means fatigue. At that time, heaviness, stiffness, etc., of the body do not occur for her at all. It is said: “She sees him who is within the womb.” From when does she see? He says: “Having passed beyond the kalala stage,” etc. He himself states the purpose in seeing. Due to the absence of this, she does not see during the kalala stage. With the tender, delicate child lying on its back. “That which is the mother's,” etc., is said with regard to natural behavior. Indeed, the Bodhisatta in the womb receives more special care than one destined to be a wheel-turning monarch because of the excellence of his accumulation of merit. Therefore, the Bodhisatta’s mother, being extremely careful about suitable food and conduct, tends to him respectfully. “For the sake of a comfortable abiding” means for the Bodhisatta’s comfortable abiding. “Facing the front” means facing the mother’s front part. Now, to show the internal and external reason for the visibility of the one within the womb, it is said: “past kamma done previously,” etc. “Of her” (`assā`) means of the queen. “The basis” (`vatthuṃ`) means the womb. Just as there is no obstruction of light because of the thinness of a crystal or a sheet of mica, so because of the thinness of the skin of the Bodhisatta's mother's belly, she sees the Bodhisatta within her womb. Does the Bodhisatta likewise see his mother and other forms standing in front? No. To explain this, he says: “But the Bodhisatta,” etc. But why, when there is the eye and light, does he not see? He says: “For eye-consciousness does not arise inside the womb.” For just as in-breathing and out-breathing do not occur there, so too eye-consciousness does not arise due to the absence of the appropriate attention.

24. Yathā [P 2.0035] aññā itthiyo vijātappaccayā tādisena rogena abhibhūtāpi hutvā maranti, bodhisattamātu pana bodhisatte kucchigate tassa vijāyananimittaṃ, na koci rogo uppajjati, kevalaṃ āyuparikkhayeneva kālaṃ karoti, svāyamattho heṭṭhā vutto eva. “Bodhisattena vasitaṭṭhānañhī”tiādi tassa kāraṇavacanaṃ. Aññesaṃ aparibhoganti aññehi na paribhuñjitabbaṃ, na paribhogayogyanti attho. Tathā sati bodhisattapitu aññāya aggamahesiyā bhavitabbaṃ, tathāpi bodhisattamātari dharantiyā ayujjamānakanti āha “na ca sakkā”tiādi. Apanetvāti aggamahesiṭhānato nīharitvā. Attani chandarāgavaseneva bahiddhā ārammaṇapariyesanāti visayinisārāgo sattānaṃ visayesu sārāgassa balavakāraṇanti dassento āha “sattānaṃ attabhāve chandarāgo balavā hotī”ti. Anurakkhituṃ na sakkotīti sammā gabbhaparihāraṃ nānuyuñjati. Tena gabbho bahvābādho hoti. Vatthu visadaṃ hotīti gabbhāsayo visuddho hoti. Mātu majjhimavayassa tatiyakoṭṭhāse bodhisattagabbhokkamanampi tassā āyuparimāṇavilokaneneva saṅgahitaṃ vayovasena uppajjanakavikārassa parivajjanato. Itthisabhāvena uppajjanakavikāro pana bodhisattassa ānubhāveneva vūpasamati.

24. Just as other women, being overwhelmed by such an illness on account of childbirth, may even die, for the Bodhisatta’s mother, when the Bodhisatta is in her womb, no illness arises on account of his birth. She passes away only from the exhaustion of her lifespan—this meaning has already been stated below. 'For it is a place inhabited by a Bodhisatta,' etc., is the statement of the reason for this. 'Not for the use of others' means it should not be used by others; the meaning is that it is not fit for use. This being so, the Bodhisatta’s father should have another chief queen, yet it is said, 'and it is not possible,' etc., because it is unsuitable while the Bodhisatta’s mother is living. 'Having removed her' means having taken her from the position of chief queen. The seeking of external objects is due to sensual lust for oneself. To show that lust for sense objects is a powerful cause for beings' lust in regard to sense objects, he says: 'Beings have strong sensual lust for their own existence.' 'She is not able to protect it' means she does not properly apply herself to the care of the womb. Because of that, the fetus is subject to many afflictions. 'The basis becomes clear' means the womb becomes pure. The Bodhisatta’s descent into the womb during the third portion of the mother’s middle age is also included by way of examining the measure of her lifespan, because of the avoidance of the deterioration that arises due to age. But any deterioration arising from her female nature is pacified by the Bodhisatta’s power.

25. Sattamāsajātoti paṭisandhiggahaṇato sattame māse jāto. So sītuṇhakkhamo na hoti ativiya sukhumālatāya. Aṭṭhamāsajāto [M 2.0029] kāmaṃ sattamāsajātato buddhivayavā, ekacce pana cammapadesā vuddhiṃ pāpuṇantā ghaṭṭanaṃ na sahanti, tena so na jīvati. “Sattamāsajātassa pana na tāva te jātā”ti vadanti.

25. 'Born in the seventh month' means born in the seventh month from conception. He is not tolerant of cold and heat because of his extreme delicacy. One born in the eighth month, though more developed in intelligence than one born in the seventh month, has certain areas of skin that, while developing, cannot endure contact, and for that reason he does not live. They say: 'But for one born in the seventh month, these have not yet arisen.'

27. Devā [P 2.0036] paṭhamaṃ paṭiggaṇhantīti “lokanāthaṃ mahāpurisaṃ sayameva paṭhamaṃ paṭiggaṇhāmā”ti sañjātagāravabahumānā attano pītiṃ pavedentā khīṇāsavā suddhāvāsabrahmāno ādito paṭiggaṇhanti. Sūtivesanti sūtijagganadhātivesaṃ. Eketi abhayagirivāsino. Macchakkhisadisaṃ chavivasena. Aṭṭhāsi na nisīdi, na nipajji vā. Tena vuttaṃ “ṭhitāva bodhisattaṃ bodhisattamātā vijāyatī”ti. Niddukkhatāya ṭhitā eva hutvā vijāyati. Dukkhassa hi balavabhāvato taṃ dukkhaṃ asahamānā aññā itthiyo nisinnā vā nipannā vā vijāyanti.

27. 'The devas receive him first': With reverence and great esteem that has arisen, thinking, 'We ourselves will be the first to receive the great being, the protector of the world,' the brahmās of the Pure Abodes, whose taints are destroyed, expressing their joy, receive him first from the start. She stood; she did not sit or lie down. Therefore it is said: 'Standing, the Bodhisatta’s mother gives birth to the Bodhisatta.' She gives birth standing because she is without pain. For other women, unable to endure the pain because of its intensity, give birth either sitting or lying down.

28. Ajinappaveṇiyāti [V 2.0026] ajinacammehi sibbitvā katapaveṇiyā. Mahātejoti mahānubhāvo. Mahāyasoti mahāparivāro, vipulakittighoso ca.

28. 'By a deerskin robe' (`ajinappaveṇiyā`) means by a robe made by sewing together deerskins. 'Of great majesty' (`mahātejo`) means of great power. 'Of great fame' (`mahāyaso`) means having a great retinue and widespread fame and glory.

29. Bhaggavibhaggāti sambādhaṭṭhānato nikkhamanena vibhāvitattā bhaggā, vibhaggā viya ca hutvā, tena nesaṃ avisadabhāvameva dasseti. Alaggo hutvāti gabbhāsaye, yonipadese ca katthaci alaggo asatto hutvā, yato “dhamakaraṇato udakanikkhamanasadisa”nti vuttaṃ. Udakenāti gabbhāsayagatena udakena. Amakkhitova nikkhamati sammakkhitassa tādisassa udakasemhādikasseva tattha abhāvato. Bodhisattassa hi puññānubhāvato paṭisandhiggahaṇato paṭṭhāya taṃ ṭhānaṃ pubbepi visuddhaṃ visesato paramasugandhagandhakuṭi viya candanagandhaṃ vāyantaṃ tiṭṭhati.

29. 'Broken and scattered': because they are manifested by exiting from a confined space, they are broken, and as if scattered; thus this shows their lack of clarity. 'Being unattached' means being unattached, unclinging, anywhere in the womb or in the birth canal, for which reason it is said, 'like the flowing of water from a water filter.' 'With water' means with the water that is in the womb. He emerges unsoiled because of the absence there of any such water, phlegm, and the like that would soil him. For, through the power of the Bodhisatta’s merit, from the time of conception onwards that place, already pure, remains especially so, like a supreme, fragrant, perfumed chamber, emitting the scent of sandalwood.

Udakavaṭṭiyoti udakakkhandhā.

'Streams of water' means masses of water.

31. Muhuttajātoti muhuttena jāto hutvā muhuttamattova. Anudhāriyamāneti [P 2.0037] anukūlavasena nīyamāne. Āgatānevāti taṃ ṭhānaṃ upagatāni eva. Anekasākhanti ratanamayānekasatapatiṭṭhānahīrakaṃ. Sahassamaṇḍalanti tesaṃ upariṭṭhitaṃ anekasahassamaṇḍalahīrakaṃ. Marūti devā. Na kho pana evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ padavītihārato pageva disāvilokanassa [M 2.0030] katattā. Tenāha “mahāsatto hī”tiādi. Ekaṅgaṇānīti vivaṭabhāvena vihāraṅgaṇapariveṇaṅgaṇāni viya ekaṅgaṇasadisāni ahesuṃ. Sadisopi natthīti tumhākaṃ idaṃ vilokanaṃ visiṭṭhe passituṃ “idha tumhehi sadisopi natthi, kuto uttaritaro”ti āhaṃsu. Aggoti padhāno, kena panassa padhānatāti āha “guṇehī”ti. Paṭhama-saddo cettha padhānapariyāyo. Bodhisattassa pana padhānatā anaññasādhāraṇāti āha “sabbapaṭhamo”ti, sabbapadhānoti attho. Etassevāti aggasaddasseva. Ettha ca mahesakkhā tāva devā tathā ca vadanti, itare pana kathanti? Mahāsattassa ānubhāvadassanādinā. Mahesakkhānañhi devānaṃ mahāsattassa ānubhāvo viya tena sadisānampi ānubhāvo paccakkho ahosīti, itare pana tesaṃ vacanaṃ sutvā saddahantā anuminantā tathā āhaṃsu. Paripākagatapubbahetusaṃsiddhāya dhammatāya codiyamāno imasmiṃ…pe… byākāsi.

31. 'Just born' means having been born in a moment, just a moment old. 'Being held up' means being carried in a favorable way. 'Just arrived' means having come to that very place. 'With many branches' means a jeweled canopy with hundreds of pedestals. 'With a thousand circles' means a canopy with thousands of circles set above them. 'The Maruts' means devas. But this should not be understood in this way, because the surveying of the directions was done before the taking of the steps. Therefore it is said: 'For the great being,' etc. 'As a single courtyard': because of being open, they were like a single courtyard, similar to the courtyards of monasteries and their precincts. 'There is no one similar': They said, 'Here there is no one similar to you, whence one superior?' so that he would see that he is the most distinguished in this regard. 'Foremost' means chief. But by what is he chief? He says: 'by virtues.' Here the word 'first' is a synonym for 'chief.' But the Bodhisatta's chieftainship is unique, so he says 'first of all,' which means 'chief of all.' 'Of this very one' means of the very word 'foremost.' And here, the devas of great power speak thus, but how do the others speak? Through seeing the great being's power, etc. For the devas of great power, the power of the great being was as directly perceptible as the power of those similar to him. But the others, hearing their words, believed and inferred, and so they spoke. Prompted by the natural law perfected by a previous cause that had reached maturity, in this... he declared...

Jātamattasseva bodhisattassa ṭhānādīni yesaṃ visesādhigamānaṃ pubbanimittabhūtānīti te niddhāretvā dassento “ettha cā”tiādimāha. Tattha patiṭṭhānaṃ caturiddhipādapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ iddhipādavasena lokuttaradhammesu suppatiṭṭhitabhāvasamijjhanato. Uttarābhimukhabhāvo [P 2.0038] lokassa [V 2.0027] uttaraṇavasena gamanassa pubbanimittaṃ. Tena hi bhagavā sadevakassa lokassa abhibhūto, kenaci anabhibhūto ahosi. Tenāha “mahājanaṃ ajjhottharitvā abhibhavitvā gamanassa pubbanimitta”nti. Tathā sattapadagamanaṃ sattapadabojjhaṅgasampannaariyamaggagamanassa. Suvisuddhasetacchattadhāraṇaṃ suvisuddhavimuttichattadhāraṇassa. Pañcarājakakudhabhaṇḍasamāyogo pañcavidhavimuttiguṇasamāyogassa. Anāvaṭadisānuvilokanaṃ anāvaṭañāṇatāya. “Aggohamasmī”tiādinā achambhitavācābhāsanaṃ kenaci avibandhanīyatāya appavattiyassa saddhammacakkappavattanassa. “Ayamantimā jātī”ti āyatiṃ jātiyā abhāvakittanā anupādi…pe… pubbanimittanti veditabbaṃ tassa tassa anāgate laddhabbavisesassa taṃ taṃ nimittaṃ abyabhicārīti katvā. Na āgatoti imasmiṃ sutte, aññattha ca vakkhamānāya anupubbiyā na āgato. Āharitvāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sutte, aṭṭhakathāsu ca āgatanayena āharitvā dīpetabbo.

To show that the Bodhisatta’s standing and so on, immediately upon birth, were precursory signs of the special attainments he would gain, the text begins, 'Here also,' and so on. In this context, the firm standing is a precursory sign of the attainment of the four bases of psychic power, because through the bases of psychic power success is achieved in being well-established in the supramundane states. The facing towards the north is a precursory sign of going beyond the world by way of transcending it. For the Blessed One, having overcome the world with its devas, was himself unovercome by anyone. Hence it is said: 'It is a precursory sign of his going forth, having covered over and overcome the great populace.' Similarly, the taking of seven steps is a precursory sign of traversing the noble path endowed with the seven factors of enlightenment. The holding of the perfectly pure white parasol is a precursory sign of holding the parasol of perfectly pure liberation. The presence of the five royal insignia is a precursory sign of the possession of the five kinds of qualities of liberation. The surveying of the directions without obstruction is a precursory sign of his unobstructed knowledge. The fearless utterance, 'I am the chief,' and so on, is a precursory sign of the turning of the irreversible Wheel of the True Dhamma, which cannot be hindered by anyone. The proclamation, 'This is my last birth,' a declaration of the future absence of birth, is a precursory sign of... [the state] without residue... and so on, it should be understood, because each sign is an infallible indicator of the specific distinction to be attained in the future. 'Not found': it is not found in this sutta, nor elsewhere in the sequential exposition to be mentioned. 'Brought forth': it should be explained by bringing forth the method found in the respective suttas and commentaries.

“Dasasahassilokadhātu [M 2.0031] kampī”ti idaṃ satipi idha pāḷiyaṃ āgatatte vakkhamānānaṃ acchariyānaṃ mūlabhūtaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ, evaṃ aññampi evarūpaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tantibaddhā vīṇā cammabaddhā bheriyoti pañcaṅgikatūriyassa nidassanamattaṃ, ca-saddena vā itaresampi saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. “Andubandhanādīni taṅkhaṇe eva chajjitvā puna pākatikāneva honti, tathā jaccandhādīnaṃ cakkhusotādīni tathārūpakammapaccayā tasmiṃyeva khaṇe uppajjitvā tāvadeva vigacchantī”ti vadanti. Chijjiṃsūti ca pādesu bandhaṭṭhānesu chijjiṃsu. Vigacchiṃsūti vūpasamiṃsu. Ākāsaṭṭhakaratanāni nāma taṃtaṃvimānagatamaṇiratanādīni. Sakatejobhāsitānīti [P 2.0039] ativiya samujjalāya attano pabhāya obhāsitāni ahesuṃ. Nappavattīti na sannipāto. Na vāyīti kharo vāto na vāyi. Mudusukho pana sattānaṃ sukhāvaho vāyi. Pathavigatā ahesuṃ uccaṭṭhāne ṭhātuṃ avisahantā. Utusampannoti anuṇhāsītatāsaṅkhātena utunā sampanno. Apphoṭanaṃ vuccati bhujahatthasaṅghaṭṭanasaddo, atthato pana vāmahatthaṃ ure ṭhapetvā dakkhiṇena puthupāṇinā hatthatāḷanena saddakaraṇaṃ. Mukhena usseḷanaṃ saddassa muñcanaṃ seḷanaṃ. Ekaddhajamālā ahosi nirantaraṃ dhajamālāsamodhānagatāya. Na kevalañca etāni eva, atha kho aññānipi “vicittapupphasugandhapupphavassadevopavassi sūriye dissamāne eva tārakā obhāsiṃsu, acchaṃ vippasannaṃ udakaṃ pathavito ubbhijji, bilāsayā ca tiracchānā āsayato nikkhamiṃsu, rāgadosamohāpi tanu bhaviṃsu, pathaviyaṃ rajo vūpasami, aniṭṭhagandho vigacchi, dibbagandho vāyi, rūpino devā sarūpeneva manussānaṃ āpāthaṃ agamaṃsu, sattānaṃ cutūpapātā nāhesu”nti evamādīni [V 2.0028] yāni mahābhinīhārasamaye uppannāni dvattiṃsapubbanimittāni, tāni anavasesato tadā ahesunti.

'The ten-thousandfold world system trembled': this is stated, even though it is found here in the Pāli, to show the basis of the wonders to be described. Similarly, other such instances should be understood. 'Lutes bound with strings, drums bound with hide': this is an example of the five-limbed orchestra. Or by the word 'and,' the inclusion of the others should be understood. They say: 'Shackles and fetters were severed at that very moment and then became normal again; similarly, the eyes, ears, and so on, of those blind from birth arose at that very moment due to the condition of such kamma, and then vanished just as quickly.' 'Were severed' means they were severed at the places of binding on the feet. 'Vanished' means they subsided. 'Jewels suspended in the sky' means the various gems and jewels in their respective celestial mansions. 'Shining with their own radiance' means they were illuminated by their own exceedingly brilliant light. 'Did not proceed' means there was no gathering. 'Did not blow' means a harsh wind did not blow; but a soft, pleasant wind, bringing happiness to beings, did blow. They went to the ground, being unable to stand in high places. 'Endowed with the season' means endowed with a season characterized by neither heat nor cold. 'Snapping the fingers' is said to be the sound of striking the arms and hands together; but in meaning, it is making a sound by placing the left hand on the chest and clapping with the flat of the right hand. 'Shouting with the mouth' is releasing a sound, a cry. There was a single garland of banners because of the continuous arrangement of banner-garlands. Not only these, but also the other thirty-two precursory signs that arose at the time of the great aspiration appeared completely then, such as: 'A rain of variegated and fragrant flowers fell from the sky; stars shone even while the sun was visible; clear, limpid water gushed up from the earth; animals in lairs and burrows came out from their dwellings; lust, hatred, and delusion diminished; dust on the earth subsided; unpleasant odors vanished; a divine fragrance wafted; devas with form appeared in their own forms within the range of human vision; and there was no passing away or rebirth of beings.'

Tatrāpīti tesupi pathavikampādīsu evaṃ pubbanimittabhāvo veditabbo. Na kevalaṃ sampatijātassa ṭhānādīsu evāti adhippāyo. Sabbaññutaññāṇapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ sabbassa ñeyyassa, titthakaramatassa ca cālanato. Kenaci anussāhitānaṃyeva imasmiṃyeva ekacakkavāḷe sannipāto kenaci anussāhitānaṃyeva ekappahāreneva [P 2.0040] sannipatitvā dhammapaṭiggaṇhanassa pubbanimittaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ devatānaṃ paṭiggahaṇaṃ dibbavihārapaṭilābhassa, pacchā manussānaṃ paṭiggahaṇaṃ tattheva ṭhānassa niccalasabhāvato [M 2.0032] āneñjavihārapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ. Vīṇānaṃ sayaṃ vajjanaṃ parūpadesena vinā sayameva anupubbavihārapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ. Bherīnaṃ vajjanaṃ cakkavāḷapariyantāya parisāya pavedanasamatthassa dhammabheriyā anusāvanassa amatadundubhighosanassa pubbanimittaṃ. Andubandhanādīnaṃ chedo mānavinibandhabhedanassa pubbanimittaṃ. Mahājanassa rogavigamo tasseva sakalavaṭṭadukkharogavigamabhūtassa saccapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ. “Mahājanassā”ti padaṃ “mahājanassa dibbacakkhupaṭilābhassa, mahājanassa dibbasotadhātupaṭilābhassā”tiādinā tattha tattha ānetvā sambandhitabbaṃ. Iddhipādabhāvanāvasena sātisayañāṇajavasampattisiddhīti āha “pīṭhasappīnaṃ javasampadā caturiddhipādapaṭilābhassa pubbanimitta”nti. Supaṭṭanasampāpuṇanaṃ catupaṭisambhidādhigamassa pubbanimittaṃ. Atthādianurūpaṃ atthādīsu sampaṭipattibhāvato. Ratanānaṃ sakatejobhāsitattaṃ yaṃ lokassa dhammobhāsaṃ dassessati, tena tassa sakatejobhāsitattassa pubbanimittaṃ.

And there too: thus, in regard to the earth-trembling and so on, their nature as precursory signs should be understood. The meaning is: not only in regard to the standing and so on of the one just born. It is a precursory sign of the attainment of the knowledge of omniscience because it shakes all that is knowable and the doctrines of the sectarians. The gathering in this single world-system of those who are unprompted by anyone is a precursory sign of their gathering together at a single stroke, though unprompted by anyone, to receive the Dhamma. First, the reception by the devas is a precursory sign of the attainment of the divine abodes; afterwards, the reception by humans, because of the immovable nature of that very place, is a precursory sign of the attainment of the imperturbable abode. The spontaneous sounding of the lutes, without instruction from another, is a precursory sign of the attainment of the successive abodes by himself alone. The sounding of the drums is a precursory sign of the proclamation of the Dhamma-drum, of the sounding of the drum of the deathless, capable of making it known to the assembly extending to the limits of the world-system. The severing of shackles and fetters is a precursory sign of the breaking of the bonds of conceit. The departure of disease from the great populace is a precursory sign of the attainment of the truth, which is the very departure of the disease of suffering in the entire round of existence. The phrase 'of the great populace' should be brought in and connected in each case, as in: 'of the attainment of the divine eye by the great populace, of the attainment of the divine ear-element by the great populace,' and so on. Because the accomplishment of swiftness of knowledge and extraordinary power is achieved through the development of the bases of psychic power, it is said: 'The swiftness of cripples is a precursory sign of the attainment of the four bases of psychic power.' The attainment of a good foundation is a precursory sign of the attainment of the four analytical knowledges, because of the state of correct practice in regard to meaning, etc., in conformity with meaning, etc. The shining of the jewels with their own radiance is a precursory sign of his own shining with radiance when he shows the world the light of the Dhamma.

Catubrahmavihārapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ tassa sabbaso veravūpasamanato. Ekādasaagginibbāpanassa pubbanimittaṃ dunnibbāpananibbānabhāvato. Ñāṇālokādassanassa pubbanimittaṃ anāloke ālokadassanabhāvato. Nibbānarasenāti kilesānaṃ nibbāyanarasena. Ekarasabhāvassāti sāsanassa sabbattha ekarasabhāvassa, tañca kho amadhurassa [P 2.0041] lokassa sabbaso madhurabhāvāpādanena. Dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhigatabhindanassa pubbanimittaṃ sabbaso diṭṭhigatavātāpanayanavasena. Ākāsādiappatiṭṭhavisamacañcalaṭṭhānaṃ pahāya sakuṇānaṃ pathavigamanaṃ tādisaṃ micchāgāhaṃ pahāya sattānaṃ pāṇehi ratanattayasaraṇagamanassa pubbanittaṃ. Bahujanakantatāyāti candassa viya bahujanassa kantatāya. Sūriyassa uṇhasītavivajjitautusukhatā pariḷāhavivajjitakāyikacetasikasukhappattiyā pubbanimittaṃ. Devatānaṃ apphoṭanādīhi kīḷanaṃ pamoduppatti bhavantagamanena, dhammasabhāvabodhanena ca udānavasena pamodavibhāvanassa pubbanimittaṃ. Dhammavegavassanassāti desanāñāṇavegena dhammāmatassa vassanassa [V 2.0029] pubbanimittaṃ. Kāyagatāsativasena laddhaṃ jhānaṃ pādakaṃ katvā uppāditamaggaphalasukhānubhavo kāyagatāsatiamatapaṭilābho, tassa pana kāyassāpi atappakasukhāvahattā khudāpipāsāpīḷanābhāvo pubbanimittaṃ vutto[M 2.0033]. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃpana khudaṃ, pipāsañca bhinditvā vuttaṃ. Tattha pubbanimittānaṃ bhedo visesasāmaññavibhāgena, gobalībaddañāyena ca gahetabbo. “Sayamevā”ti padaṃ “aṭṭhaṅgikamaggadvāravivaraṇassā”ti etthāpi ānetvā sambandhitabbaṃ. Bharitabhāvassāti paripuṇṇabhāvassa. “Ariyaddhajamālāmālitāyāti kāsāyaddhajamālāvantatāyā”ti keci, sadevakassa lokassa pana ariyamaggabojjhaṅgaddhajamālāhi mālibhāvassa pubbanimittaṃ. Yaṃ panettha anuddhaṭaṃ, taṃ suviññeyyameva.

It is a precursory sign of the attainment of the four divine abodes because of the complete pacification of all enmity. It is a precursory sign of the extinguishing of the eleven fires because of its nature of extinguishing what is difficult to extinguish. It is a precursory sign of seeing the light of knowledge because of the seeing of light where there is no light. 'With the taste of Nibbāna' means with the taste that extinguishes the defilements. 'Of the state of a single taste' means of the state of the teaching having a single taste everywhere, and this by making the unsweet world entirely sweet. It is a precursory sign of the shattering of the sixty-two kinds of wrong views by way of completely removing the winds of wrong views. The going of birds to the earth, having abandoned their unsupported, uneven, and unsteady place in the sky, is a precursory sign of beings abandoning such wrong graspings and going for refuge with their lives to the Triple Gem. 'Because of being dear to the multitude' means because of being dear to the multitude like the moon. The sun's comfort of a season devoid of heat and cold is a precursory sign of the attainment of bodily and mental happiness devoid of torment. The devas' playing by snapping their fingers and so on is a precursory sign of the manifestation of joy by way of an inspired utterance, because of the arising of gladness through reaching the end of existence and through awakening to the nature of the Dhamma. 'Of the raining with the force of the Dhamma' is a precursory sign of the raining of the deathless Dhamma with the force of the knowledge of teaching. The experiencing of the happiness of the path and fruition, produced by making the jhāna attained through mindfulness directed to the body its basis, is the attainment of the deathless through mindfulness directed to the body; the absence of affliction by hunger and thirst is said to be a precursory sign of this, because it brings effortless happiness even to the body. But in the commentary, it is stated by analyzing 'hunger' and 'thirst' separately. Herein, the distinction among the precursory signs should be understood by the division into specific and general, and by the maxim of the ox and the bull. The word 'by itself' should be brought in and connected here too with 'of the opening of the door of the eightfold path.' 'Of the state of being filled' means of the state of being complete. 'Of being wreathed with the garland of the noble banner' means, according to some, 'of possessing the garland of the ochre-robe banner'; but it is a precursory sign of the world with its devas being wreathed with the garlands of the banners of the noble path and the factors of enlightenment. Whatever herein has not been cited is easy to understand.

Etthāti “sampatijāto”tiādinā āgate imasmiṃ vāre. Vissajjitova, tasmā amhehi idha apubbaṃ vattabbaṃ natthīti adhippāyo. Tadā [P 2.0042] pathaviyaṃ gacchantopi mahāsatto ākāsena gacchanto viya mahājanassa tathā upaṭṭhāsīti ayamettha niyati dhammaniyāmo bodhisattānaṃ dhammatā ti idaṃ niyativādavasena kathanaṃ. Pubbe purimajātīsu tādisassa puññasambhārakammassa katattā upacitattā mahājanassa tathā upaṭṭhāsīti idaṃ pubbekatakammavādavasena kathanaṃ. Imesaṃ sattānaṃ upari īsanasīlatāya yathāsakaṃ kammameva issaro nāma, tassa nimmānaṃ attano phalassa nibbattanaṃ mahāpurisopi sadevakaṃ lokaṃ abhibhavituṃ samatthena uḷārena puññakammena nibbattito, tena issarena nimmito nāma, tassa cāyaṃ nimmānaviseso, yadidaṃ mahānubhāvatā, yāya mahājanassa tathā upaṭṭhāsīti idaṃ issaranimmānavasena kathanaṃ. Evaṃ taṃ taṃ bahulaṃ vatvā kiṃ imāya pariyāyakathāyāti avasāne ujukameva byākari. Sampatijāto pathaviyaṃ kathaṃ padasā gacchati, evaṃ mahānubhāvo ākāsena maññe gacchatīti parikappanavasena ākāsena gacchanto viya ahosi. Sīghataraṃ pana sattapadavītihārena gatattā dissamānarūpopi mahājanassa adissamāno viya ahosi. Acelakabhāvo, khuddakasarīratā ca tādisassa iriyāpathassa na anucchavikāti kammānubhāvasañjanitapāṭihāriyavasena alaṅkatapaṭiyatto viya, soḷasavassuddesiko viya ca mahājanassa upaṭṭhāsīti veditabbaṃ. Mahāsattassa puññānubhāvena tadā tathā upaṭṭhānamattamevetanti. Pacchā bāladārakova ahosi, na tādisoti. Buddhabhāvānucchavikassa bodhisattānubhāvassa yāthāvato paveditattā parisā cassa byākaraṇena buddhena viya…pe… attamanā ahosi.

Here, in this section that has come up beginning with ‘just born.’ It has already been explained; therefore, the intention is that there is nothing new for us to say here. At that time, though the Great Being was walking on the earth, he appeared to the great multitude as if he were walking through the sky. This here is a fixed law, a natural principle, the nature of bodhisattas—this is a statement in terms of the doctrine of determinism. Because in the past, in former births, he had performed and accumulated such a store of meritorious kamma, he appeared thus to the great multitude—this is a statement in terms of the doctrine of past kamma. For these beings, because of its nature of ruling over them, their own kamma is the lord. Its creation is the production of its own fruit. The Great Man, too, was produced by lofty meritorious kamma capable of overcoming the world with its devas. Thus he is said to be created by that lord, and this special creation of his is this great power by which he appeared thus to the great multitude—this is a statement in terms of the doctrine of creation by a lord. Having spoken thus at length on this and that, what is the use of this roundabout talk? At the end, he explained it directly. ‘How does one just born walk on the earth with his feet? Being so powerful, I think he walks through the sky.’ Thus, by way of conjecture, he was as if walking through the sky. But because he went more quickly with his seven-step stride, though his form was visible, he was as if invisible to the great multitude. It should be understood that because his nakedness and small body were unsuitable for such a posture, by way of a miracle produced by the power of his kamma, he appeared to the great multitude as if adorned and arrayed, like a youth of sixteen years. It was merely an appearance at that time due to the power of the Great Being’s merit. Afterwards, he was just a young child, not like that. Because the power of the Bodhisatta, befitting his future Buddhahood, was truly explained, the assembly was gratified by his explanation as if by the Buddha… and so on… and was delighted.

Sabbadhammatāti [V 2.0030][M 2.0034] sabbā soḷasavidhāpi yathāvuttā dhammatā [P 2.0043] sabbabodhisattānaṃ hontīti veditabbā puññañāṇasambhāradassanena nesaṃ ekasadisattā.

‘All natures’ means that it should be understood that all sixteen kinds of natures, as mentioned, are found in all bodhisattas, because they are seen to be identical in their accumulation of merit and knowledge.

Dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇavaṇṇanā

An Exposition of the Thirty-Two Marks of a Great Man

33. Dukūlacumbaṭaketi daharassa nipajjanayogyatāvasena paṭisaṃhaṭadukūlasukhume. “Khattiyo brāhmaṇo”ti evamādi jāti. “Koṇḍañño gotamo”ti evamādi gottaṃ. “Poṇikā cikkhallikā sākiyā koḷiyā”ti evamādi kulapadeso. Ādi-saddena rūpissariyaparivārādisabbasampattiyo saṅgaṇhāti. Mahantassāti vipulassa, uḷārassāti attho. Nipphattiyoti siddhiyo. Gantabbagatiyāti gati-saddassa kammasādhanatamāha. Upapajjanavasena hi sucaritaduccaritehi gantabbāti gatiyo, upapattibhavaviseso. Gacchati yathāruci pavattatīti gati, ajjhāsayo. Paṭisaraṇeti parāyaṇe avassaye. Sabbasaṅkhatavisaṃyuttassa hi arahato nibbānameva taṃpaṭisaraṇaṃ. Tyāhanti te ahaṃ.

33. ‘A roll of fine cloth’ means a fine, soft cloth folded to be suitable for a young child to lie on. ‘Khattiya, brahmin,’ and so on is birth. ‘Koṇḍañña, Gotama,’ and so on is clan. ‘Poṇikā, Cikkhallikā, Sākiyā, Koḷiyā,’ and so on is the family line. By the word ‘and so on,’ it includes all accomplishments such as beauty, sovereignty, and retinue. ‘Of a great one’ means of a vast one; the meaning is of a lofty one. ‘Accomplishments’ means successes. ‘A destination to be gone to’: this states that the word ‘gati’ is an instrumental noun of action. For destinations are to be gone to by means of good and bad conduct, in the sense of taking rebirth; they are particular states of existence through rebirth. ‘One goes,’ one proceeds according to one’s inclination; this is ‘gati,’ disposition. ‘Refuge’ means final resort, support. For an arahant, who is disjoined from all conditioned things, Nibbāna alone is that refuge. ‘Tyāhaṃ’ is `te ahaṃ`.

Dasavidhe kusaladhamme, agarahite ca rājadhamme (jā. 2 mahāmaṃsajātake vitthāro) niyuttoti dhammiko. Tena ca dhammena sakalaṃ lokaṃ rañjetīti dhammarājā. Yasmā cakkavattī dhammena ñāyena rajjaṃ adhigacchati, na adhammena, tasmā vuttaṃ “dhammena laddharajjattā dhammarājā”ti. Catūsu disāsu samuddapariyosānatāya caturantā nāma tattha tattha dīpe mahāpathavīti āha “puratthima…pe… issaro”ti. Vijitāvīti vijetabbassa vijitavā, kāmakodhādikassa abbhantarassa, paṭirājabhūtassa bāhirassa ca arigaṇassa vijayi, vijetvā ṭhitoti attho. Kāmaṃ cakkavattino kenaci yuddhaṃ nāma natthi, yuddhena pana sādhetabbassa vijayassa siddhiyā “vijitasaṅgāmo”ti vuttaṃ. Janapadova catubbidhaacchariyadhammādisamannāgate asmiṃ rājini thāvariyaṃ kenaci asaṃhāriyaṃ daḷhaṃ bhattabhāvaṃ patto, janapade [P 2.0044] vā attano dhammikāya paṭipattiyā thāvariyaṃ thirabhāvaṃ pattoti janapadatthāvariyappatto. Manussānaṃ ure satthaṃ ṭhapetvā icchitadhanaharaṇādinā parasāhasakāritāya sāhasikā.

He is engaged in the ten kinds of wholesome states and in the blameless royal duties (detailed in the Mahāmaṃsa Jātaka, Ja 2); thus he is righteous. And because he delights the entire world with that Dhamma, he is a Dhamma-king. Since a wheel-turning monarch gains his kingdom by Dhamma, by principle, not by what is not Dhamma, it is therefore said: ‘Because his kingdom was gained by Dhamma, he is a Dhamma-king.’ Because it ends at the ocean in the four directions, the great earth with its continents is called ‘four-ended.’ Hence he says: ‘of the eastern… and so on… lord.’ ‘A conqueror’ means he has conquered what is to be conquered; the meaning is that he is victorious over the inner host of enemies such as lust and anger, and over the outer host of enemies, the rival kings; he stands having conquered. It is true that a wheel-turning monarch has no war with anyone, but because the victory that would have to be won by war is accomplished, he is called ‘victorious in battle.’ The country, endowed with the four marvelous qualities and so on, has attained under this king a firm state of allegiance, a stability that cannot be shaken by anyone; or, he has attained stability, a firm state, in the country through his own righteous conduct; thus he has ‘attained a stable country.’ ‘Violent men’ are those who act with violence towards others, for instance by placing a sword on people’s chests and forcibly taking their desired wealth.

Ratijananaṭṭhenāti atappakapītisomanassuppādanena. Saddatthato pana rametīti ratanaṃ. “Aho manohara”nti citte kattabbatāya cittīkataṃ[M 2.0035]. “Svāyaṃ cittīkāro tassa pūjanīyatāyā”ti cittīkatanti pūjanīyanti atthaṃ vadanti. Mahantaṃ vipulaṃ aparimitaṃ mūlaṃ agghatīti mahagghaṃ. Natthi etassa tulā upamāti atulaṃ, asadisaṃ. Kadāci eva uppajjanato dukkhena laddhabbattā [V 2.0031] dullabhadassanaṃ. Anomehi uḷāraguṇeheva sattehi paribhuñjitabbato anomasattaparibhogaṃ. Idāni nesaṃ cittīkatādiatthānaṃ savisesaṃ cakkaratane labbhamānataṃ dassetvā itaresupi te atidisituṃ “cakkaratanassa cā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Aññaṃ devaṭṭhānaṃ nāma na hoti rañño anaññasādhāraṇissariyādisampattipaṭilābhahetuto, sattānañca yathicchitatthapaṭilābhahetuto. Aggho natthi ativiya uḷārasamujjalasattaratanamayattā, acchariyabbhutamahānubhāvatāya ca. Yadaggena mahagghaṃ, tadaggena atulaṃ. Sattānaṃ pāpajigucchanena vigatakāḷako puññapasutatāya maṇḍabhūto yādiso kālo buddhuppādāraho, tādise eva cakkavattīnampi sambhavoti āha “yasmā ca panā”tiādi. Upamāvasena cetaṃ vuttaṃ, upamopameyyānañca na accantameva sadisatā. Tasmā yathā buddhā kadāci karahaci uppajjanti, na tathā cakkavattino, evaṃ santepi cakkavattivattaparipūraṇassāpi dukkarabhāvatopi dullabhuppādāyevāti[P 2.0045], iminā dullabhuppādatāsāmaññena tesaṃ dullabhadassanatā vuttāti veditabbaṃ. Kāmaṃ cakkaratanānubhāvena sijjhamāno guṇo cakkavattiparivārasādhāraṇo, tathāpi “cakkavattī eva naṃ sāmibhāvena visavitāya paribhuñjatī”ti vattabbataṃ arahati tadatthaṃ uppajjanatoti dassento “tadeta”ntiādimāha. Yathāvuttānaṃ pañcannaṃ, channampi vā atthānaṃ itararatanesupi labbhanato “evaṃ sesānipī”ti vuttaṃ. Hatthiassa-pariṇāyakaratanehi ajitavijayato, cakkaratanena ca parivārabhāvena, sesehi paribhogūpakaraṇabhāvena samannāgato. Hatthiassamaṇiitthiratanehi paribhogūpakaraṇabhāvena sesehi parivārabhāvenāti yojanā.

‘In the sense of producing delight’ means by producing insatiable joy, zest, and mental happiness. In terms of the literal meaning, ‘it delights’ (rameti), thus it is a ‘treasure’ (ratana). ‘Oh, how captivating!’—because it should be made so in the mind, it is ‘esteemed’ (cittīkata). ‘This esteem is due to its being worthy of veneration’; thus they say the meaning of ‘esteemed’ is ‘worthy of veneration.’ It is worth a great, vast, immeasurable price; thus it is ‘of great price’ (mahaggha). There is no measure or comparison for it; thus it is ‘immeasurable’ (atula), incomparable. Because it arises only sometimes and is obtained with difficulty, it is ‘rare to see’ (dullabhadassana). Because it is to be enjoyed by beings with faultless, lofty qualities, it is for ‘the enjoyment of faultless beings’ (anomasattaparibhoga). Now, having shown that these meanings—such as being esteemed—are found with special distinction in the wheel-treasure, in order to extend them to the others, the text begins, ‘And of the wheel-treasure….’ There is no other divine station, because it is the cause for the king to obtain sovereignty and other accomplishments not shared by others, and because it is the cause for beings to obtain their desired aims. It is priceless because it is made of the seven treasures, which are exceedingly sublime and radiant, and because of its marvelous, great power. In the same way that it is of great price, it is also immeasurable. Just as a time is suitable for the arising of a Buddha when beings, through their loathing of evil, are free from stain and, through their devotion to merit, have become the essence of purity, so too is such a time suitable for the arising of wheel-turning monarchs.
