Hence it is said, “internally,” and so on. `Rūpajjhāna` (form-jhāna) becomes `rūpa` (form) by elision of the latter part of the compound. Here in `rūpāni` (forms), however, the elision of the former part of the compound should be understood. Therefore, it is said, “forms such as the blue kasiṇa,” etc. Perception of form in the kasiṇa-form is “form-perception.” One who possesses this is “one with form-perception,” and the jhāna is spoken of with perception as the principal factor. By its negation, one is “one without form-perception.” Hence it is said, “internally not perceiving form,” and so on.

“Anto appanāyaṃ subhanti ābhogo natthī”ti iminā pubbābhogavasena tathā adhimutti siyāti dasseti. Evañhettha tathāvattabbatāpatticodanā samatthitā hoti. Yasmā suvisuddhesu nīlādīsu vaṇṇakasiṇesu tattha katādhikārānaṃ abhirativasena suṭṭhu adhimuccanaṭṭho sambhavati[M 2.0119], tasmā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ tathā tatiyo vimokkho saṃvaṇṇito, yasmā pana mettāvasena pavattamānā bhāvanā satte appaṭikūlato dahanti tesu tato adhimuccitvāva pavattati, tasmā paṭisambhidāmagge (paṭi. ma. 212) “brahmavihārabhāvanā subhavimokkho”ti vuttā, tayidaṃ ubhayampi tena tena pariyāyena vuttattā na virujjhatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

By the statement, “In the internal absorption, there is no advertence ‘beautiful,’” he shows that such a conviction might arise by way of prior advertence. Thus, the charge of having to speak in such a way is supported here. Because in the perfectly pure blue and other color kasiṇas, for those who have made their aspiration in them, a strong sense of conviction can arise by way of delight, therefore the third liberation is described in that way in the commentary. And because the meditation that proceeds by way of loving-kindness establishes beings as non-repulsive and proceeds by resolving upon them, therefore in the Paṭisambhidāmagga (Paṭi. Ma. 212), it is said: “The development of the divine abodes is the liberation through the beautiful.” Since both of these are stated in their respective ways, they should be understood as not contradictory.

Sabbasoti anavasesato. Na hi catunnaṃ arūpakkhandhānaṃ ekadesopi tattha avassissati. Visuddhattāti yathāparicchinnakāle nirodhitattā. Uttamo vimokkho nāma ariyeheva samāpajjitabbato, ariyaphalapariyosānattā diṭṭheva dhamme nibbānappattibhāvato ca.

“Completely” (sabbaso) means without remainder. For not even a portion of the four immaterial aggregates will remain there. “Because of purity” (visuddhattā) means because of having been ceased at the determined time. It is called the supreme liberation because it is to be attained only by the noble ones, because it culminates in the noble fruits, and because it is the state of having attained Nibbāna in this very life.

130. Ādito paṭṭhāyāti paṭhamasamāpattito paṭṭhāya. Yāva pariyosānā samāpatti, tāva. Aṭṭhatvāti katthaci samāpattiyaṃ aṭṭhito eva, nirantarameva paṭipāṭiyā, uppaṭipāṭiyā ca samāpajjatevāti attho. Tenāha “ito cito ca sañcaraṇavasena vutta”nti. Icchati samāpajjituṃ. Tattha “samāpajjati pavisatī”ti samāpattisamaṅgīpuggalo taṃ taṃ paviṭṭho viya hotīti katvā vuttaṃ.

130. “From the beginning” means beginning from the first attainment, up to the final attainment. “Being established” means that, being established in any attainment, one enters continuously in forward order and in reverse order; this is the meaning. Hence it is said, “This is stated by way of moving about from here to there.” He wishes to enter into attainment. There, “he enters into attainment” (samāpajjati) means “he enters” (pavisati), and it is said because the person endowed with the attainment is as if entered into that particular attainment.

Dvīhi [V 2.0106] bhāgehi vimuttoti arūpajjhānena vikkhambhanavimokkhena, maggena samucchedavimokkhenāti dvīhi vimuccanabhāgehi, arūpasamāpattiyā rūpakāyato, maggena nāmakāyatoti dvīhi vimuccitabbabhāgehi ca vimutto. Tenāha “arūpasamāpattiyā”tiādi[P 2.0155]. Vimuttoti hi kilesehi vimutto, vimuccanto ca kilesānaṃ vikkhambhanasamucchindanehi kāyadvayato vimuttoti ayamettha attho. Gāthāya ca ākiñcaññāyatanalābhino upasivabrāhmaṇassa bhagavatā “nāmakāyā vimutto”ti ubhatobhāgavimutto muni akkhāto. Tattha atthaṃ paletīti atthaṃ gacchati. Na upeti saṅkhanti “asukaṃ nāma disaṃ gato”ti vohāraṃ na gacchati. Evaṃ muni nāmakāyā vimuttoti evaṃ arūpaṃ upapanno sekkhamuni pakatiyā pubbeva rūpakāyā vimutto, tattha ca catutthamaggaṃ nibbattetvā nāmakāyassa pariññātattā puna nāmakāyāpi vimutto. Ubhatobhāgavimutto khīṇāsavo hutvā anupādāya parinibbānasaṅkhātaṃ [M 2.0120] atthaṃ paleti na upeti saṅkhaṃ, “khattiyo brāhmaṇo”ti evaṃ ādikaṃ samaññaṃ na gacchatīti attho.

“Liberated in two parts” means: by the formless absorption through suppression-liberation, and by the path through eradication-liberation—thus, by two parts of liberation. By the formless attainment, one is liberated from the form-body; by the path, from the name-body—thus, one is liberated from two parts from which to be liberated. Therefore, it is said, “by the formless attainment,” and so on. “Liberated” means freed from defilements, and in being liberated, one is freed from the two bodies through the suppression and eradication of defilements—this is the meaning here. And in the verse, the Blessed One declared the brahmin Upasiva, an attainer of the base of nothingness, as “liberated from the name-body”—thus, the sage is declared as liberated in both parts. There, “he goes to the goal” means he reaches the goal. “He does not come to reckoning” means he does not enter into conventional speech such as “he has gone to such-and-such a direction.” “Thus, the sage is liberated from the name-body” means: thus, having attained the formless realm, the trainee sage is naturally already liberated from the form-body. And there, having generated the fourth path, because the name-body has been fully understood, he is also liberated from the name-body. The one liberated in both parts, having become one whose cankers are destroyed, goes to the goal called final Nibbāna without clinging. He does not come to reckoning, meaning he does not enter into designations such as “a warrior, a brahmin,” and so on.

“Aññatarato vuṭṭhāyā”ti idaṃ kiṃ ākāsānañcāyatanādīsu aññataralābhīvasena vuttaṃ, udāhu sabbāruppalābhīvasenāti yathicchasi, tathā hotu, yadi sabbāruppalābhīvasena vuttaṃ, na koci virodho. Atha tattha aññataralābhīvasena vuttaṃ, “yato kho, ānanda, bhikkhu ime aṭṭha vimokkhe anulomampi samāpajjatī”tiādivacanena virujjheyyāti? Yasmā arūpāvacarajjhānesu ekassāpi lābhī “aṭṭhavimokkhalābhī” tveva vuccati aṭṭhavimokkhe ekadesassāpi taṃnāmadānasamatthatāsambhavato. Ayañhi aṭṭhavimokkhasamaññā samudāye viya tadekadesepi niruḷhāpattisamaññā viyāti. Tena vuttaṃ “ākāsānañcāyatanādīsu aññatarato vuṭṭhāyā”ti. “Pañcavidho hotī”ti vatvā chabbidhataṃpissa keci parikappenti, taṃ tesaṃ matimattaṃ, nicchitovāyaṃ pañho pubbācariyehīti dassetuṃ “keci panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha kecīti uttaravihāravāsino, sārasamāsācariyā ca. Te hi “ubhatobhāgavimuttoti [P 2.0156] ubhayabhāgavimutto samādhivipassanāto”ti vatvā rūpāvacarasamādhināpi samādhiparipanthato vimuttiṃ maññanti. Evaṃ rūpajjhānabhāgena, arūpajjhānabhāgena ca ubhato vimuttoti pāyasamāno. “Tādisamevā”ti iminā yādisaṃ arūpāvacarajjhānaṃ kilesavikkhambhane, tādisaṃ rūpāvacaracatutthajjhānaṃ pīti imamatthaṃ ullaṅgeti. Tenāha “tasmā”tiādi.

“Having emerged from one of them”—is this said with reference to one who has attained any of the formless attainments beginning with the base of infinite space, or with reference to one who has attained all of them? Let it be as you wish. If it is said with reference to one who has attained all of them, there is no contradiction. But if it is said with reference to one who has attained any of them, would it not conflict with the statement, “When, Ānanda, a bhikkhu enters these eight liberations in forward order...”? Because even one who has attained just one of the formless-sphere jhānas is called “one who has attained the eight liberations,” since it is possible for that name to be given even to a part of the eight liberations. For this designation “eight liberations” is established for a part of it just as for the whole, like the designation “offense.” Therefore, it is said, “having emerged from one of them, such as the base of infinite space.” Having stated that it is “fivefold,” some propose it as sixfold. That is merely their opinion. To show that this question has been definitively settled by the ancient teachers, it is said, “but some say...” and so on. Here, “some” refers to the dwellers of the Uttaravihāra and the teachers of the Sārasamāsa. They, having said, “one liberated in both parts is liberated from the two parts of concentration and insight,” consider that even by form-sphere concentration there is liberation from the obstacles to concentration. Thus, it is comparable to being liberated in both ways by a part of form-jhāna and a part of formless-jhāna. By “just like that,” it indicates this meaning: just as the formless-sphere jhāna is for the suppression of defilements, so too is the fourth form-sphere jhāna. Therefore, it is said, “for this reason...” and so on.

Ubhatobhāgavimuttapañhoti ubhatobhāgavimuttassa chabbidhataṃ nissāya uppannapañho. Vaṇṇanaṃ nissāyāti tassa padassa atthavacanaṃ nissāya. Cirenāti therassa aparabhāge cirena kālena. Vinicchayanti [V 2.0107] saṃsayachedakaṃ sanniṭṭhānaṃ patto. Taṃ pañhanti tamatthaṃ. Ñātuṃ icchito hi attho pañho. Na kenaci sutapubbanti kenaci kiñci na sutapubbaṃ, idaṃ atthajātanti adhippāyo. Kiñcāpi upekkhāsahagataṃ, kiñcāpi kilese vikkhambhetīti paccekaṃ kiñcāpi-saddo yojetabbo. Samudācaratīti pavattati. Tattha kāraṇamāha “ime hī”tiādinā, tena rūpāvacarabhāvanato āruppabhāvanā savisesaṃ kilese vikkhambheti rūpavirāgabhāvanābhāvato[M 2.0121], uparibhāvanābhāvato cāti dassetīti. Evañca katvā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ āruppabhāvanāniddese yaṃ vuttaṃ “tassevaṃ tasmiṃ nimitte punappunaṃ cittaṃ cārentassa nīvaraṇāni vikkhambhanti sati santiṭṭhatī”tiādi, (visuddhi. 1.281) taṃ samatthataṃ hotīti. Idaṃ suttanti puggalapaññattipāṭhamāha (pu. pa. niddesa 27). Sabbañhi buddhavacanaṃ atthasūcanādiatthena suttanti vutto vāyamattho. Yaṃ pana tattha [P 2.0157] vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Aṭṭhannaṃ vimokkhānaṃ anulomādito samāpajjanena sātisayaṃ santānassa abhisaṅkhatattā, aṭṭhamañca uttamaṃ vimokkhaṃ padaṭṭhānaṃ katvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā aggamaggādhigamena ubhatobhāgavimuccanato ca imāya ubhatobhāgavimuttiyā sabbaseṭṭhatā veditāti daṭṭhabbā.

The question concerning one liberated in both parts is a question that arises based on the sixfold classification of one liberated in both parts. ‘Based on the explanation’ means relying on the statement of meaning of that term. ‘After a long time’ means after a long period in the elder’s later life. A decision is the reaching of a conclusion that cuts off doubt. ‘That question’ means that matter, for a question is a matter one desires to know. ‘Never heard before by anyone’ means that nothing of this kind of meaning had ever been heard before by anyone—this is the intended meaning. ‘Although accompanied by equanimity,’ ‘although it suppresses defileles’—the word ‘although’ should be applied separately to each. ‘It occurs’ means it proceeds. There, the reason is stated with ‘for these,’ and so on. By this it is shown that the formless meditative development suppresses defilements with special distinction compared to the form meditative development, because of the absence of the development of dispassion for form and because of the absence of a higher development. And so, what is said in the commentary in the exposition of formless meditative development—“For one who repeatedly directs the mind toward that sign, the hindrances are suppressed, mindfulness is established,” and so on (Vism. 1.281)—is thereby supported. ‘This discourse’ refers to the text of the Puggalapaññatti (Pug. Pa. Niddesa 27). Indeed, all the Buddha’s words are called a ‘discourse’ in the sense of indicating meaning, and so on; or this meaning is so called. As for what should be said there, that has already been stated below. It should be understood that the supreme excellence of this liberation in both parts is due to the mental continuum being pre-eminently conditioned by attaining the eight liberations in forward order, and due to liberation in both parts through the attainment of the supreme path by developing insight, having made the eighth and ultimate liberation the foundation.

Mahānidānasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā.

The Elucidation of the Hidden Meaning in the Commentary on the Great Discourse on Causation.

3. Mahāparinibbānasuttavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Mahāparinibbāna Sutta

131. Pūjanīyabhāvato[V 2.0108][M 2.0122], [P 2.0158] buddhasampadañca pahāya pavattatā mahantañca taṃ parinibbānañcāti mahāparinibbānaṃ; savāsanappahānato mahantaṃ kilesakkhayaṃ nissāya pavattaṃ parinibbānantipi mahāparinibbānaṃ; mahatā kālena mahatā vā guṇarāsinā sādhitaṃ parinibbānantipi mahāparinibbānaṃ; mahantabhāvāya, dhātūnaṃ bahubhāvāya parinibbānantipi mahāparinibbānaṃ; mahato lokato nissaṭaṃ parinibbānantipi mahāparinibbānaṃ; sabbalokāsādhāraṇattā buddhānaṃ sīlādiguṇehi mahato buddhassa bhagavato parinibbānantipi mahāparinibbānaṃ; mahati sāsane patiṭṭhite parinibbānantipi mahāparinibbānanti buddhassa bhagavato parinibbānaṃ vuccati, tappaṭisaṃyuttaṃ suttaṃ mahāparinibbānasuttaṃ. Gijjhā ettha vasantīti gijjhaṃ, gijjhaṃ kūṭaṃ etassāti gijjhakūṭo, gijjhaṃ viya vā gijjhaṃ, kūṭaṃ, taṃ etassāti gijjhakūṭo, pabbato, tasmiṃ gijjhakūṭe. Tenāha “gijjhā”tiādi. Abhiyātukāmoti ettha abhi-saddo abhibhavanattho, “abhivijānātū”tiādīsu (dī. ni. 2.244; 3.85; ma. ni. 3.256) viyāti āha “abhibhavanatthāya yātukāmo”ti. Vajjirājānoti “vajjetabbā ime”tiādito pavattaṃ vacanaṃ upādāya “vajjī”ti laddhanāmā rājāno, vajjīraṭṭhassa vā rājāno vajjirājāno. Vajjiraṭṭhassa pana vajjisamaññā tannivāsirājakumāravasena veditabbā. Rājiddhiyāti rājabhāvānugatena sabhāvena. So pana sabhāvo nesaṃ [P 2.0159] gaṇarājūnaṃ mitho sāmaggiyā loke pākaṭo, ciraṭṭhāyī ca ahosīti “samaggabhāvaṃ kathesī”ti vuttaṃ. Anu anu taṃsamaṅgino bhāveti vaḍḍhetīti anubhāvo, anubhāvo eva ānubhāvo, patāpo, so pana nesaṃ patāpo hatthiassādivāhanasampattiyā, tattha ca susikkhitabhāvena loke pākaṭo jātoti “etena…pe… kathesī”ti vuttaṃ. Tāḷacchiggalenāti kuñcikāchiddena. Asananti saraṃ. Atipātayissantīti atikkāmenti. Poṅkhānupoṅkhanti poṅkhassa anupoṅkhaṃ, purimasarassa poṅkhapadānugatapoṅkhaṃ itaraṃ saraṃ katvāti attho. Avirādhitanti avirajjhitaṃ. Ucchindissāmīti ummūlanavasena kulasantatiṃ chindissāmi. Ayanaṃ [V 2.0109] vaḍḍhanaṃ ayo, tappaṭikkhepena anayoti āha “avaḍḍhiyā etaṃ nāma”nti. Vikkhipatīti vidūrato khipati, apanetīti attho.

131. Because of its venerability, and because it occurs after relinquishing the perfection of Buddhahood, and because that final Nibbāna is great, it is called the Great Final Nibbāna. Because it occurs relying on the great destruction of defilements through the abandonment of all latent tendencies, it is also called the Great Final Nibbāna. Because it is accomplished over a long time or through a great accumulation of virtues, it is also called the Great Final Nibbāna. Because of its greatness and the abundance of relics, it is also called the Great Final Nibbāna. Because it is the departure from the great world, it is also called the Great Final Nibbāna. Because the virtues of morality and so forth of the Buddhas are uncommon to the entire world, the final Nibbāna of the Blessed One, the great Buddha, is also called the Great Final Nibbāna. Because it occurs after the great Dispensation has been established, it is also called the Great Final Nibbāna. Thus, the final Nibbāna of the Blessed Buddha is called the Great Final Nibbāna, and the discourse connected with it is called the Mahāparinibbāna Sutta. Here, vultures dwell, hence it is called Gijjha (vulture). The peak where vultures dwell is called Gijjhakūṭa (Vulture’s Peak). Or, because it resembles a vulture, it is a peak, hence it is called Gijjhakūṭa—the mountain. Therefore, it is said, ‘Gijjha,’ etc. ‘Desiring to conquer’—here the prefix ‘abhi’ means overcoming, as in ‘may he fully understand,’ etc. Thus, it is said, ‘desiring to go to overcome.’ ‘The Vajjian kings’—because they are called ‘Vajjī’ from the statement, ‘these should be avoided,’ etc., they are kings who acquired the name ‘Vajjī.’ Or, they are the kings of the Vajjian country. The designation ‘Vajjī’ for the Vajjian country should be understood as referring to the princes dwelling in that region. ‘By royal majesty’—by the inherent nature of kingship. This inherent nature of theirs, the unity among the ruling chiefs, was evident in the world and long-lasting. Thus, it is said, ‘he spoke of their unity.’ ‘Power’—‘anubhāvo’ means that which develops and increases those who are endowed with it, step by step. ‘Anubhāvo’ is indeed ‘ānubhāvo,’ splendor. This splendor of theirs was evident in the world due to their wealth of elephants, horses, and vehicles, and because they were well-trained in them. Thus, it is said, ‘he spoke of this…etc.’ ‘Through a keyhole’—with a keyhole. ‘Arrows’—missiles. ‘They will shoot past’—they will surpass. ‘One arrow after another’—the meaning is, making one arrow follow the nock-position of the previous arrow’s nock. ‘Without missing’—unharmed. ‘I will annihilate’—I will cut off the family line by uprooting them. ‘Decline’—‘ayo’ is growth; ‘anayo’ is its opposite. Thus, it is said, ‘this is called non-growth.’ ‘He scatters’—he throws far away, removes—this is the meaning.

Gaṅgāyanti [M 2.0123] gaṅgāsamīpe. Paṭṭanagāmanti sakaṭapaṭṭanagāmaṃ. Āṇāti āṇā vattati. Aḍḍhayojananti ca tasmiṃ paṭṭane aḍḍhayojanaṭṭhānavāsino sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tatrāti tasmiṃ paṭṭane. Balavāghātajātoti uppannabalavakodho.

‘Gaṅgāyaṃ’ means near the Ganges. ‘Paṭṭanagāma’ refers to a cart-market town. ‘Āṇā’ means the command prevails. ‘Half a yojana’ refers to those dwelling at a distance of half a yojana in that market town. ‘There’ means in that market town. ‘For whom a violent affliction has arisen’ means for whom intense anger has arisen.

Meti mayhaṃ. Gatenāti gamanena.

‘Me’ means ‘my’. ‘Gatena’ means by the going.

Rājaaparihāniyadhammavaṇṇanā

Exposition on the Principles of a King's Non-Decline

134. Sītaṃ vā uṇhaṃ vā natthi, tāyaṃ velāyaṃ puññānubhāvena buddhānaṃ sabbakālaṃ samasītuṇhāva utu hoti, taṃ sandhāya tathā vuttaṃ. Abhiṇhaṃ sannipātāti niccasannipātā, taṃ pana niccasannipātataṃ dassetuṃ “divasassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sannipātabahulāti pacurasannipātā. Vosānanti saṅkocaṃ. “Yāvakīva”nti ekamevetaṃ padaṃ aniyamato parimāṇavācī, kālo cettha adhippetoti āha “yattakaṃ kāla”nti. “Vuddhiyevā”tiādinā vuttamatthaṃ byatirekamukhena [P 2.0160] dassetuṃ “abhiṇhaṃ asannipatantā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ākulāti khubhitā, na pasannā. Bhijjitvāti vaggabandhato vibhajja visuṃ visuṃ hutvā.

134. “There is neither cold nor heat”: By the power of merit, the weather for the Buddhas is always evenly temperate at all times; it was said thus with reference to that. “Frequent assemblies” means constant gatherings. To show this constancy of gathering, “of the day” and so on was said. “Abundant assemblies” means numerous gatherings. “Vosāna” means shrinkage. “Yāvakīva” is a single term indicating an indefinite quantity; time is intended here, thus it is said, “for whatever time.” To show the meaning stated by “only growth” and so on, by way of contrast, “if they do not assemble frequently” and so on was said. “Ākulā” means agitated, not serene. “Bhijjitvā” means having been divided from their group bond, having become separate and distinct.

Sannipātabheriyāti sannipātārocanabheriyā. Aḍḍhabhuttā vāti sāmibhuttā ca. Osīdamāneti hāyamāne.

“Sannipātabheriyā” means the drum for announcing an assembly. “Aḍḍhabhuttā vā” means and eaten by the master. “Osīdamāne” means deteriorating.

Pubbe akatanti pubbe anibbattaṃ. Suṅkanti bhaṇḍaṃ gahetvā gacchantehi pabbatakhaṇḍa nadītitthagāmadvārādīsu rājapurisānaṃ dātabbabhāgaṃ. Balinti nipphannasassādito chabhāgaṃ, sattabhāgantiādinā laddhakaraṃ. Daṇḍanti dasavīsatikahāpaṇādikaṃ aparādhānurūpaṃ gahetabbadhanadaṇḍaṃ. Vajjidhammanti vajjirājadhammaṃ. Idāni apaññattapaññāpanādīsu tappaṭikkhepa ādīnavānisaṃse vitthārato dassetuṃ “tesaṃ apaññatta”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Pāricariyakkhamāti upaṭṭhānakkhamā.

“Previously unmade” means previously unproduced. “Suṅka” means the portion to be given to royal officials at mountain passes, river fords, village gates, etc., by those carrying goods. “Bali” means the tax obtained as one-sixth, one-seventh, etc., of the harvested crops. “Daṇḍa” means a monetary fine to be taken according to the offense, such as ten or twenty kahāpaṇas. “Vajjidhamma” means the law of the Vajjian kings. Now, to explain in detail the dangers and benefits regarding the rejection of those principles such as establishing the unestablished, it was said, “their unestablished,” etc. “Pāricariyakkhamā” means capable of attendance.

Kulabhogaissariyādivasena mahatī mattā pamāṇaṃ etesanti mahāmattā, nītisatthavihite vinicchaye [V 2.0110] ṭhapitā mahāmattā vinicchayamahāmattā, tesaṃ. Dentīti niyyātenti. Sace coroti evaṃsaññino sace honti. Pāpabhīrutāya attanā kiñci avatvā. Daṇḍanītisaññite vohāre niyuttāti vohārikā, ye “dhammaṭṭhā”ti vuccanti. Suttadharā nītisuttadharā[M 2.0124], īdise vohāravinicchaye niyametvā ṭhapitā. Paramparābhatesu aṭṭhasu kulesu jātā agatigamanaviratā aṭṭhamahallakapurisā aṭṭhakulikā.

“Mahāmattā” (great ministers) are those who have a great measure (mattā, pamāṇaṃ) in terms of family, wealth, power, and so on. “Vinicchayamahāmattā” (judicial ministers) are great ministers established in judgments decided according to the science of policy. “Denti” means they deliver. “Sace coro” (if a thief) means if they are perceived as such. Out of fear of evil, without saying anything themselves. “Vohārikā” (legal officers) are those appointed in legal proceedings known as the science of punishment, who are called “Dhammaṭṭhā” (just men). “Suttadharā” means those who hold the policy texts (nītisuttadharā), appointed to regulate such legal decisions. “Aṭṭhakulikā” (the eight clansmen) are eight elder men (aṭṭhamahallakapurisā) born into the eight families that have been continuously handed down through tradition, abstaining from going to wrong destinations.

Sakkāranti upakāraṃ. Garubhāvaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvāti “ime amhākaṃ garuno”ti tattha garubhāvaṃ pati pati upaṭṭhapetvā. Mānentīti sammānenti, taṃ pana sammānanaṃ tesu nesaṃ attamanatāpubbakanti āha “manena piyāyantī”ti. Nipaccakāranti paṇipātaṃ. Dassentīti “ime amhākaṃ pitāmahā[P 2.0161], mātāmahā”tiādinā nīcacittā hutvā garucittākāraṃ dassenti. Sandhāretunti sambandhaṃ avicchinnaṃ katvā ghaṭetuṃ.

“Sakkāra” means help. “Having established reverence” (garubhāvaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvā) means repeatedly establishing reverence in them, [thinking] “These are our revered ones.” “Mānenti” means they honor. That honoring, however, is preceded by their satisfaction in them, thus it is said, “They gladden them in mind.” “Nipaccakāra” means bowing down. “Dassenti” means they show, that is, with a humble mind, displaying the demeanor of reverence, [thinking] “These are our paternal grandfathers, maternal grandfathers,” and so on. “Sandhāretuṃ” means to maintain, that is, to make the connection continuous, to cause it to cohere.

Pasayhākārassāti balakkārassa. Kāmaṃ vuddhiyā pūjanīyatāya “vuddhihāniyo”ti vuttaṃ, attho pana vuttānukkameneva yojetabbo, pāḷiyaṃ vā yasmā “vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti vuttaṃ, tasmā tadanukkamena “vuddhihāniyo”ti vuttaṃ.

“Pasayhākārassa” means of forceful action. Although “growth and decline” (vuddhihāniyo) is said for the sake of growth and venerability, the meaning should be construed in accordance with the order previously stated. Alternatively, since in the Pāli text it is said, “Only growth is to be anticipated, not decline,” therefore “growth and decline” is said following that order.

Vipaccituṃ aladdhokāse pāpakamme, tassa kammassa vipāke vā anavasarova devatopasaggo, tasmiṃ pana laddhokāse siyā devatopasaggassa avasaroti āha “anuppannaṃ…pe… vaḍḍhentī”ti. Eteneva anuppannaṃ sukhanti etthāpi attho veditabbo. “Balakāyassa diguṇatiguṇatādassanaṃ, paṭibhayabhāvadassana”nti evaṃ ādinā devatānaṃ saṅgāmasīse sahāyatā veditabbā.

When an evil deed has not found an opportunity to ripen, or for the result of that deed, affliction by deities is indeed without opportunity. But when an opportunity is obtained, there may be an occasion for affliction by deities, thus it is said, “The unarisen... they increase.” By this same reasoning, the meaning regarding “unarisen happiness” should also be understood here. “Showing the army's strength to be double or triple, showing a fearful appearance”—by such means, the deities’ assistance at the head of the battle should be understood.

Anicchitanti aniṭṭhaṃ. Āvaraṇatoti nisedhanato. Yassa dhammato anapetā dhammiyāti idha “dhammikā”ti vuttā. Migasūkarādighātāya sunakhādīnaṃ kaḍḍhitvā vanacaraṇaṃ vājo, migavā, tattha niyuttā, te vā vājenti nentīti vājikā, migavadhacārino. Cittappavattiṃ pucchati. Kāyikavācasikapayogena hi sā loke pākaṭā pakāsabhūtāti.

“Anicchita” means unwished-for (aniṭṭha). “Āvaraṇato” means by prevention (nisedhanato). Those who have not departed from the Dhamma are here called “dhammikā” (righteous). “Vāja” is the wandering in the forest by dragging dogs, etc., for the killing of deer, boars, etc., that is, hunting (migavā). Those engaged in that are “vājikā” (hunters), deer-slayers. Or, because they drive and lead, they are “vājikā,” followers of deer-slaughter. He asks about the course of thought. For in the world it is clearly manifest through bodily and verbal application, being apparent.

135. Devāyatanabhāvena citattā, lokassa cittīkāraṭṭhānattā ca cetiyaṃ ahosi.

135. Because it was regarded as an abode of deities and a place of veneration for the world, it became a shrine.

Kāmaṃkāravasena kiñcipi na karaṇīyāti akaraṇīyā. Kāmaṃkāro pana hatthagatakaraṇavasenāti [V 2.0111] āha “aggahetabbāti attho”ti. Abhimukhayuddhenāti abhimukhaṃ ujukameva saṅgāmakaraṇena. Upalāpanaṃ [M 2.0125] sāmaṃ dānañcāti dassetuṃ “ala”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Bhedopi idha upāyo evāti vuttaṃ “aññatra mithubhedāyā”ti. Yuddhassa pana anupāyatā [P 2.0162] pageva pakāsitā. Idanti “aññatra upalāpanāya, aññatra mithubhedā”ti ca idaṃ vacanaṃ. Kathāya nayaṃ labhitvāti “yāvakīvañca…pe… no parihānī”ti imāya bhagavato kathāya nayaṃ upāyaṃ labhitvā.

“Akaraṇīyā” means nothing whatsoever is to be done by way of arbitrary will. But “kāmaṃkāra” is by way of seizing control, thus he said, “it means not to be grasped.” “Abhimukhayuddhena” means by engaging directly in battle. To show that conciliation includes gifts, “enough” and so on was said. Division, too, is a means here, thus it is said, “except for causing division.” But that battle is not a proper means has already been declared. “Idaṃ” means this statement: “except for conciliation, except for causing division.” “Having gained a method from the discourse” (kathāya nayaṃ labhitvā) means having obtained a method, a means, from the Blessed One’s discourse: “As long as... no decline.”

Anukampāyāti vajjirājesu anuggahena. Assāti bhagavato.

“Anukampāya” means with favor towards the Vajjian rulers. “Assa” means of the Blessed One.

Kathanti vajjīhi saddhiṃ kātabbayuddhakathaṃ. Ujuṃ karissāmīti paṭirājāno ānetvā pākāraparikhānaṃ aññathābhāvāpādanena ujubhāvaṃ karissāmi.

“Kathā” means the discourse on the war to be waged with the Vajjians. “I will make it straight” (ujuṃ karissāmi) means: I will make them level by bringing in opposing kings and by altering the walls and moats.

Patiṭṭhitaguṇoti patiṭṭhitācariyaguṇo. Issarā sannipatantu, mayaṃ anissarā, tattha gantvā kiṃ karissāmāti licchavino na sannipatiṃsūti yojanā. Sūrā sannipatantūti etthāpi eseva nayo.

“Patiṭṭhitaguṇa” means possessing the qualities of established teachers. The construction (yojanā) is: “Let the powerful assemble; we are powerless, what shall we do there?” Thus, the Licchavis did not assemble. The same method applies to “Let the heroes assemble.”

Balabherinti yuddhāya balakāyassa uṭṭhānabheriṃ.

“Balabheri” means the drum for mustering the army for battle.

Bhikkhuaparihāniyadhammavaṇṇanā

Exposition on the Qualities that Prevent Decline for Bhikkhus

136. Aparihānāya hitāti aparihāniyā, na parihāyanti etehīti vā aparihāniyā, te pana yasmā aparihāniyā kārakā nāma honti, tasmā vuttaṃ “aparihānikare”ti. Yasmā pana te parihānikarānaṃ ujupaṭipakkhabhūtā, tasmā āha “vuddhihetubhūte”ti. Yasmā bhagavato desanā uparūpari ñāṇālokaṃ pasādentī sattānaṃ hadayandhakāraṃ vidhamati, pakāsetabbe ca atthe hatthatale āmalakaṃ viya suṭṭhutaraṃ pākaṭe katvā dasseti, tasmā vuttaṃ “candasahassaṃ…pe… kathayissāmī”ti.

136. Beneficial for non-decline, thus 'aparihāniyā'; or, they do not decline by these, thus 'aparihāniyā'. But because they are indeed called 'makers of non-decline' (aparihāniyā kārakā), therefore it is said, 'conducive to non-decline' (aparihānikare). And because they are directly opposed to those that cause decline, therefore he said, 'causes of growth' (vuddhihetubhūte). Because the Blessed One’s teaching, by progressively illuminating the light of wisdom, dispels the darkness in beings' hearts, and because it makes the meaning to be illuminated very clear, like an amalaka fruit in the palm of the hand, therefore it is said, 'like a thousand moons... I will explain.'

Yasmā bhagavā “tassa brāhmaṇassa sammukhā vajjīnaṃ abhiṇhasannipātādipaṭipattiṃ kathentoyeva ayaṃ aparihāniyakathā aniyyānikā vaṭṭanissitā, mayhaṃ pana sāsane tathārūpī kathā kathetabbā, sā hoti niyyānikā vivaṭṭanissitā, yāya sāsanaṃ mayhaṃ parinibbānato parampi [V 2.0112] addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitika”nti cintesi, tasmā bhikkhū sannipātāpetvā tesaṃ aparihāniye dhamme desento teneva niyāmena desesi. Tena vuttaṃ “idaṃ vajjisattake vuttasadisamevā”ti. Evaṃ saṅkhepato vuttamatthaṃ [M 2.0126] vitthārato dassento “idhāpi cā”tiādimāha. Tattha “tato”tiādi [P 2.0163] disāsu āgatasāsane vuttaṃ taṃ kathanaṃ. Vihārasīmā ākulā yasmā, tasmā uposathapavāraṇā ṭhitā.

Because the Blessed One thought, "While explaining to that brahmin the frequent assemblies and so on of the Vajjis, this talk on non-decline is not leading to liberation, being dependent on the round of rebirth. But in my dispensation, such a talk should be given—one that is leading to liberation, being dependent on turning away from the round, so that my dispensation might be enduring and long-lasting even after my final Nibbāna," he assembled the bhikkhus and taught them these non-decline Dhammas in the same manner. Hence, it is said, "This is similar to what was said regarding the Vajjian heptad." Thus, having briefly stated the meaning, he elaborates further, saying, "Here too..." Herein, "then" refers to that teaching given when the dispensation had spread in all directions. Because the monastery boundaries were disordered, the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā were established.

Olīyamānakoti pāḷito, atthato ca vinassamāno. Ukkhipāpentāti paguṇabhāvakaraṇena, atthasaṃvaṇṇanena ca paggaṇhantā.

“Olīyamānako” means disappearing from the text and in meaning. “Ukkhipāpenti” means they uphold it by making it proficient and by elaborating on the meaning.

Sāvatthiyaṃ bhikkhū viya pācittiyaṃ desāpetabboti (pārā. 565 vitthāravatthu). Vajjiputtakā viya dasavatthudīpanena (cūḷava. 446 vitthāravatthu). “Gihigatānīti gihipaṭisaṃyuttānī”ti vadanti. Gihīsu gatāni, tehi ñātāni gihigatāni. Dhūmakālo etassāti dhūmakālikaṃ citakadhūmavūpasamato paraṃ appavattanato.

Like the bhikkhus in Sāvatthī, the Pācittiya should be made to be confessed (Pārā. 565, detailed account). Like the Vajjiputtakas, by an exposition of the ten points (Cūḷava. 446, detailed account). They say 'gihigatāni' means 'connected with laypeople'. Gone among laypeople, known by them, are 'gihigatāni'. 'Dhūmakālikaṃ' means 'of smoke time' because after the smoke of the funeral pyre has subsided, there is no further activity.

Thirabhāvappattāti sāsane thirabhāvaṃ anivattitabhāvaṃ upagatā. Therakārakehīti therabhāvasādhakehi sīlādiguṇehi asekkhadhammehi. Bahū rattiyoti pabbajitā hutvā bahū rattiyo jānanti. Sīlādiguṇesu patiṭṭhāpanameva sāsane pariṇāyakatāti āha “tīsu sikkhāsu pavattentī”ti.

“Thirabhāvappattā” means having reached a steadfast, unshakeable state in the Dispensation. “Therakārakehi” means by the qualities that make one an elder, that is, by the virtues such as morality, etc., that establish one as an elder, and by the qualities of one beyond training. “Bahū rattiyo” means, having gone forth, they know many nights. Establishing others in virtues like morality is indeed leadership in the Dispensation, thus he said: “engaging in the three trainings.”

Ovādaṃ na denti abhājanabhāvato. Paveṇīkathanti ācariyaparamparābhataṃ sammāpaṭipattidīpanaṃ dhammakathaṃ. Sārabhūtaṃ dhammapariyāyanti samathavipassanāmaggaphalasampāpanena sārabhūtaṃ bojjhaṅgakosallaanuttarasītībhāvaadhicittasuttādidhammatantiṃ.

They do not give advice because of unworthiness. “Paveṇīkathā” refers to the Dhamma talk handed down through the lineage of teachers, that illuminates the proper practice. “Sārabhūtaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ” means the essential Dhamma teaching that leads to the attainment of serenity, insight, path, and fruition, which is the body of doctrine comprising skill in the enlightenment factors, the supreme coolness, the state of higher mind, and suttas such as the Adhicitta Sutta.

Punabbhavadānaṃ punabbhavo uttarapadalopena. Itareti ye na paccayavasikā na āmisacakkhukā, te na gacchanti taṇhāya vasaṃ.

“Punabbhavadānaṃ” is 'punabbhavo' (renewed existence) by elision of the latter term. “Itare” means others, those who are not subject to conditions, nor have an eye for material things; they do not come under the power of craving.

Āraññakesūti araññabhāgesu araññapariyāpannesu. Nanu yattha katthacipi taṇhā sāvajjā evāti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “gāmantasenāsanesu hī”tiādi, tena “anuttaresu vimokkhesu pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayato”ti ettha vuttasinehādayo viya āraññakesu senāsanesu sālayatā sevitabbapakkhiyā evāti dasseti.

“Āraññakesu” means in wilderness areas, in places included within the scope of wilderness. Considering the objection, 'Is craving not blameworthy wherever it may be?', he said, 'for in village and monastery dwellings,' etc. Thereby, it is shown that just as the attachment and so on mentioned in the phrase 'one who cultivates longing for the unsurpassed liberations,' so too, for one attached to wilderness dwellings, this attachment is on the side of things that should be cultivated.

Attanāvāti [P 2.0164][V 2.0113] sayameva, tena parehi anussāhitānaṃ saraseneva anāgatānaṃ pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgamanaṃ, āgatānañca phāsuvihāraṃ paccāsisantīti dasseti. Iminā nīhārenāti imāya paṭipattiyā. Aggahitadhammaggahaṇanti [M 2.0127] aggahitassa pariyattidhammassa uggahaṇaṃ. Gahitasajjhāyakaraṇanti uggahitassa suṭṭhu atthacintanaṃ. Cintanattho hi sajjhāyasaddo.

“Attanāva” means of one's own accord. Thereby, it shows that they hope for the coming of virtuous monks who have not yet come, spontaneously, without being urged by others, and for a comfortable dwelling for those who have come. “Iminā nīhārena” means by this course of practice. “Aggahitadhammaggahaṇaṃ” means learning the ungrasped Dhamma of study. “Gahitasajjhāyakaraṇaṃ” means thoroughly reflecting on the meaning of what has been learned, for the word 'sajjhāya' has the meaning of reflection.

Entīti upagacchanti. Nisīdanti āsanapaññāpanādinā.

“Enti” means they approach. “Nisīdanti” means they are seated by the preparing of seats, etc.

137. Āramitabbaṭṭhena kammaṃ ārāmo. Kamme ratā, na ganthadhure, vāsadhure vāti kammaratā, anuyuttāti tapparabhāvena punappunaṃ pasutā. Iti kātabbakammanti taṃ taṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kātabbaṃ uccāvacakammaṃ cīvaravicāraṇādi. Tenāha “seyyathida”ntiādi. Upatthambhananti dupaṭṭatipaṭṭādikaraṇaṃ. Tañhi paṭhamapaṭalādīnaṃ upatthambhanakāraṇattā tathā vuttaṃ. Yadi evaṃ kathaṃ ayaṃ kammarāmatā paṭikkhittāti āha “ekacco hī”tiādi.

137. Work is 'ārāmo' (delight) in the sense of what is to be delighted in. 'Delighting in work' (kammaratā) means being devoted to work, not to the burden of study or the burden of residence; 'anuyuttā' (engaged) means being repeatedly engaged in it due to absorption in it. 'Kātabbakammaṃ' (the work to be done) refers to the various duties of monks, such as attending to robes, etc. Hence it is said: 'such as,' etc. 'Supporting' (upatthambhanaṃ) means making double-layered or triple-layered robes, etc. For that is so called because it is the cause of supporting the first layer, etc. If so, how is this delight in work rejected? He said: 'for some,' etc.

Karonto yevāti yathāvuttatiracchānakathaṃ kathentoyeva. Atiracchānakathābhāvepi tassa tattha tapparabhāvadassanatthaṃ avadhāraṇavacanaṃ. Pariyantakārīti sapariyantaṃ katvā vattā. “Pariyantavatiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā”ti (dī. ni. 1.9, 194) hi vuttaṃ. Appabhasso vāti parimitakathoyeva ekantena kathetabbasseva kathanato. Samāpattisamāpajjanaṃ ariyo tuṇhībhāvo.

“Karonto yeva” means just speaking the animal talk as previously mentioned. Even in the absence of animal talk, this emphatic word is to show his focused nature there. “Pariyantakārī” means one who speaks having made a limit. For it is said, 'He speaks speech with a limit' (Dī. Ni. 1.9, 194). “Appabhasso” means one who speaks limited words, since only what should be spoken is spoken. The noble silence is entering into meditative attainments.

Niddāyatiyevāti [P 2.0165] niddokkamane anādīnavadassī niddāyatiyeva. Iriyāpathaparivattanādinā na naṃ vinodeti.

'Just sleeps' (niddāyati yeva) means, seeing no fault in drowsiness, one just sleeps. One does not dispel it by changing posture or by other means.

Evaṃ saṃsaṭṭho vāti vuttanayena gaṇasaṅgaṇikāya saṃsaṭṭho eva viharati.

Or 'thus associated' (evaṃ saṃsaṭṭho vā) means, in the manner described, one lives associated only with groups and gatherings.

Dussīlā pāpicchā nāmāti sayaṃ nissīlā asantaguṇasambhāvanicchāya samannāgatattā pāpā lāmakā icchā etesanti pāpicchā.

The immoral (dussīlā) and those of evil wishes (pāpicchā) are so called because they themselves are devoid of virtue and possess the desire to be esteemed for qualities they do not have; thus, their wishes are evil and base, hence they are 'of evil wishes'.

Pāpapuggalehi mettikaraṇato pāpamittā. Tehi sadā saha pavattanena pāpasahāyā. Tattha ninnatādinā tadadhimuttatāya pāpasampavaṅkā.

'Evil friends' (pāpamittā) are so called from making friendship with evil individuals. 'Evil companions' (pāpasahāyā) are so called from always keeping company with them. 'Devoted to evil' (pāpasampavaṅkā) are so called because, through inclination and so on, they are devoted to them.

138. Saddhā etesaṃ atthīti saddhāti āha “saddhāsampannā”ti. Āgamanīyapaṭipadāya āgatasaddhā [V 2.0114] āgamanīyasaddhā, sā sātisayā mahābodhisattānaṃ paropadesena vinā saddheyyavatthuṃ aviparītato ogāhetvā [M 2.0128] adhimuccanatoti āha “sabbaññubodhisattānaṃ hotī”ti. Saccapaṭivedhato āgatasaddhā adhigamasaddhā surabandhādīnaṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 3.118; dha. pa. aṭṭha. 1.suppabuddhakuṭṭhivatthu; udā. aṭṭha. 43) viya. “Sammāsambuddho bhagavā”tiādinā buddhādīsu uppajjanakapasādo pasādasaddhā mahākappinarājādīnaṃ (a. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.231; dha. pa. aṭṭha. 1.mahākappinattheravatthu; theragā. aṭṭha. 2.mahākappinattheragāthāvaṇṇanā, vitthāro) viya. “Evameta”nti okkantitvā pakkhanditvā saddahanavasena kappanaṃ okappanaṃ. Duvidhāpīti pasādasaddhāpi okappanasaddhāpi. Tattha pasādasaddhā aparaneyyarūpā hoti savanamattena pasīdanato. Okappanasaddhā saddheyyavatthuṃ ogāhetvā anupavisitvā “evameta”nti paccakkhaṃ karontī viya pavattati. Tenāha “saddhādhimutto vakkalittherasadiso hotī”ti. Tassa hīti okappanasaddhāya samannāgatassa. Hirī etassa atthīti hiri, hiri mano etesanti hirimanāti āha “pāpa…pe… cittā”ti. Pāpato ottappenti ubbijjanti bhāyantīti ottappī.

138. 'They have faith,' thus they are faithful (saddhā); hence the words 'endowed with faith.' Faith that has come by the path of arrival is 'arriving faith.' It is extraordinary for the great bodhisattas, who, without the instruction of others, plunge into the object of faith without distortion and become resolved—thus it is said, 'It belongs to the all-knowing bodhisattas.' Faith that has come through the penetration of the truths is 'attainment faith,' like that of Surabandha and others. The confidence that arises towards the Buddha and others, beginning with 'The Blessed One is a perfectly enlightened Buddha,' is 'confidence-faith,' like that of King Mahākappina and others. Having entered and plunged in, the settling by way of belief, thinking 'It is so,' is 'settling faith' (okappana). It is also twofold: confidence-faith and settling-faith. Therein, confidence-faith is of a nature not to be led by another, as one has confidence merely upon hearing. Settling-faith, having plunged into and penetrated the object of faith, proceeds as if making it directly evident, thinking, 'It is so.' Therefore it is said, 'One resolved by faith becomes like the elder Vakkali.' 'For him' means for one endowed with settling-faith. 'He has a sense of shame,' thus he has shame (hiri); 'their mind has a sense of shame,' thus they are conscientious (hirimano), as stated: 'a mind... from evil...' They are scrupulous, shrink back, and are afraid of evil, thus they are 'fearful of wrongdoing' (ottappī).

Bahu sutaṃ suttageyyādi etenāti bahussuto, sutaggahaṇaṃ cettha nidassanamattaṃ dhāraṇaparicayaparipucchānupekkhanadiṭṭhinijjhānānaṃ [P 2.0166] pettha icchitabbattā. Savanamūlakattā vā tesampi taggahaṇeneva gahaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Atthakāmena pariyāpuṇitabbato, diṭṭhadhammikādipurisatthasiddhiyā pariyattabhāvato ca pariyatti, tīṇi piṭakāni. Saccappaṭivedho saccānaṃ paṭivijjhanaṃ. Tadapi bāhusaccaṃ yathāvuttabāhusaccakiccanipphattito. Pariyatti adhippetā saccapaṭivedhāvahena bāhusaccena bahussutabhāvassa idha icchitattā. Soti pariyattibahussuto. Catubbidho hoti pañcamassa pakārassa abhāvato. Sabbatthakabahussutoti nissayamuccanakabahussutādayo viya padesiko ahutvā piṭakattaye sabbatthakameva bāhusaccasabbhāvato sabbassa atthassa kāyanato kathanato sabbatthakabahussuto. Te idha adhippetā paṭipattipaṭivedhasaddhammānaṃ mūlabhūte pariyattisaddhamme suppatiṭṭhitabhāvato.

One by whom much has been heard, such as discourses and verses, is called 'well-learned' (bahussuta). Here, the term 'hearing' is merely an indication, for retention, familiarity, questioning, investigation, reflection, and penetration by view are also intended here. Or, because these too are rooted in listening, their inclusion should be seen as implied by the term 'hearing'. It is 'scripture' (pariyatti) because it should be mastered by one who desires the goal, and because it constitutes the scriptural basis for the accomplishment of the human goal, beginning with that in this very life; it is the three Piṭakas. The penetration of the truths is the piercing of the truths. That too is 'extensive learning' (bāhusacca), as it accomplishes the function of extensive learning as described. 'Scripture' is intended, because the state of being well-learned is desired here by means of extensive learning that leads to the penetration of the truths. He is one well-learned in the scriptures. This is fourfold, as there is no fifth kind. A 'universally well-learned one' (sabbatthakabahussuta) is one who is not partial, like those well-learned in matters of dependence and its termination and so on, but is one whose extensive learning exists universally throughout the three Piṭakas; because of explaining and speaking of all the meaning, one is universally well-learned. These are intended here because they are firmly established in the scriptural Dhamma, which is the root of the Dhamma of practice and penetration.

Āraddhanti paggahitaṃ. Taṃ pana duvidhampi vīriyārambhavibhāgena dassetuṃ “tatthā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha ekakāti ekākino, vūpakaṭṭhavihārinoti attho.

Āraddha means 'exerted'. To show that this is twofold, by way of the division of the commencement of energy, 'therein...' and so on is stated. Therein, 'ekakā' means 'solitary'; the meaning is 'dwelling secluded'.

Pucchitvāti [M 2.0129] parato pucchitvā. Sampaṭicchāpetunti “tvaṃ asukanāmo”ti vatvā tehi “āmā”ti paṭijānāpetunti attho. Evaṃ cirakatādianussaraṇasamatthasatinepakkānaṃ appakasireneva [V 2.0115] satisambojjhaṅgabhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchatīti dassanatthaṃ “evarūpe bhikkhū sandhāyā”ti vuttaṃ. Tenevāha “apicā”tiādi.

'Having asked' means having inquired from another. 'Having them acknowledge' means saying to them, "You are so-and-so," and having them acknowledge it with, "Yes"; that is the meaning. To show that for those whose mindfulness is astute and capable of recollecting things done long ago and so on, the development of the enlightenment factor of mindfulness reaches fulfillment with little effort, it is said, "With reference to such monks." Therefore it is also said, "Moreover..." and so on.

139. Bujjhati etāyāti “bodhī”ti laddhanāmāya sammādiṭṭhiādidhammasāmaggiyā aṅgoti bojjhaṅgo, pasattho, sundaro vā bojjhaṅgo sambojjhaṅgo. Upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇoti kāyavedanācittadhammānaṃ asubhadukkhāniccānattabhāvasallakkhaṇasaṅkhātaṃ ārammaṇe upaṭṭhānaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ etassāti upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇo. Catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ pīḷanādippakārato vicayo upaparikkhā lakkhaṇaṃ etassāti pavicayalakkhaṇo. Anuppannā kusalānuppādanādivasena cittassa [P 2.0167] paggaho paggaṇhanaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ etassāti paggahalakkhaṇo. Pharaṇaṃ vipphārikatā lakkhaṇaṃ etassāti pharaṇalakkhaṇo. Upasamo kāyacittapariḷāhānaṃ vūpasamanaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ etassāti upasamalakkhaṇo. Avikkhepo vikkhepaviddhaṃsanaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ etassāti avikkhepalakkhaṇo. Līnuddhaccarahite adhicitte pavattamāne paggahaniggahasampahaṃsanesu abyāvaṭattā ajjhupekkhanaṃ paṭisaṅkhānaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ etassāti paṭisaṅkhānalakkhaṇo.

139. One awakens by means of it, thus it is a factor (aṅga) of the collection of phenomena beginning with right view which has obtained the name 'awakening' (bodhi); hence 'bojjhaṅga'. A praised or beautiful bojjhaṅga is a 'sambojjhaṅga'. Its characteristic is presence: the establishment on the object, which is characterized as the discerning of the nature of foulness, suffering, impermanence, and non-self regarding body, feeling, mind, and phenomena. Its characteristic is investigation: the examination of the Four Noble Truths according to their aspects of oppression and so on. Its characteristic is exertion: the uplifting of the mind by way of producing unarisen wholesome states and so on. Its characteristic is pervasion: the quality of being pervasive. Its characteristic is calming: the pacifying of bodily and mental fevers. Its characteristic is non-distraction: the destruction of distraction. Its characteristic is reflective equanimity: looking on, because of not being occupied with exertion, restraint, and gladdening when the higher mind, free from sloth and restlessness, is proceeding.

Catūhi kāraṇehīti satisampajaññaṃ, muṭṭhassatipuggalaparivajjanā, upaṭṭhitassatipuggalasevanā, tadadhimuttatāti imehi catūhi kāraṇehi. Chahi kāraṇehīti paripucchakatā, vatthuvisadakiriyā, indriyasamattapaṭipādanā, duppaññapuggalaparivajjanā, paññavantapuggalasevanā, tadadhimuttatāti imehi chahi kāraṇehi. Mahāsatipaṭṭhānavaṇṇanāyaṃ pana “sattahi kāraṇehī” (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.385; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.118) vakkhati, taṃ gambhīrañāṇacariyāpaccavekkhaṇāti imaṃ kāraṇaṃ pakkhipitvā veditabbaṃ. Navahi kāraṇehīti apāyabhayapaccavekkhaṇā, gamanavīthipaccavekkhaṇā, piṇḍapātassa apacāyanatā, dāyajjamahattapaccavekkhaṇā, satthumahattapaccavekkhaṇā, sabrahmacārīmahattapaccavekkhaṇā, kusītapuggalaparivajjanā, āraddhavīriyapuggalasevanā, tadadhimuttatāti imehi navahi kāraṇehi. Mahāsatipaṭṭhānavaṇṇanāyaṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.385; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.118) pana [M 2.0130] ānisaṃsadassāvitā, jātimahattapaccavekkhaṇāti imehi saddhiṃ “ekādasā”ti vakkhati. Dasahi kāraṇehīti buddhānussati, dhammānussati, saṅghasīlacāgadevatāupasamānussati, lūkhapuggalaparivajjanā, siniddhapuggalasevanā, tadadhimuttatāti imehi dasahi. Mahāsatipaṭṭhānavaṇṇanāyaṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.385; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.118) pana pasādaniyasuttantapaccavekkhaṇāya saddhiṃ “ekādasā”ti vakkhati. Sattahi kāraṇehīti paṇītabhojanasevanatā[P 2.0168], utusukhasevanatā, iriyāpathasukhasevanatā, majjhattapayogatā, sāraddhakāyapuggalaparivajjanatā[V 2.0116], passaddhakāyapuggalasevanatā, tadadhimuttatāti imehi sattahi. Dasahi kāraṇehīti vatthuvisadakiriyā, indriyasamattapaṭipādanā, nimittakusalatā, samaye cittassa paggahaṇaṃ, samaye cittassa niggahaṇaṃ, samaye cittassa sampahaṃsanaṃ, samaye cittassa ajjhupekkhanaṃ, asamāhitapuggalaparivajjanaṃ, samāhitapuggalasevanaṃ, tadadhimuttatāti imehi dasahi kāraṇehi. Mahāsatipaṭṭhānavaṇṇanāyaṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.385; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.118) pana “jhānavimokkhapaccavekkhaṇā”ti iminā saddhiṃ “ekādasahī”ti vakkhati. Pañcahi kāraṇehīti sattamajjhattatā, saṅkhāramajjhattatā, sattasaṅkhārakelāyanapuggalaparivajjanā, sattasaṅkhāramajjhattapuggalasevanā, tadadhimuttatāti imehi pañcahi kāraṇehi. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ mahāsatipaṭṭhānavaṇṇanāyaṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.385; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.118) āgamissati. Kāmaṃ bodhipakkhiyadhammā nāma nippariyāyato ariyamaggasampayuttā eva niyyānikabhāvato. Suttantadesanā nāma pariyāyakathāti “iminā vipassanā…pe… kathesī”ti vuttaṃ.

By four reasons: mindfulness and clear comprehension, avoiding unmindful persons, associating with mindful persons, and inclination towards that—by these four reasons. By six reasons: being inquisitive, clarifying the object, balancing the faculties, avoiding unwise persons, associating with wise persons, and inclination towards that—by these six reasons. In the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna commentary, however, it will be said 'by seven reasons'; that should be understood by including this reason: reviewing profound knowledge and conduct. By nine reasons: reviewing the fear of the lower realms, reviewing the path of going, reverence for almsfood, reviewing the greatness of the inheritance, reviewing the greatness of the Teacher, reviewing the greatness of the spiritual companions, avoiding lazy persons, associating with energetic persons, and inclination towards that—by these nine reasons. In the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna commentary, however, it will be said 'by eleven' along with these: seeing the benefits and reviewing the greatness of birth. By ten reasons: recollection of the Buddha, recollection of the Dhamma, recollection of the Sangha, recollection of virtue, recollection of generosity, recollection of deities, recollection of peace, avoiding coarse persons, associating with refined persons, and inclination towards that—by these ten. In the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna commentary, however, it will be said 'by eleven' along with reviewing inspiring suttas. By seven reasons: resorting to fine foods, resorting to an agreeable climate, resorting to a comfortable posture, applying neutrality, avoiding persons with agitated bodies, associating with persons with calmed bodies, and inclination towards that—by these seven. By ten reasons: clarifying the object, balancing the faculties, skillfulness in signs, arousing the mind at the right time, restraining the mind at the right time, gladdening the mind at the right time, looking on at the mind with equanimity at the right time, avoiding unconcentrated persons, associating with concentrated persons, and inclination towards that—by these ten reasons. In the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna commentary, however, it will be said 'by eleven' along with this: 'reviewing jhāna and liberation'. By five reasons: equanimity towards beings, equanimity towards formations, avoiding persons who delight in beings and formations, associating with persons who are equanimous towards beings and formations, and inclination towards that—by these five reasons. Whatever is to be said on this will come in the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna commentary. Indeed, the factors of enlightenment are, in the direct sense, connected to the noble path due to their nature of leading out. The teaching of the suttas is an indirect teaching, thus it is said: 'With this insight... he taught'.

140. Tebhūmake saṅkhāre “aniccā”ti anupassati etāyāti aniccānupassanā, tathā pavattā vipassanā, sā pana yasmā attanā sahagatasaññāya bhāvitāya vibhāvitā eva hotīti vuttaṃ “aniccānupassanāya saddhiṃ uppannasaññā”ti. Saññāsīsena vāyaṃ vipassanāya eva niddeso. Anattasaññādīsupi eseva nayo. Lokiyavipassanāpi honti, yasmā “anicca”ntiādinā tā pavattantīti. Lokiyavipassanāpīti pi-saddena missakāpettha santīti atthato āpannanti atthāpattisiddhamatthaṃ niddhāretvā sarūpato dassetuṃ “virāgo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha āgatavasenāti tathā āgatapāḷivasena “virāgo nirodho”ti hi tattha [M 2.0131] nibbānaṃ vuttanti idha [P 2.0169] “virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā”ti vuttasaññā nibbānārammaṇāpi siyuṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “dve lokuttarāpi hontī”ti.

140. One contemplates formations in the three planes as 'impermanent' by means of this; thus, it is 'aniccānupassanā' (contemplation of impermanence), which is insight that proceeds in that way. But since that insight, when developed, is indeed made manifest by a perception that has arisen together with it, it is said, 'the perception arisen together with the contemplation of impermanence'. This is indeed a designation of insight with perception as its chief. The same method applies to the perception of not-self, and so on. There are also mundane insights, because they proceed with 'impermanent' and so on. The 'pi' (also) in 'mundane insights also' implies that mixed ones are present here, which is arrived at from the meaning. To determine the meaning established by implication and to show its nature, 'dispassion' and so on is stated. In that case, 'by way of what has come' means by way of the Pāli text that has come thus; since there 'dispassion, cessation' refers to Nibbāna, here the perceptions stated as 'perception of dispassion, perception of cessation' can also have Nibbāna as their object. Therefore, it is said, 'two can be supramundane'.

141. Mettā etassa atthīti mettaṃ, cittaṃ. Taṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ kāyakammaṃ mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ. Esa nayo sesadvayepi. Imānipi mettākāyakammādīni bhikkhūnaṃ vasena āgatāni tesaṃ seṭṭhaparisabhāvato. Yathā pana bhikkhūsupi labbhanti, evaṃ gihīsupi labbhanti catuparisasādhāraṇattāti taṃ dassento “bhikkhūnañhī”tiādimāha. Kāmaṃ ādibrahmacariyakadhammassavanenapi mettākāyakammāni labbhanti, nippariyāyato pana cārittadhammassavanena ayamattho icchitoti dassento “ābhisamācārikadhammapūraṇa”nti āha. Tepiṭakampi buddhavacanaṃ paripucchanaatthakathanavasena pavattiyamānaṃ hitajjhāsayena pavattitabbato.

141. Loving-kindness is present in this, thus it is 'mettaṃ': the mind. Bodily action originating from that is loving-kindness bodily action. This is the method in the remaining two as well. These loving-kindness bodily actions and so on are presented with reference to bhikkhus because they are the superior assembly. But just as they are found in bhikkhus, so too are they found in householders, since they are common to the four assemblies. To show this, he said, 'for bhikkhus, indeed,' and so on. Indeed, loving-kindness bodily actions can be attained even by hearing the Dhamma at the beginning of the holy life; but to show that this meaning is intended in the direct sense through hearing the Dhamma of conduct, he said, 'fulfilling the code of higher conduct'. The Tipiṭaka, the word of the Buddha, should also be set forth with a benevolent intention, as it proceeds by way of questioning and explaining the meaning.

Āvīti [V 2.0117] pakāsaṃ, pakāsabhāvo cettha yaṃ uddissa taṃ kāyakammaṃ karīyati, tassa sammukhabhāvatoti āha “sammukhā”ti. Rahoti appakāsaṃ, appakāsatā ca yaṃ uddissa taṃ kāyakammaṃ karīyati, tassa paccakkhābhāvatoti āha “parammukhā”ti. Sahāyabhāvagamanaṃ tesaṃ purato. Ubhayehīti navakehi, therehi ca.

'Āvī' means openly. The state of being open here is due to the one towards whom that bodily action is performed being face-to-face; thus, he said 'sammukhā' (in one's presence). 'Raho' means secretly. And the state of not being open is due to the absence of the one towards whom that bodily action is performed; thus, he said 'parammukhā' (behind one's back). 'Going with a friendly disposition' means in front of them. 'By both' means by both junior and senior bhikkhus.

Paggayhāti paggaṇhitvā uccaṃ katvā.

'Paggayha' means having taken up and made high.

Kāmaṃ mettāsinehasiniddhānaṃ nayanānaṃ ummīlanā, pasannena mukhena olokanañca mettaṃ kāyakammameva, yassa pana cittassa vasena nayanānaṃ mettāsinehasiniddhatā, mukhassa ca pasannatā, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “mettaṃ manokammaṃ nāmā”ti.

Indeed, the opening of eyes that are gentle with loving-kindness and affection, and looking with a serene face, is itself loving-kindness as bodily action. But with reference to the mind, by the power of which the eyes are gentle with loving-kindness and affection and the face is serene, it is said, 'this is called loving-kindness as mental action'.

Lābhasaddo kammasādhano “lābhāvata, lābho laddho”tiādīsu viya, so cettha “dhammaladdhā”ti vacanato atītakālikoti āha “cīvarādayo laddhapaccayā”ti. Dhammato [P 2.0170] āgatāti dhammikā. Tenāha “dhammaladdhā”ti. Imameva hi atthaṃ dassetuṃ “kuhanādī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Cittena vibhajanapubbakaṃ kāyena vibhajananti mūlameva dassetuṃ “evaṃ cittena vibhajana”nti vuttaṃ, tena cittuppādamattenapi paṭivibhāgo na kātabboti dasseti. Appaṭivibhattanti bhāvanapuṃsakaniddeso, appaṭivibhattaṃ vā lābhaṃ bhuñjatīti kammaniddeso eva.

The word 'lābha' (gain) is a noun in the objective sense, as in 'lābhāvata, lābho laddho' (gain has come, gain has been obtained) and so on. Here, since it is said 'dhammaladdhā' (righteously obtained), it is in the past tense; thus, he said 'the requisites such as robes are obtained requisites'. 'Dhammato āgatā' means 'come from the Dhamma', thus 'dhammikā' (righteous). Therefore, he said 'dhammaladdhā' (righteously obtained). Indeed, to show this very meaning, 'deceit, etc.' and so on is stated. To show the very root—dividing with the body, which is preceded by dividing with the mind—it is said, 'thus, dividing with the mind'. By this, he shows that a separate portion should not be made even with the mere arising of a thought. 'Appaṭivibhatta' (unshared) is a neuter designation in the abstract sense of 'not sharing', or in 'enjoys unshared gain', it is simply a designation of the object.

Taṃ [M 2.0132] taṃ neva gihīnaṃ deti attano ājīvasodhanatthaṃ. Na attanā bhuñjatīti attanāva na paribhuñjati “mayhaṃ asādhāraṇabhogitā mā hotū”ti. “Paṭiggaṇhanto ca…pe… passatī”ti iminā tassa lābhassa tīsupi kālesu sādhāraṇato ṭhapanaṃ dassitaṃ. “Paṭiggaṇhanto ca saṅghena sādhāraṇaṃ hotū”ti iminā paṭiggahaṇakālo dassito, “gahetvā…pe… passatī”ti iminā paṭiggahitakālo, tadubhayaṃ pana tādisena pubbābhogena vinā na hotīti atthasiddho purimakālo. Tayidaṃ paṭiggahaṇato pubbe vassa hoti “saṅghena sādhāraṇaṃ hotūti paṭiggahessāmī”ti. Paṭiggaṇhantassa hoti “saṅghena sādhāraṇaṃ hotūti paṭiggaṇhāmī”ti. Paṭiggahetvā hoti “saṅghena sādhāraṇaṃ hotūti paṭiggahitaṃ mayā”ti evaṃ tilakkhaṇasampannaṃ katvā laddhalābhaṃ osānalakkhaṇaṃ avikopetvā paribhuñjanto sādhāraṇabhogī, appaṭivibhattabhogī ca hoti.

He does not give it to householders for the sake of purifying his own livelihood. Nor does he consume it himself—thus he does not use it personally, thinking, 'May my enjoyment not be unshared.' By 'while receiving... he sees,' the establishing of that gain as shared in all three times is shown. By 'while receiving, may it be shared with the Sangha,' the time of receiving is indicated. By 'having taken... he sees,' the time after receiving is indicated. But both of these cannot occur without such prior intention; thus, the prior time is established by implication. This occurs before receiving: 'I will receive it, thinking, "May it be shared with the Sangha."' While receiving, it occurs: 'I am receiving it, thinking, "May it be shared with the Sangha."' After receiving, it occurs: 'I have received it, thinking, "May it be shared with the Sangha."' Having made the received gain endowed with these three characteristics, while enjoying it without destroying the characteristic of relinquishment, he is one who enjoys shared things and one who enjoys things without apportioning them.

Imaṃ pana sāraṇīyadhammanti imaṃ catutthaṃ saritabbayuttadhammaṃ. Na hi…pe… gaṇhanti, tasmā [V 2.0118] sādhāraṇabhogitā eva dussīlassa natthīti ārambhopi tāva na sambhavati, kuto pūraṇanti adhippāyo. “Parisuddhasīlo”ti iminā lābhassa dhammikabhāvaṃ dasseti. “Vattaṃ akhaṇḍento”ti iminā appaṭivibhattabhogitaṃ, sādhāraṇabhogitañca dasseti. Sati pana tadubhaye sāraṇīyadhammo pūrito eva hotīti āha “pūretī”ti. “Odissakaṃ [P 2.0171] katvā”ti etena anodissakaṃ katvā pituno, ācariyupajjhāyādīnaṃ vā therāsanato paṭṭhāya dentassa sāraṇīyadhammoyeva hotīti. Sāraṇīyadhammo panassa na hotīti paṭijagganaṭṭhāne odissakaṃ katvā dinnattā. Tenāha “palibodhajagganaṃ nāma hotī”tiādi. Yadi evaṃ sabbena sabbaṃ sāraṇīyadhammapūrakassa odissakadānaṃ na vaṭṭatīti? No na vaṭṭati yuttaṭṭhāneti dassento “tena panā”tiādimāha. Gilānādīnaṃ odissakaṃ katvā dānaṃ appaṭivibhāgapakkhikaṃ “asukassa na dassāmī”ti paṭikkhepassa abhāvato. Byatirekappadhāno hi paṭivibhāgo. Tenāha “avasesa”ntiādi. Adātumpīti pi-saddena dātumpi vaṭṭatīti dasseti, tañca kho karuṇāyanavasena, na vattapūraṇavasena.

Now, 'this sāraṇīyadhamma' means this fourth quality suitable to be remembered. Indeed... they do not take... therefore, shared enjoyment is simply not for the immoral one; thus, even the beginning of it is not possible, let alone the fulfillment—this is the intended meaning. By 'of purified virtue,' he shows the righteous nature of the gain. By 'not breaking the practice,' he shows both enjoyment without division and shared enjoyment. When both of these are present, the sāraṇīyadhamma is indeed fulfilled; thus, he said 'he fulfills.' By 'having specified': by this it is shown that for one who gives without specifying to his father, teacher, preceptor, and so on, starting from the elder's seat, it is indeed the sāraṇīyadhamma. But it is not the sāraṇīyadhamma for him, because of giving with specification in a place of care. Therefore, it is said, 'it is called guarding against obstacles,' and so on. If so, is giving with specification entirely inappropriate for one fulfilling the sāraṇīyadhamma in every way? No, it is not inappropriate in a suitable place; to show this, he said, 'but by that,' and so on. Giving with specification to the sick and others is on the side of non-division, as there is no rejection such as, 'I will not give to so-and-so.' For division is predominantly about exclusion. Therefore, he said, 'the rest,' and so on. By the particle 'pi' in 'even not to give,' it is indicated that giving is also suitable, but that too out of compassion, not for the sake of fulfilling a duty.

Susikkhitāyāti sāraṇīyadhammapūraṇavidhimhi suṭṭhu sikkhitāya, sukusalāyāti attho. Idāni tassā kosallaṃ dassetuṃ “susikkhitāya hī”tiādi [M 2.0133] vuttaṃ. “Dvādasahi vassehi pūrati, na tato ora”nti iminā tassa duppūraṇaṃ dasseti. Tathā hi so mahapphalo mahānisaṃso, diṭṭhadhammikehipi tāva garutarehi phalānisaṃsehi ca anugato. Taṃsamaṅgī ca puggalo visesalābhī ariyapuggalo viya loke acchariyabbhutadhammasamannāgato hoti. Tathā hi so duppajahaṃ dānamayassa, sīlamayassa ca puññassa paṭipakkhadhammaṃ sudūre vikkhambhitaṃ katvā suvisuddhena cetasā loke pākaṭo paññāto hutvā viharati, tassimamatthaṃ byatirekato, anvayato ca vibhāvetuṃ “sace hī”tiādi vuttaṃ, taṃ suviññeyyameva.

'Susikkhitāya' means well-trained in the method of fulfilling the sāraṇīyadhamma; that is, highly skilled. Now, to show her skill, 'for one who is well-trained,' and so on is stated. By 'it is fulfilled in twelve years, not less than that,' he shows the difficulty of its fulfillment. For indeed, it is of great fruit and great benefit, and is accompanied by fruits and benefits in this very life that are even more weighty. And a person endowed with it becomes one who has obtained a special attainment, like a noble person, endowed with astonishing and wonderful qualities in the world. Indeed, having suppressed far away the opposing qualities to merit born of generosity and virtue—which are hard to abandon—such a person dwells, manifest and renowned in the world, with a very purified mind. To explain this meaning by way of contrast and connection, 'if indeed,' and so on is stated, and this is easily understood.

Idāni ye samparāyike, diṭṭhadhammike ca ānisaṃse dassetuṃ “eva”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Neva issā, na macchariyaṃ hoti cirakālabhāvanāya vidhutabhāvato. Manussānaṃ piyo hoti pariccāgasīlatāya visuddhattā. Tenāha “dadaṃ piyo hoti bhajanti naṃ bahū”tiādi [P 2.0172] (a. ni. 5.34). Sulabhapaccayo hoti dānavasena uḷārajjhāsayānaṃ paccayalābhassa idhānisaṃsabhāvato dānassa. Pattagataṃ assa diyyamānaṃ na khīyati pattagatavasena dvādasavassikassa mahāpattassa avicchedena pūritattā. Aggabhaṇḍaṃ labhati devasikaṃ dakkhiṇeyyānaṃ aggato paṭṭhāya dānassa dinnattā. Bhayevā…pe… āpajjanti deyyapaṭiggāhakavikappaṃ [V 2.0119] akatvā attani nirapekkhacittena cirakālaṃ dānapūratāya pasāditacittattā.

Now, to show the benefits both in the future life and in the present life, 'thus,' and so on is stated. There is neither envy nor stinginess, because they have been dispelled through long cultivation. He becomes dear to people due to his generous nature and purity. Therefore, it is said, 'The giver becomes dear, and many associate with him,' and so on (AN 5.34). He easily obtains requisites through the power of giving, since obtaining requisites is a benefit of giving in this life for those with noble intentions. What is placed in his bowl, being given, is not exhausted, because his great bowl is continuously filled, as if for twelve years. He receives the finest items daily, because gifts are given starting from the foremost of those worthy of offerings. Even in danger... they resort to him, because their minds are pleased by the long fulfillment of giving with a mind unconcerned for oneself, not making distinctions between what is to be given and the recipient.

Tatrāti tesu ānisaṃsesu vibhāvetabbesu. Imāni taṃ dīpanāni vatthūni kāraṇāni. Alabhantāpīti amahāpuññatāya na lābhino samānāpi. Bhikkhācāramaggasabhāganti sabhāgaṃ tabbhāgiyaṃ bhikkhācāramaggaṃ jānanti.

'Tatra' means among those benefits that are to be explained. These are the illuminating stories and reasons for it. 'Alabhantāpi' means even while not being recipients of gain, due to not having great merit. 'Bhikkhācāramaggasabhāgaṃ' means they know the path of alms-gathering to be common and shared.

Anuttarimanussadhammattā, therānaṃ saṃsayavinodanatthañca “sāraṇīyadhammo me bhante pūrito”ti āha. Tathā hi dutiyavatthusmimpi therena attā pakāsito. Manussānaṃ piyatāya, sulabhapaccayatāyapi idaṃ vatthumeva. Pattagatākhīyanassa pana visesaṃ vibhāvanato “idaṃ tāva…pe… ettha vatthu”nti vuttaṃ.

Because of possessing a superhuman quality, and to dispel the doubts of the elders, he said, 'Venerable sir, the sāraṇīyadhamma has been fulfilled by me.' Indeed, in the second story as well, the elder declared this about himself. This very story is also an example of being dear to people and being easily supported with requisites. But because it explains the special quality of the non-exhaustion of the bowl's contents, it is said, 'this indeed... here is the story.'

Giribhaṇḍamahāpūjāyāti [M 2.0134] cetiyagirimhi sakalalaṅkādīpe, yojanappamāṇe samudde ca nāvāsaṅghāṭādike ṭhapetvā dīpapupphagandhādīhi kariyamānamahāpūjāyaṃ. Pariyāyenapīti lesenapi. Anucchavikanti sāraṇīyadhammapūraṇatopi idaṃ yathābhūtappavedanaṃ tumhākaṃ anucchavikanti attho.

'Giribhaṇḍamahāpūjāya' means at the great offering made on Cetiyagiri, throughout the entire island of Laṅkā, and in the sea for the extent of a yojana, with lamps, flowers, perfumes, and so on, setting aside ships, rafts, and the like. 'Pariyāyenapi' means even by a hint. 'Anucchavikaṃ' means this truthful declaration is more fitting for you than even the fulfillment of the sāraṇīyadhamma.

Anārocetvāva palāyiṃsu corabhayena. “Attano dujjīvikāyā”ti ca vadanti.

Without informing anyone, they fled due to fear of thieves. And they say, 'Because of our own difficult livelihood.'

Vaṭṭissatīti kappissati. Therī sāraṇīyadhammapūrikā ahosi, therassa pana sīlatejeneva devatā ussukkaṃ āpajji.

'Vaṭṭissati' means it will be fitting. The elder nun was a fulfiller of the sāraṇīyadhamma, but it was solely through the elder monk's power of virtue that a deity became zealous.

Natthi [P 2.0173] etesaṃ khaṇḍanti akhaṇḍāni. Taṃ pana nesaṃ khaṇḍaṃ dassetuṃ “yassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha upasampannasīlānaṃ uddesakkamena ādi antā veditabbā. Tenāha “sattasū”tiādi. Anupasampannasīlānaṃ pana samādānakkamenapi ādi antā labbhanti. Pariyante chinnasāṭako viyāti vatthante, dasante vā chinnavatthaṃ viya, visadisūdāharaṇaṃ cetaṃ “akhaṇḍānī”ti imassa adhigatattā. Evaṃ sesānipi udāharaṇāni. Khaṇḍitabhinnatā khaṇḍaṃ, taṃ etassa atthīti khaṇḍaṃ, sīlaṃ. “Chidda”ntiādīsupi eseva nayo. Vemajjhe bhinnaṃ vinivijjhanavasena visabhāgavaṇṇena gāvī viyāti sambandho. Sabalarahitāni asabalāni. Tathā akammāsāni. Sīlassa taṇhādāsabyato mocanaṃ vivaṭṭūpanissayabhāvāpādanaṃ. Yasmā ca taṃsamaṅgīpuggalo serī sayaṃvasī bhujisso nāma hoti, tasmāpi bhujissāni. Tenevāha “bhujissabhāvakāraṇato [V 2.0120] bhujissānī”ti. Suparisuddhabhāvena pāsaṃsattā viññupasatthāni. Imināhaṃ sīlena devo vā bhaveyyaṃ, devaññataro vā, tattha “nicco dhuvo sassato”ti, “sīlena suddhī”ti ca evaṃ ādinā taṇhādiṭṭhīhi aparāmaṭṭhattā. “Ayaṃ te sīlesu doso”ti catūsupi vipattīsu yāya kāyaci vipattiyā dassanena parāmaṭṭhuṃ anuddhaṃsetuṃ. Samādhisaṃvattanappayojanāni samādhisaṃvattanikāni.

There is no breaking for them; they are unbroken. But to point out what constitutes a break for them, it is said, 'whose,' etc. Herein, for the virtue of the fully ordained, the beginning and end should be understood according to the order of recitation. Therefore, it is said, 'in the seven,' etc. For the virtue of the not fully ordained, however, the beginning and end can also be obtained according to the method of undertaking. At the edge, like a torn robe; or at the hem, like a cut cloth—this is an example of dissimilarity because the meaning of 'unbroken' is understood. Similarly, the other examples should be understood. The state of being broken and split is a break; that which has this is called 'broken,' regarding virtue. The same method applies to 'flawed,' etc. The connection is: broken in the middle by way of piercing, like a cow of a dissimilar color. Devoid of spots means unspotted. Likewise, unblemished. The liberation of virtue from slavery to craving is making it a basis for turning away from saṃsāra. And because a person possessing that is independent, self-mastered, and called 'free,' therefore, they are also 'liberating.' Therefore, it is said, 'Because they are the cause of the state of being free, they are called liberating.' Because of being supremely pure, they are praised by the wise. Because they are not grasped by craving and wrong view—such as, 'By this virtue, may I become a god or another kind of divine being,' or notions such as 'eternal, permanent, everlasting' and 'purity through virtue'—and because they cannot be assailed or disparaged by pointing out any of the four kinds of failure, saying, 'This is your fault in regard to the virtues.' Having the purpose of leading to concentration, they are conducive to concentration.

Samānabhāvūpagatasīlāti sīlasampattiyā samānabhāvaṃ upagatasīlā sabhāgavuttikā. Kāmaṃ puthujjanānañca catupārisuddhisīle nānattaṃ na siyā, taṃ [M 2.0135] pana na ekantikaṃ, idaṃ ekantikaṃ niyatabhāvatoti āha “natthi maggasīle nānatta”nti. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttanti maggasīlaṃ sandhāya etaṃ “yāni tāni sīlānī”tiādi vuttaṃ.

“Possessing similar virtue” means possessing virtue that has attained similarity through the accomplishment of moral conduct, having a shared livelihood. Though there might be no difference in the fourfold purified virtue among ordinary people, that is not definitive. This is definitive, being of a fixed nature; therefore it is said, “There is no difference in path virtue.” Referring to that, it is said with reference to path virtue: “Whatever those virtues are,” and so on.

Yāyanti yā ayaṃ mayhañceva tumhākañca paccakkhabhūtā[P 2.0174]. Diṭṭhīti maggasammādiṭṭhi. Niddosāti nidhutadosā, samucchinnarāgādipāpadhammāti attho. Niyyātīti vaṭṭadukkhato nissarati nigacchati. Sayaṃ niyyantasseva hi “taṃsamaṅgīpuggalaṃ vaṭṭadukkhato niyyāpetī”ti vuccati. Yā satthu anusiṭṭhi, taṃ karotīti takkaro, tassa, yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipajjanakassāti attho. Samānadiṭṭhibhāvanti sadisadiṭṭhibhāvaṃ saccasampaṭivedhena abhinnadiṭṭhibhāvaṃ. Vuddhiyevāti ariyavinaye guṇehi vuḍḍhiyeva, no parihānīti ayaṃ aparihāniyadhammadesanā attanopi sāsanassa addhaniyataṃ ākaṅkhantena bhagavatā idha desitā.

That which is directly evident to both me and you. 'View' means the path's right view. 'Free from defilements' means rid of faults, with evil qualities like greed cut off—this is the meaning. 'Leads out' means escapes from the suffering of the cycle of existence, goes forth. For one who himself escapes, it is said, “He leads that person endowed with such qualities out from the suffering of the cycle of existence.” He who does as instructed by the Teacher is called a 'doer'—one who practices according to the instruction—this is the meaning. 'Having the same view' means having a similar view, having an undivided view through the penetration of truth. 'Only growth' means only growth in virtues within the Noble Discipline, not decline—this teaching on the qualities that prevent decline was given here by the Blessed One, who desired the long duration of his Dispensation.

142. Āsannaparinibbānattāti katipayamāsādhikena saṃvaccharamattena parinibbānaṃ bhavissatīti katvā vuttaṃ. Etaṃyevāti “iti sīla”ntiādikaṃyeva iti sīlanti ettha iti-saddo pakārattho, parimāṇattho ca ekajjhaṃ katvā gahitoti āha “evaṃ sīlaṃ ettakaṃ sīla”nti. Evaṃ sīlanti evaṃ pabhedaṃ sīlaṃ. Ettakanti etaṃ paramaṃ, na ito bhiyyo. Catupārisuddhisīlanti maggassa sambhārabhūtaṃ lokiyacatupārisuddhisīlaṃ. Cittekaggatā samādhīti etthāpi eseva nayo. Yasmiṃ sīle ṭhatvāti yasmiṃ lokuttarakusalassa padaṭṭhānabhūte “pubbeva kho panassa kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ ājīvo suparisuddho hotī”ti (ma. ni. 3.431; kathā. 874) evaṃ vuttasīle patiṭṭhāya. Esoti maggaphalasamādhi. Paribhāvitoti tena sīlena sabbaso bhāvito sambhāvito. Mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃsoti maggasamādhi tāva sāmaññaphalehi mahapphalo, vaṭṭadukkhavūpasamena mahānisaṃso. Itaro paṭippassaddhippahānena mahapphalo, nibbutisukhuppattiyā mahānisaṃso. Yamhi samādhimhi [P 2.0175] ṭhatvāti yasmiṃ lokuttarakusalassa [V 2.0121] padaṭṭhānabhūte pādakajjhānasamādhimhi ceva vuṭṭhānagāminisamādhimhi ca ṭhatvā. Sāti maggaphalapaññā. Tena paribhāvitāti tena yathāvuttasamādhinā sabbaso bhāvitā paribhāvitā. Mahapphalamahānisaṃsatā samādhimhi vuttanayena veditabbā. Api ca te bojjhaṅgamaggaṅgajhānaṅgappabhedahetutāya mahapphalā sattadakkhiṇeyyapuggalavibhāgahetutāya [M 2.0136] mahānisaṃsāti veditabbā. Yāya paññāya ṭhatvāti yāyaṃ vipassanāpaññāyaṃ, samādhivipassanāpaññāyaṃ vā ṭhatvā. Samathayānikassa hi samādhisahagatāpi paññā maggādhigamāya visesapaccayo hotiyeva. Sammadevāti suṭṭhuyeva yathā āsavānaṃ lesopi nāvasissati, evaṃ sabbaso āsavehi vimuccati. Aggamaggakkhaṇañhi sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

142. “Because of the nearness of his final extinguishment” means that it is said because his final extinguishment would occur in about a year and a few more months. “This very thing” refers to the same as “such is virtue” and so forth—here, the word “such” conveys both manner and measure, taken together as “virtue of such a kind, virtue of this much.” “Virtue of such a kind” means virtue of such a classification. “This much” means this is the maximum, not more than this. “Fourfold purified virtue” refers to the mundane fourfold purified virtue, which serves as the foundation for the path. “Concentration is one-pointedness of mind” follows the same principle here. “Having stood in which virtue” means having established oneself in that virtue which is the basis for supramundane wholesome states, as stated: “Before that, his bodily action, verbal action, and livelihood were thoroughly purified” (MN 3.431; Kathā 874). “This” refers to the concentration of the path and fruition. “Developed” means fully developed and cultivated by that virtue. “It is of great fruit, of great benefit” means the path concentration is greatly fruitful with the fruits of recluseship, and of great benefit in the calming of the suffering of the cycle. The other (fruition concentration) is greatly fruitful through the pacification and abandonment of defilements, and of great benefit in the arising of the bliss of nibbāna. “Having stood in which concentration” means having stood in that concentration which is the basis for supramundane wholesome states, namely the foundational absorption concentration and the concentration leading to emergence. “That” refers to the wisdom of the path and fruition. “Developed by that” means fully developed and cultivated by that aforementioned concentration. Its great fruitfulness and great benefit should be understood in the manner described for concentration. Moreover, they are to be understood as greatly fruitful for being the cause of the classification of the factors of enlightenment, path factors, and absorption factors, and of great benefit for being the cause of the distinction of the seven kinds of persons worthy of offerings. “Having stood in which wisdom” means having stood in that wisdom, whether insight wisdom or the wisdom of serenity and insight. For one following the path of serenity, even wisdom accompanied by concentration serves as a special condition for attaining the path. “Perfectly” means quite perfectly—so thoroughly that not even a trace of the taints remains; thus one is completely liberated from the taints. This is said with reference to the moment of the supreme path.

143. Lokiyatthasaddānaṃ viya abhiranta-saddassa siddhi daṭṭhabbā. Abhirantaṃ abhirataṃ abhiratīti hi atthato ekaṃ. Abhiranta-saddo cāyaṃ abhirucipariyāyo, na assādapariyāyo. Assādavasena hi katthaci vasantassa assādavatthuvigamena siyā tassa tattha anabhirati, yadidaṃ khīṇāsavānaṃ natthi, pageva buddhānanti āha “buddhānaṃ…pe… natthī”ti. Abhirativasena katthaci vasitvā tadabhāvato aññattha gamanaṃ nāma buddhānaṃ natthi. Veneyyavinayanatthaṃ pana katthaci vasitvā tasmiṃ siddhe veneyyavinayanatthameva tato aññattha gacchanti, ayamettha yathāruci. Āyāmāti ettha ā-saddo “āgacchā”ti iminā samānatthoti āha “ehi yāmā”ti. Ayāmāti pana pāṭhe a-kāro nipātamattaṃ. Santikāvacarattā theraṃ ālapati, na pana tadā satthu santike vasantānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhāvato. Aparicchinnagaṇano hi tadā bhagavato santike bhikkhusaṅgho[P 2.0176]. Tenāha “mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhi”nti. Ambalaṭṭhikāgamananti ambalaṭṭhikāgamanapaṭisaṃyuttapāṭhamāha. Pāṭaligamaneti etthāpi eseva nayo. Uttānameva anantaraṃ, heṭṭhā ca saṃvaṇṇitarūpattā.

143. The derivation of the word “delighted” should be understood like that of worldly terms. For in meaning, “delighted” (abhiranta), “delighted” (abhirata), and “delight” (abhirati) are one. This word “delighted” is a synonym for inclination, not a synonym for enjoyment. For one who dwells somewhere due to enjoyment might become dissatisfied there when the object of enjoyment disappears—but this does not apply to the arahants, let alone the Buddhas, as it is said: “For the Buddhas… there is none.” There is no case where the Buddhas, having dwelled somewhere out of delight, would leave for elsewhere due to the absence of that delight. However, for the sake of training those to be guided, they may dwell in a place and, once that purpose is fulfilled, depart elsewhere for the very same purpose of training those to be guided—this is according to their inclination.
