In “Let us go” (āyāma), the prefix “ā-” has the same meaning as “come” (āgaccha), hence it is said, “Come, let us go.” In the variant reading “ayāma,” the “a-” is merely a particle. He addresses the elder because he is nearby, not because there was an absence of monks in the presence of the Teacher at that time. For the community of monks around the Blessed One at that time was of an uncountable number. Hence it is said, “together with a great community of monks.” “The going to Ambalaṭṭhikā” refers to the passage connected with the going to Ambalaṭṭhikā. “In the going to Pāṭaligāma” follows the same principle. What follows is clear, as its nature has been explained below.

Sāriputtasīhanādavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Lion's Roar of Sāriputta

145. “Āyasmā sāriputto”tiādi pāṭhajātaṃ. Sampasādanīyeti sampasādanīyasutte (dī. ni. 3.141) vitthāritaṃ porāṇaṭṭhakathāyaṃ, tasmā mayampi tattheva naṃ atthato vitthārayissāmāti adhippāyo.

145. “The Venerable Sāriputta” and so forth is the textual passage. Regarding the Sampasādanīya, it is elaborated in the ancient commentary on the Sampasādanīya Sutta (DN 28); therefore, our intention is that we too will explain its meaning in detail there.

Dussīlaādīnavavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Dangers of Immorality

148. Āgantvā [V 2.0122] vasanti ettha āgantukāti āvasatho, tadeva agāranti āha “āvasathāgāranti āgantukānaṃ āvasathageha”nti. Dvinnaṃ [M 2.0137] rājūnanti licchavirājamagadharājūnaṃ. Sahāyakāti sevakā. Kulānīti kuṭumbike. Santhatanti santhari, sabbaṃ santhari sabbasanthari, taṃ sabbasanthariṃ. Bhāvanapuṃsakaniddeso cāyaṃ. Tenāha “yathā sabbaṃ santhataṃ hoti, eva”nti.

148. Because guests come and stay here, it is an `āvasatha`. That very building is an `agāra`; hence, it is said: '`āvasathāgāra` means a guest house.' 'Of the two kings' means of the Licchavi king and the Magadha king. '`Sahāyakā`' means attendants. '`Kulāni`' means householders. '`Santhataṃ`' means spread. '`Sabbaṃ santhari`' is 'completely spread,' and that is '`sabbasanthariṃ`.' This is a designation as a neuter abstract noun. Therefore, it is said: 'just as everything is spread out, so...'

149. Dussīloti ettha du-saddo abhāvattho “duppañño”tiādīsu (ma. ni. 1.449; a. ni. 5.10) viya, na garahatthoti āha “asīlo nissīlo”ti. Bhinnasaṃvaroti ettha yo samādinnasīlo kenaci kāraṇena sīlabhedaṃ patto, so tāva bhinnasaṃvaro hoti. Yo pana sabbena sabbaṃ asamādinnasīlo ācārahīno, so kathaṃ bhinnasaṃvaro nāma hotīti? Sopi sādhusamācārassa parihāniyassa bheditattā bhinnasaṃvaro eva nāma. Vissaṭṭhasaṃvaro saṃvararahitoti hi vuttaṃ hoti.

149. Here, in ‘dussīlo,’ the prefix ‘du-’ signifies absence, as in words like ‘duppañño,’ and is not pejorative; hence, it is said: ‘asīlo,’ ‘nissīlo.’ As for ‘bhinnasaṃvaro,’ one who, having undertaken the precepts, has for some reason arrived at a breach of virtue, is called ‘bhinnasaṃvaro.’ But how can someone who has not undertaken the precepts at all, being devoid of good conduct, be called ‘bhinnasaṃvaro’? Even that person is indeed called ‘bhinnasaṃvaro’ because good conduct has been lost and broken. For this means one who has cast off restraint, one who is devoid of restraint.

Taṃ taṃ sippaṭṭhānaṃ. Māghātakāleti “mā ghātetha pāṇino”ti evaṃ māghātāti ghosanaṃ ghositadivase.

That particular skill. '`Māghātakāle`' means on the day the proclamation '`mā ghātā`'—that is, 'Do not kill living beings'—was announced.

Abbhuggacchati pāpako kittisaddo.

An evil report rises up.

Ajjhāsayena maṅku hotiyeva vippaṭisāribhāvato.

Due to their underlying tendency, they are indeed troubled, because of remorse.

Tassāti [P 2.0177] dussīlassa. Samādāya pavattiṭṭhānanti uṭṭhāya samuṭṭhāya katakāraṇaṃ. Āpāthaṃ āgacchatīti taṃ manaso upaṭṭhāti. Ummīletvā idhalokanti ummīlanakāle attano puttadārādidassanavasena idha lokaṃ passati. Nimīletvā paralokanti nimīlanakāle gatinimittupaṭṭhānavasena paralokaṃ passati. Tenāha “cattāro apāyā”tiādi. Pañcamapadanti “kāyassa bhedā”tiādinā vutto pañcamo ādīnavakoṭṭhāso.

‘Tassa’ refers to the immoral one. ‘Samādāya pavattiṭṭhānaṃ’ means the cause of the action, undertaken and instigated. ‘Āpāthaṃ āgacchati’ means it occurs to the mind. ‘Ummīletvā idhalokaṃ’ means at the time of opening the eyes, one sees this world by seeing one’s children, spouse, and so on. ‘Nimīletvā paralokaṃ’ means at the time of closing the eyes, one sees the next world through the appearance of the signs of one's destination. Hence it is said, ‘the four woeful states,’ etc. ‘Pañcamapadaṃ’ refers to the fifth drawback, the section beginning with ‘after the breakup of the body,’ etc.

Sīlavantaānisaṃsavaṇṇanā

The Description of the Benefits of the Virtuous

150. Vuttavipariyāyenāti vuttāya ādīnavakathāya vipariyāyena. “Appamatto taṃ taṃ kasivāṇijjādiṃ [V 2.0123] yathākālaṃ sampādetuṃ sakkotī”tiādinā “pāsaṃsaṃ sīlamassa atthīti sīlavā. Sīlasampannoti sīlena samannāgato. Sampannasīlo”ti evamādikaṃ pana atthavacanaṃ sukaranti anāmaṭṭhaṃ.

150. ‘Vuttavipariyāyena’ means in the opposite way to the talk on dangers that was given. By the passage beginning, ‘Being diligent, one is able to accomplish this or that farming, trade, and so on, at the appropriate time...’ And further, such explanations of meaning as: ‘`sīlavā` (virtuous) means one who has praiseworthy virtue’; ‘`sīlasampanno` means endowed with virtue’; ‘`sampannasīlo` (one of accomplished virtue)’ are easy to understand and so are not discussed.

151. Pāḷimuttakāyāti [M 2.0138] saṅgītianāruḷhāya dhammikathāya. Tatthevāti āvasathāgāre eva.

151. ‘Pāḷimuttakāya’ means by a Dhamma talk not included in the recitations. ‘Tattheva’ means right there in the guest house.

Pāṭaliputtanagaramāpanavaṇṇanā

The Description of the Founding of the City of Pāṭaliputta

152. Issariyamattāyāti issariyappamāṇena, issariyena ceva vittūpakaraṇena cāti evaṃ vā attho daṭṭhabbo. Upabhogūpakaraṇānipi hi loke “mattā”ti vuccanti. Pāṭaligāmaṃ nagaraṃ katvāti pubbe “pāṭaligāmo”ti laddhanāmaṃ ṭhānaṃ idāni nagaraṃ katvā. Māpentīti patiṭṭhāpenti. Āyamukhapacchindanatthanti āyadvārānaṃ upacchedanāya. “Sahassasevā”ti vā pāṭho, sahassaso eva. Tenāha “ekekavaggavasena sahassaṃ sahassaṃ hutvā”ti. Gharavatthūnīti gharapatiṭṭhāpanaṭṭhānāni. Cittāni namantīti taṃtaṃdevatānubhāvena tattha tattheva cittāni namanti vatthuvijjāpāṭhakānaṃ, yattha yattha tāhi vatthūni pariggahitāni. Sippānubhāvenāti sippānugatavijjānubhāvena. Nāgaggāhoti nāgānaṃ nivāsappariggaho. Sesadvayesupi eseva nayo. Pāsāṇoti appalakkhaṇapāsāṇo. Khāṇukoti yo koci khāṇuko[P 2.0178]. Sippaṃ jappitvā tādisaṃ sārambhaṭṭhānaṃ pariharitvā anārambhe ṭhāne tāhi vatthupariggāhikāhi devatāhi saddhiṃ mantayamānā viya taṃtaṃgehāni māpenti upadesadānavasena. Nesanti vatthuvijjāpāṭhakānaṃ, sabbāsaṃ devatānaṃ. Maṅgalaṃ vaḍḍhāpessantīti maṅgalaṃ brūhessanti. Paṇḍitadassanādīni hi uttamamaṅgalāni. Tenāha “atha maya”ntiādi.

152. ‘Issariyamattāya’ means by the extent of sovereignty, or the meaning should be understood as by sovereignty and by wealth and equipment. For in the world, even the means of enjoyment are called ‘mattā.’ ‘Pāṭaligāmaṃ nagaraṃ katvā’ means having made the place formerly named ‘Pāṭaligāma’ into a city now. ‘Māpenti’ means they establish. ‘Āyamukhapacchindanatthaṃ’ means for the purpose of cutting off the avenues of income. Or the reading is ‘sahassasevā,’ meaning ‘a thousand each.’ Hence it is said, ‘group by group, a thousand each.’ ‘Gharavatthūni’ means the sites for establishing houses. ‘Cittāni namanti’ means that, by the influence of the respective deities, the minds of the geomancers incline to those very spots where the sites had been selected by those deities. ‘Sippānubhāvena’ means by the influence of the knowledge associated with their craft. ‘Nāgaggāho’ means the area designated for the dwelling of elephants. The same method applies to the other two. ‘Pāsāṇo’ refers to an unremarkable stone. ‘Khāṇuko’ means any kind of stump. Having muttered their craft, having avoided such a place of conflict, in a place free of conflict, they lay out the respective houses by way of giving instructions, as if consulting with those deities who have taken possession of the sites. ‘Nesaṃ’ refers to the geomancers and to all the deities. ‘Maṅgalaṃ vaḍḍhāpessanti’ means they will augment what is auspicious. For seeing the wise and so on are the highest auspicious signs. Hence it is said, ‘then we,’ etc.

Saddo abbhuggacchati avayavadhammena samudāyassa apadisitabbato yathā “alaṅkato devadatto”ti.

The sound arises because the whole is designated by means of a quality of its parts, as in ‘Devadatta is adorned.’

Ariyakamanussānanti ariyadesavāsimanussānaṃ. Rāsivasenevāti “sahassaṃ satasahassa”ntiādinā rāsivaseneva, appakassa pana bhaṇḍassa kayavikkayo aññatthāpi labbhatevāti “rāsivasenevā”ti vuttaṃ. Vāṇijāya patho pavattiṭṭhānanti vaṇippathoti purimavikappe attho dutiyavikappe pana vāṇijānaṃ patho pavattiṭṭhānanti, vaṇippathoti imamatthaṃ dassento [V 2.0124] “vāṇijānaṃ vasanaṭṭhāna”nti āha. Bhaṇḍapuṭe bhindanti mocenti etthāti puṭabhedananti ayamettha atthoti āha “bhaṇḍapuṭe…pe… vuttaṃ hotī”ti.

‘Ariyakamanussānaṃ’ means of people living in noble regions. ‘Rāsivaseneva’ means by way of a heap only, as in by the thousand or hundred thousand. Since the buying and selling of a small amount of goods can also be found elsewhere, it is said ‘by way of a heap only.’ In the first interpretation, `vaṇippatho` means 'the path and place of business for trade.' In the second interpretation, however, it means 'the path and place of business for merchants'; showing this meaning of `vaṇippatho`, he said: 'the dwelling place of merchants.' '`Puṭabhedanaṃ`' is so called because 'they break open or release the bundles of goods here.' This is the meaning here, as he said: 'bundles of goods... it is said.'

Ca-kārattho [M 2.0139] samuccayattho vā-saddo.

The word `vā` has the meaning of the particle `ca`, that is, the meaning of accumulation.

153. Kāḷakaṇṇī sattāti attanā kaṇhadhammabahulatāya paresañca kaṇhavipākānatthanibbattinimittatāya “kāḷakaṇṇī”ti laddhanāmā parūpaddavakarā appesakkhasattā. Tanti bhagavantaṃ. Pubbaṇhasamayanti pubbaṇhe ekaṃ samayaṃ. Gāmappavisananīhārenāti gāmappavesana nivasanākārena. Kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ katvāti cīvaraṃ pārupitvā, pattaṃ hatthena gahetvāti attho.

153. ‘Kāḷakaṇṇī sattā’ refers to beings of little influence who cause trouble to others, so named because of their own abundance of dark qualities and because they are a sign for the production of disadvantageous, dark results for others. ‘Taṃ’ refers to the Blessed One. ‘Pubbaṇhasamayaṃ’ means one morning. ‘Gāmappavisananīhārena’ means with the manner of entering the village and dressing. ‘Kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ katvā’ means having put on the robe and taken the bowl in hand.

Etthāti [P 2.0179] etasmiṃ vā sakappitappadese. Saññateti sammadeva saññate susaṃvutakāyavācācitte.

‘Ettha’ means in this very place or in a place determined by oneself. ‘Saññate’ means rightly restrained, with body, speech, and mind well-controlled.

Pattiṃ dadeyyāti attanā pasutaṃ puññaṃ tāsaṃ devatānaṃ anuppadajjeyya. “Pūjitā”tiādīsu tadeva pattidānaṃ pūjā, anāgate eva upaddave ārakkhasaṃvidhānaṃ paṭipūjā. “Yebhuyyena ñātimanussā ñātipetānaṃ pattidānādinā pūjanamānanādīni karonti ime pana aññātakāpi samānā tathā karonti, tasmā nesaṃ sakkaccaṃ ārakkhā saṃvidhātabbā”ti aññamaññaṃ sampavāretvā devatā tattha ussukkaṃ āpajjantīti dassento “ime”tiādimāha. Balikammakaraṇaṃ mānanaṃ, sampati uppannaparissayaharaṇaṃ paṭimānanti dassetuṃ “ete”tiādi vuttaṃ.

‘Pattiṃ dadeyyā’ means one should dedicate the merit one has accumulated to those deities. In phrases like ‘Pūjitā,’ that very dedication of merit is worship, and preparing a protective arrangement for future dangers is counter-worship. To show that the deities, having encouraged one another by saying, ‘For the most part, human relatives perform acts of worship, honor, and so on for their departed kin through the dedication of merit, but these people, though they are strangers, do likewise; therefore, protection should be carefully arranged for them,’ become diligent there, he said the passage beginning ‘ime.’ To show that making an offering is an act of honor, and that removing a presently arisen danger is a counter-honor, the passage beginning ‘ete’ was spoken.

Sundarāni passatīti sundarāni iṭṭhāni eva passati, na aniṭṭhāni.

‘Sundarāni passati’ means one sees only beautiful, desirable things, not undesirable things.

154. Āṇiyo koṭṭetvāti lahuke dārudaṇḍe gahetvā kavāṭaphalake viya aññamaññaṃ sambandhe kātuṃ āṇiyo koṭṭetvā. Nāvāsaṅkhepena kataṃ uḷumpaṃ, veḷunaḷādike saṅgharitvā valliādīhi kalāpavasena bandhitvā kattabbaṃ kullaṃ.

154. ‘Āṇiyo koṭṭetvā’ means having taken light wooden sticks and struck pegs to connect them to one another, like door panels. A `kulla` is a raft, a simple boat-like float, to be made by assembling bamboo, reeds, and so on, and binding them into bundles with vines and so on.

Udakaṭṭhānassetaṃ adhivacananti yathāvuttassa yassa kassaci udakaṭṭhānassa etaṃ “aṇṇava”nti adhivacanaṃ, samuddassevāti adhippāyo. Saranti idha nadī adhippetā sarati sandatīti [V 2.0125] katvā. Gambhīravitthatanti agādhaṭṭhena gambhīraṃ, sakalalokattayabyāpitāya vitthataṃ. Visajjāti anāsajja appatvā. Pallalāni tesaṃ ataraṇato. Vināyeva kullenāti īdisaṃ udakaṃ kullena īdisena vinā eva tiṇṇā medhāvino janā, taṇhāsaraṃ pana ariyamaggasaṅkhātaṃ setuṃ katvā nittiṇṇāti yojanā.

‘Udakaṭṭhānassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ’ means that the term ‘aṇṇava’ is a designation for any place of water as described, the intention being the ocean itself. ‘Saranti’ here refers to a river, understood as that which flows and streams. ‘Gambhīravitthataṃ’ means deep in the sense of being unfathomable, and vast by pervading the entire threefold world. ‘Visajjā’ means without getting stuck, without reaching. ‘Pallalāni’ refers to puddles, because they are not crossed. ‘Vināyeva kullena’ means wise people cross such water even without such a raft, but they have completely crossed the flood of craving by making the Noble Path, which is called a bridge, the means—this is the connection.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the first recitation section is concluded.

Ariyasaccakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Noble Truths

155. Mahāpanādassa [P 2.0180][M 2.0140] rañño. Pāsādakoṭiyaṃ katagāmoti pāsādassa patitathupikāya patiṭṭhitaṭṭhāne niviṭṭhagāmo. Ariyabhāvakarānanti ye paṭivijjhanti, tesaṃ ariyabhāvakarānaṃ nimittassa kattubhāvūpacāravaseneva vuttaṃ. Tacchāvipallāsabhūtabhāvena saccānaṃ. Anubodho pubbabhāgiyaṃ ñāṇaṃ, paṭivedho maggañāṇena abhisamayo, tattha yasmā anubodhapubbako paṭivedho anubodhena vinā na hoti, anubodhopi ekacco paṭivedhena sambandho, tadubhayābhāvahetukañca vaṭṭeva saṃsaraṇaṃ, tasmā vuttaṃ pāḷiyaṃ “ananubodhā…pe… tumhākañcā”ti. Paṭisandhiggahaṇavasena bhavato bhavantarūpagamanaṃ sandhāvanaṃ, aparāparaṃ cavanupapajjanavasena sañcaraṇaṃ saṃsaraṇanti āha “bhavato”tiādi. Sandhāvitasaṃsaritapadānaṃ kammasādhanataṃ sandhāyāha “mayā ca tumhehi cā”ti paṭhamavikappe. Dutiyavikappe pana bhāvasādhanataṃ hadaye katvā “mamañceva tumhākañcā”ti yathārutavaseneva vuttaṃ. Nayanasamatthāti pāpanasamatthā, dīgharajjunā baddhasakuṇaṃ viya rajjuhattho puriso desantaraṃ taṇhārajjunā baddhaṃ sattasantānaṃ abhisaṅkhāro bhavantaraṃ neti etāyāti bhavanetti, taṇhā, sā ariyamaggasatthena suṭṭhu hatā chinnāti bhavanettisamūhatā.

155. Of King Mahāpanāda. ‘A village made at the palace-pinnacle’ means the village established at the place where the palace's fallen pinnacle rested. ‘Those who make the noble state’ refers to those who penetrate them; this is said by way of a figurative attribution of agency to the sign of the noble state. ‘Of the truths’ is because of their true and undistorted nature. ‘Initial understanding’ is preliminary knowledge; ‘penetration’ is realization, the full understanding by means of path knowledge. Herein, because penetration is preceded by initial understanding and does not occur without it, and some initial understanding is also connected with penetration, and because the wandering in the round of existence is caused by the absence of both, it is therefore said in the Pāli: “Through not understanding… for you and for me.” ‘Running through’ means passing from one existence to another by way of rebirth-linking; ‘wandering’ means moving repeatedly by way of dying and arising—thus it is said, “from existence,” and so on. Considering the words for running through and wandering to be agentive, it says, “by me and by you” in the first alternative. In the second alternative, however, taking them in an abstract sense, it says, “of me and of you,” according to the wording of the text. ‘Capable of leading’ means capable of bringing. Just as a bird tied by a long string is led by a man holding the string to another place, so a volitional formation leads the continuum of a being, tied by the string of craving, to another existence—thus it is called ‘the leader to existence,’ which is craving. It is well destroyed, cut off by the sword of the noble path—thus the leader to existence is eradicated.

Anāvattidhammasambodhiparāyaṇavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Discourse on the State of Non-Returning and Being Bound for Supreme Enlightenment

156. Dve gāmā “nātikā”ti evaṃ laddhanāmo, ña-kārassa cāyaṃ na-kārādesena niddeso “animittā na nāyare”tiādīsu (visuddhi. 1.174; jā. aṭṭha. 2.2.34) viya. Tenāha “ñātigāmake”ti[V 2.0126]. Giñjakā vuccanti iṭṭhakā, giñjakāhi eva kato āvasathoti giñjakāvasatho[P 2.0181]. So kira āvāso yathā sudhāparikammena sampayojanaṃ natthi, evaṃ iṭṭhakāhi eva cinitvā chādetvā kato. Tena vuttaṃ “iṭṭhakāmaye āvasathe”ti. Tulādaṇḍakavāṭaphalakāni pana dārumayāneva.

156. Two villages are called ‘Nātikā’—thus they are named. Here, the letter ‘ñ’ is indicated by substitution with the letter ‘n’, as in ‘animittā na nāyare’ and so on. Therefore, it is said, ‘in the Ñātika village.’ ‘Giñjakā’ are called bricks; a dwelling made of bricks is called a giñjakāvasatha. It is said that this dwelling was constructed by merely piling up and covering with bricks, such that there was no use for plasterwork. Hence, it is said, ‘in the brick-made dwelling.’ However, the beams, door-bars, and door-panels were made of wood.

157. Oraṃ vuccati kāmadhātu, paccayabhāvena taṃ oraṃ bhajantīti orambhāgiyāni, orambhāgassa vā hitāni orambhāgiyāni. Tenāha “heṭṭhābhāgiyāna”ntiādi. Tīhi maggehīti heṭṭhimehi tīhi maggehi. Tehi [M 2.0141] pahātabbatāya hi nesaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ orambhāgiyatā. Orambhañjiyāni vā orambhāgiyāni vuttāni niruttinayena. Idāni byatirekamukhena nesaṃ orambhāgiyabhāvaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “tatthā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Vikkhambhitāni samatthatāvighātena puthujjanānaṃ, samucchinnāni sabbaso abhāvena ariyānaṃ rūpārūpabhavūpapattiyā vibandhāya na hontīti vuttaṃ “avikkhambhitāni asamucchinnānī”ti. Nibbattavasenāti paṭisandhiggahaṇavasena. Gantuṃ na denti mahaggatagāmikammāyūhanassa vinibandhanato. Sakkāyadiṭṭhiādīni tīṇi saṃyojanāni kāmacchandabyāpādā viya mahaggatūpapattiyā avinibandhabhūtānipi kāmabhavūpapattiyā visesapaccayattā tattha mahaggatabhave nibbattampi tannibbattihetukammaparikkhaye kāmabhavūpapattipaccayatāya mahaggatabhavato ānetvā puna idheva kāmabhave eva nibbattāpenti, tasmā sabbānipi pañcapi saṃyojanāni orambhāgiyāni eva. Paṭisandhivasena anāgamanasabhāvāti paṭisandhiggahaṇavasena tasmā lokā idha na āgamanasabhāvā. Buddhadassanatheradassanadhammassavanānaṃ panatthāyassa āgamanaṃ anivāritaṃ.

157. The lower part is called the desire realm. Because they pertain to that lower part by way of being a condition, they are called lower-part fetters; or, what is conducive to the lower part is called lower-part fetters. Hence it is said, “belonging to the lower part,” etc. ‘By the three paths’ means by the lower three paths. For it is because these fetters are to be abandoned by them that they are called lower-part fetters. Alternatively, by way of etymology, they are called orambhāgiyāni because they are to be broken (orambhañjiyāni) in the lower part. Now, to clarify their nature as pertaining to the lower part by way of contrast, it is said, “therein,” etc. It is said “not suppressed, not eradicated” because those that are suppressed for worldlings by the obstruction of their capability, and those that are eradicated for noble ones by their complete absence, do not form an obstruction to rebirth in the form or formless realms. ‘By way of arising’ means by way of taking rebirth-linking. They do not allow one to go, because they obstruct the accumulation of kamma leading to the sublime states. The three fetters—identity view, etc.—like sensual desire and ill-will, though not obstructing rebirth in sublime states, are specific conditions for rebirth in the desire realm. Even if one is reborn in a sublime state, when the kamma that caused that rebirth is exhausted, they bring one back from that sublime state and cause rebirth right here in the desire realm. Therefore, all five fetters are indeed lower-part fetters. ‘Of a nature not to return by way of rebirth’ means that by way of taking rebirth-linking, they are of a nature not to return here from that world. However, their coming for the sake of seeing the Buddha, seeing the elders, or hearing the Dhamma is not prevented.

Kadāci karahaci uppattiyā saviraḷākāratā [P 2.0182] pariyuṭṭhānamandatāya abahalatāti dvedhāpi tanubhāvo. Abhiṇhanti bahuso. Bahalabahalāti tibbatibbā. Yattha uppajjanti, taṃ santānaṃ maddantā, pharantā, sādhentā, andhakāraṃ karontā uppajjanti, dvīhi pana maggehi pahīnattā tanukatanukā mandamandā uppajjanti. “Puttadhītaro hontī”ti idaṃ akāraṇaṃ. Tathā hi aṅgapaccaṅgaparāmasanamattenapi te honti. Idanti “rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā”ti idaṃ vacanaṃ. Bhavatanukavasenāti appakabhavavasena. Tanti mahāsivattherassa vacanaṃ paṭikkhittanti sambandho. Ye bhavā ariyānaṃ labbhanti, te paripuṇṇalakkhaṇabhavā eva. Ye na labbhanti, tattha kīdisaṃ taṃ bhavatanukaṃ, tasmā ubhayathāpi bhavatanukassa asambhavo evāti dassetuṃ “sotāpannassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhame bhave bhavatanukaṃ natthi aṭṭhamasseva bhavassa sabbasseva abhāvato. Sesesupi eseva nayo.

The attenuation is twofold: infrequency, from arising only sometimes, rarely; and lack of strength, from the weakness of the obsession. ‘Frequently’ means often. ‘Very strong’ means very intense. Wherever they arise, they arise crushing, pervading, mastering, and creating darkness in that mental continuum. However, because they have been abandoned by two paths, they arise very attenuated and very weakly. “‘Let there be sons and daughters’—this is not the reason. For they come to be even by the mere touching of limbs and minor limbs.” ‘This’ refers to this statement: “the attenuation of lust, hatred, and delusion.” ‘Due to the attenuation of existence’ means due to the fewness of existences. The connection is that this refutes the statement of the Elder Mahāsīva. Those existences that are obtained by noble ones are existences with fully complete characteristics. For those that are not obtained, what kind of attenuated existence could there be? Therefore, to show that an attenuated existence is impossible in either case, it is said, “For a stream-enterer,” etc. In the eighth existence, there is no attenuated existence, because the eighth existence is completely absent. The same principle applies to the remaining cases.

Kāmāvacaralokaṃ [V 2.0127] sandhāya vuttaṃ itarassa lokassa vasena tathā vattuṃ asakkuṇeyyattā. Yo hi sakadāgāmī devamanussalokesu vomissakavasena nibbattati, sopi kāmabhavavaseneva paricchinditabbo. Bhagavatā ca kāmaloke ṭhatvā “sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā”ti [M 2.0142] vuttaṃ, “imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā”ti ca iminā pañcasu sakadāgāmīsu cattāro vajjetvā ekova gahito. Ekacco hi idha sakadāgāmiphalaṃ patvā idheva parinibbāyati, ekacco idha patvā devaloke parinibbāyati, ekacco devaloke patvā tattheva parinibbāyati, ekacco devaloke patvā idhūpapajjitvā parinibbāyati, ime cattāro idha na labbhanti. Yo pana idha patvā devaloke yāvatāyukaṃ vasitvā puna idhūpapajjitvā parinibbāyati, ayaṃ idha adhippeto. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana imaṃ lokanti kāmabhavo adhippetoti imamatthaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “sace hī”tiādinā aññaṃyeva catukkaṃ dassitaṃ.

This was said with reference to the sensuous-sphere world, because it is not possible to speak thus with regard to the other worlds. A once-returner who is reborn in the worlds of gods and humans in alternating existences should be defined solely by their connection to sensuous existence. The Blessed One, while residing in the sensuous world, said, “having come back to this world only once,” and by this saying, “having come back to this world,” among the five types of once-returners, four are excluded, and only one is taken. For one, having attained the fruit of once-returning here, attains final Nibbāna right here. Another, having attained it here, attains final Nibbāna in the deva world. Another, having attained it in the deva world, attains final Nibbāna right there. Another, having attained it in the deva world, is reborn here and then attains final Nibbāna—these four are not included here. But the one who, having attained it here, dwells in the deva world for the duration of their life and then is reborn here again before attaining final Nibbāna—this is the one intended here. In the commentary, however, “this world” is understood to mean the sensuous existence. To clarify this point, yet another set of four is shown beginning with “if indeed.”

Catūsu [P 2.0183] …pe… sabhāvoti attho apāyagamanīyānaṃ pāpadhammānaṃ sabbaso pahīnattā. Dhammaniyāmenāti maggadhammaniyāmena. Niyato uparimaggādhigamassa avassaṃbhāvibhāvato. Tenāha “sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti.

In four... and so on... 'By nature' means because evil qualities leading to the lower realms have been completely abandoned in every way. 'By the fixed order of phenomena' means by the fixed order of the path-phenomenon. 'Certain' because of the inevitability of attaining the higher path. Therefore, it is said: 'Destined for enlightenment.'

Dhammādāsadhammapariyāyavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Dhamma Mirror

158. Tesaṃ tesaṃ ñāṇagatinti tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ “asuko sotāpanno, asuko sakadāgāmī”tiādinā taṃtaṃñāṇādhigamanaṃ. Ñāṇūpapattiṃ ñāṇābhisamparāyanti tato parampi “niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissatī”tiādinā ca ñāṇasahitaṃ uppattipaccayabhāvaṃ. Olokentassa ñāṇacakkhunā pekkhantassa kāyakilamathova, na tena kāci veneyyānaṃ atthasiddhīti adhippāyo. Cittavihesāti cittakhedo, sā kilesūpasaṃhitattā buddhānaṃ natthi. Ādīyati ālokīyati attā etenāti ādāsaṃ, dhammabhūtaṃ ādāsaṃ dhammādāsaṃ, ariyamaggañāṇassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ, tena ariyasāvakā catūsu ariyasaccesu viddhastasammohattā attānampi yāthāvato ñatvā yāthāvato byākareyya, tappakāsanato pana dhammapariyāyassa suttassa dhammādāsatā veditabbā. Yena dhammādāsenāti idha pana maggadhammameva vadati.

158. 'The course of knowledge for those respective beings' refers to the attainment of specific knowledge by those beings, such as 'this one is a stream-enterer, this one is a once-returner,' and so on. 'Knowledge arising, knowledge in the future' means that beyond that, there is the state of being a condition for arising accompanied by knowledge, such as 'he is destined for enlightenment, having come to this world only once, he will make an end of suffering,' and so on. 'For one who looks, for one who sees with the eye of knowledge, there is only bodily fatigue'—the meaning is that no benefit is accomplished for those who are to be trained by that. 'Mental distress' means mental vexation; this does not exist for the Buddhas because it is associated with defilements. 'The self is taken up, is looked into by this,' thus it is a mirror. The mirror that is the Dhamma is the Dhamma-mirror. This is a designation for the knowledge of the noble path; by this, noble disciples, having dispelled delusion regarding the four noble truths, knowing themselves as they truly are, would declare themselves as they truly are. However, because it makes that known, the nature of being a Dhamma-mirror for this Dhamma discourse, this sutta, should be understood. 'By which Dhamma-mirror'—here, however, it speaks only of the path-Dhamma itself.

Avecca yāthāvato jānitvā tannimittauppannapasādo aveccapasādo, maggādhigamena uppannapasādo[V 2.0128], so pana yasmā pāsāṇapabbato viya niccalo, na ca kenaci kāraṇena vigacchati, tasmā vuttaṃ “acalena accutenā”ti.

Having understood and known as it truly is, the confidence arisen from that cause is unwavering confidence, the confidence arisen from the attainment of the path. Since it is unshaken like a rocky mountain and cannot be removed for any reason, therefore it is said, 'unshaken and unassailable.'

“Pañcasīlānī”ti [M 2.0143] gahaṭṭhavasenetaṃ vuttaṃ tehi ekantapariharaṇīyato. Ariyānaṃ pana sabbāni sīlāni kantāneva. Tenāha “sabbopi panettha saṃvaro labbhatiyevā”ti.

'The Five Precepts'—this is said in relation to householders, because these are to be completely observed by them. But for the Noble Ones, all precepts are indeed dear. Therefore, it is said, 'Here, indeed, all restraint is obtained.'

Sabbesanti [P 2.0184] sabbesaṃ ariyānaṃ. Sikkhāpadāvirodhenāti yathā bhūtarocanāpatti na hoti, evaṃ. Yuttaṭṭhāneti kātuṃ yuttaṭṭhāne.

`Sabbesaṃ` means 'of all noble ones'. 'By not conflicting with the training precepts' means in such a way that there is no offense of declaring a true attainment. 'In a suitable place' means in a place where it is suitable to do so.

Ambapālīgaṇikāvatthuvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of Ambapālī the Courtesan

161. Tadā kira vesālī iddhā phītā sabbaṅgasampannā ahosi vepullappattā, taṃ sandhāyāha “khandhake vuttanayena vesāliyā sampannabhāvo veditabbo”ti. Tasmiṃ kira bhikkhusaṅghe pañcasatamattā bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā ahesuṃ osannavīriyā ca. Tathā hi vakkhati “tattha kira ekacce bhikkhū osannavīriyā”tiādi (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.165). Satipaccupaṭṭhānatthanti tesaṃ satipaccupaṭṭhāpanatthaṃ. Saratīti kāyādike yathāsabhāvato ñāṇasampayuttāya satiyā anussarati upadhāreti. Sampajānātīti samaṃ pakārehi jānāti avabujjhati. Ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthāro pana parato satipaṭṭhānavaṇṇanāyaṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.373; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.106) āgamissati.

161. At that time, it is said, Vesālī was prosperous, thriving, complete in every way, and had attained great abundance. Referring to this, it is said, 'The prosperity of Vesālī should be understood according to the method stated in the Khandhaka.' In that Saṅgha of monks, it is said, there were about five hundred monks who were new, recently ordained, and of slackened energy. For so it will be said: 'There, it is said, some monks were of slackened energy,' and so on. 'For the purpose of establishing mindfulness' means for the purpose of establishing mindfulness for them. 'He remembers' means he recollects and attends to the body and so forth according to their true nature, with mindfulness accompanied by knowledge. 'He clearly knows' means he knows and understands rightly and in various ways. This is the summary here; the detailed explanation, however, will come later in the commentary on the Satipaṭṭhāna (Dī. Ni. Aṭṭha. 2.373; Ma. Ni. Aṭṭha. 1.106).

Sabbasaṅgāhakanti sarīragatassa ceva vatthālaṅkāragatassa cāti sabbassa nīlabhāvassa saṅgāhakaṃ vacanaṃ. Tassevāti nīlāti sabbasaṅgāhakavasena vuttaatthasseva. Vibhāgadassananti pabhedadassanaṃ. Yathā te licchavirājāno apītādivaṇṇā eva keci vilepanavasena pītādivaṇṇā khāyiṃsu, evaṃ anīlādivaṇṇā eva keci vilepanavasena nīlādivaṇṇā khāyiṃsūti vuttaṃ “na tesaṃ pakativaṇṇo nīlo”tiādi. Nīlo maṇi etesūti nīlamaṇi, indanīlamahānīlādinīlaratanavinaddhā alaṅkārā. Te kira suvaṇṇaviracite hi maṇiobhāsehi ekanīlā viya khāyanti. Nīlamaṇikhacitāti nīlaratanaparikkhittā. Nīlavatthaparikkhittāti nīlavatthanīlakampalaparikkhepā. Nīlavammikehīti nīlakaghaṭaparikkhittehi. Sabbapadesūti “pītā hontī”tiādisabbapadesu. Parivaṭṭesīti [P 2.0185] paṭighaṭṭesi. Āharanti imasmā rājapurisā balinti āhāro, tappattajanapadoti āha “sāhāranti sajanapada”nti. Aṅguliphoṭopi aṅguliyā cālanavaseneva [M 2.0144][V 2.0129] hotīti vuttaṃ “aṅguliṃ cālesu”nti. Ambakāyāti mātugāmena. Upacāravacanaṃ hetaṃ itthīsu, yadidaṃ “ambakā mātugāmo jananikā”ti.

'All-encompassing' means a statement encompassing the entire state of being blue, both that pertaining to the body and that pertaining to garments and ornaments. 'Of that very' means of the very meaning stated by way of being all-encompassing, namely 'blue'. 'Seeing distinctions' means seeing differences. Just as some Licchavi kings, though not of yellow and other colors by nature, appeared to be of yellow and other colors due to the application of ointments, so too, some who were not of blue and other colors by nature appeared to be of blue and other colors due to the application of ointments; thus it is said, 'Their natural color was not blue,' and so on. 'Blue gems are on them,' thus `nīlamaṇi`; ornaments adorned with indranīla, mahānīla, and other blue jewels. It is said that these, when set in gold, appeared uniformly blue due to the radiance of the gems. 'Inlaid with blue gems' means surrounded by blue jewels. 'Surrounded by blue garments' means enveloped in blue cloth and blue blankets. 'With blue `vammika`' means surrounded by blue water pots. 'In all passages' means in all passages such as 'they are yellow'. `Parivaṭṭesi` means `paṭighaṭṭesi` (he struck against). 'Royal officials bring tribute from this,' thus `āhāro` (revenue); meaning the district from which it is obtained, he said, '`sāhāra` means with its people'. 'Finger-snapping' also occurs by way of moving the finger; thus it is said, 'they moved their fingers'. 'By Ambakā' means by a woman. For this is a polite term for women, that is, `ambakā`, `mātugāmo`, `jananikā`.

Avalokethāti apavattitvā olokanaṃ oloketha. Taṃ pana apavattitvā olokanaṃ anu anu dassanaṃ hotīti āha “punappunaṃ passathā”ti. Upanethāti “yathāyaṃ licchavirājaparisā sobhātisayena yuttā, evaṃ tāvatiṃsaparisā”ti upanayaṃ karotha. Tenāha “tāvatiṃsehi samake katvā passathā”ti.

'Look at' means look without turning away. That looking without turning away is seeing again and again—thus he said, 'see again and again.' 'Compare' means make a comparison thus: 'just as this assembly of Licchavi kings is endowed with surpassing splendor, so too is the assembly of the Tāvatiṃsa devas.' Therefore, he said, 'having made them equal to the Tāvatiṃsa devas, see.'

“Upasaṃharatha bhikkhave licchaviparisaṃ tāvatiṃsasadisa”nti nayidaṃ nimittaggāhe niyojanaṃ, kevalaṃ pana dibbasampattisadisā etesaṃ rājūnaṃ issariyasampattīti anupubbikathāya saggasampattikathanaṃ viya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tesu pana bhikkhūsu ekaccānaṃ tattha nimittaggāhopi siyā, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “nimittaggāhe uyyojetī”ti. Hitakāmatāya tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yathā āyasmato nandassa hitakāmatāya saggasampattidassanaṃ. Tenāha “tatra kirā”tiādi. Osannavīriyāti sammāpaṭipattiyaṃ avasannavīriyā, ossaṭṭhavīriyā vāti attho. Aniccalakkhaṇavibhāvanatthanti tesaṃ rājūnaṃ vasena bhikkhūnaṃ aniccalakkhaṇavibhūtabhāvatthaṃ.

'Compare, monks, the assembly of the Licchavis to that of the Tāvatiṃsa gods'—this is not an instruction in grasping signs, but it should be regarded simply as a talk on heavenly attainment within the gradual discourse, to the effect that the lordly fortune of these kings is similar to divine fortune. However, for some of those monks, there might be a grasping of signs there; referring to that it was said, 'he urges them to grasp at signs.' This was out of a desire for the welfare of those monks, just as the venerable Nanda was shown heavenly attainment out of a desire for his welfare. Therefore, it is said, 'there indeed,' and so on. 'With slackened energy' means those whose energy has slackened in right practice, or whose energy is abandoned—this is the meaning. 'For the purpose of explaining the characteristic of impermanence' means for the purpose of the characteristic of impermanence becoming manifest to the monks by means of those kings.

Veḷuvagāmavassūpagamanavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on Entering the Rains Residence at Veḷuvagāma

163. Samīpe veḷuvagāmoti pubbaṇhaṃ vā sāyanhaṃ vā gantvā nivattanayogye āsannaṭṭhāne niviṭṭhā parivāragāmo. Saṅgammāti sammā gantvā. Assāti bhagavato.

163. 'Near Veḷuvagāma' means a surrounding village established in a nearby place suitable for going and returning in the morning or evening. `Saṅgamma` means having gone properly. `Assa` means 'of the Blessed One.'

164. Pharusoti kakkhaḷo, garutaroti attho. Visabhāgarogoti [P 2.0186] dhātuvisabhāgatāya samuṭṭhito bahalatararogo, na ābādhamattaṃ. Ñāṇena paricchinditvāti vedanānaṃ khaṇikataṃ, dukkhataṃ, attasuññatañca yāthāvato ñāṇena paricchijja parituletvā. Adhivāsesīti tā abhibhavanto yathāparimadditākārasallakkhaṇena attani āropetvā vāsesi, na tāhi abhibhuyyamāno. Tenāha “avihaññamāno”tiādi. Adukkhiyamānoti cetodukkhavasena adukkhiyamāno[M 2.0145], kāyadukkhaṃ pana “natthī”ti na sakkā vattuṃ. Asati hi tasmiṃ adhivāsanāya eva asambhavoti. Anāmantetvāti anālapitvā. Anapaloketvāti avissajjitvā. Tenāha “ovādānusāsaniṃ adatvāti vuttaṃ hotī”ti. Pubbabhāgavīriyenāti phalasamāpattiyā parikammavīriyena. Phalasamāpattivīriyenāti phalasamāpattisampayuttavīriyena. Vikkhambhetvāti [V 2.0130] vinodetvā. Yathā nāma pupphanasamaye campakādirukkhe vekhe dinne yāva so vekho nāpanīyati, tāvassa pupphanasamatthatā vikkhambhitā vinoditā hoti, evameva yathāvuttavīriyavekhadānena tā vedanā satthu sarīre yathāparicchinnaṃ kālaṃ vikkhambhitā vinoditā ahesuṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “vikkhambhetvāti vinodetvā”ti. Jīvitampi jīvitasaṅkhāro kammunā saṅkharīyatīti katvā. Chijjamānaṃ virodhipaccayasamāyogena payogasampattiyā ghaṭetvā ṭhapīyati. Adhiṭṭhāyāti adhiṭṭhānaṃ katvā. Tenāha “dasamāse mā uppajjitthāti samāpattiṃ samāpajjī”ti. Taṃ pana “adhiṭṭhānaṃ, pavattana”nti ca vattabbataṃ arahatīti vuttaṃ “adhiṭṭhahitvā pavattetvā”ti.

164. Harsh: rough; the meaning is 'weighty'. A disease of incompatible elements: a severe illness arisen from an imbalance of bodily elements, not merely a minor ailment. Having discerned with knowledge: having thoroughly discerned and weighed the momentary nature, suffering, and emptiness of feelings with knowledge as they truly are. Endured: overcoming them, having imposed them on himself by recognizing their nature as if crushed, not being overwhelmed by them. Hence it is said, 'without being afflicted,' etc. Without suffering: not suffering in terms of mental suffering, though bodily pain cannot be said to be absent. For if it were absent, endurance would be simply impossible. Without informing: without addressing. Without taking leave: without dismissing. Hence it is said, 'which means without giving instruction or advice.' With preliminary effort: the effort of preliminary work for fruition attainment. With fruition attainment effort: the effort associated with fruition attainment. Suppressed: eliminated. Just as when a wedge is inserted into a champaka tree or similar tree during the flowering season, its capacity to flower is suppressed until that wedge is removed, so too those feelings in the Teacher’s body were suppressed and eliminated for the determined period through the aforementioned effort of applying a wedge. Therefore, it is said, 'suppressed: eliminated.' Even life: because the life-formation is conditioned by kamma. Though it is being cut off, it is maintained by the success of application through the conjunction of opposing conditions. Having resolved: having made a determination. Hence it is said, 'he entered absorption resolving, "Let it not arise for ten months."' Moreover, it is fit to be called 'determination and maintenance,' hence it is said, 'having determined and maintained.'

Khaṇikasamāpattīti tādisaṃ pubbābhisaṅkhāraṃ akatvā ṭhānaso samāpajjitabbasamāpatti. Puna sarīraṃ vedanā ajjhottharati savisesapubbābhisaṅkhārassa akatattā. Rūpasattakaarūpasattakāni visuddhimaggasaṃvaṇṇanāsu [P 2.0187] (visuddhi. ṭī. 2.706, 717) vitthāritanayena veditabbāni. Suṭṭhu vikkhambheti pubbābhisaṅkhārassa sātisayattā. Idāni tamatthaṃ upamāya vibhāvetuṃ “yathā nāmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Apabyūḷhoti apanīto. Cuddasahākārehi sannetvāti tesaṃyeva rūpasattakaarūpasattakānaṃ vasena cuddasahi pakārehi vipassanācittaṃ, sakalameva vā attabhāvaṃ visabhāgarogasañjanitalūkhabhāvanirogakaraṇāya sinehetvā na uppajjiyeva sammāsambuddhena sātisayasamāpattivegena suvikkhambhitattā.

The momentary attainment: an attainment that should be entered immediately without making such a prior preparation. Moreover, feeling overwhelms the body because a special prior preparation was not made. The seven rūpa and seven arūpa [attainments] should be understood in detail in the manner explained in the commentaries on the Visuddhimagga (Visuddhi. Ṭī. 2.706, 717). It thoroughly suppresses [it] due to the superior nature of the prior preparation. Now, to explain that meaning by way of simile, 'Just as...' etc. has been said. Apabyūḷha: removed. Having connected with fourteen aspects: having anointed the vipassanā consciousness, or even the entire personality, in fourteen ways based on those same seven rūpa and seven arūpa [attainments], in order to remove the coarseness produced by a disease of dissimilarity and to restore health, [the feeling] does not even arise because it has been thoroughly suppressed by the overwhelmingly powerful attainment-force of the Sammāsambuddha.

Gilāno hutvā puna vuṭṭhitoti pubbe gilāno hutvā puna tato gilānabhāvato vuṭṭhito. Madhurakabhāvo nāma sarīrassa thambhitattaṃ, taṃ pana garubhāvapubbakanti āha “sañjātagarubhāvo sañjātathaddhabhāvo”ti. “Nānākārato na upaṭṭhahantī”ti iminā disāsammohopi me ahosi [M 2.0146] sokabalenāti dasseti. Satipaṭṭhānādidhammāti kāyānupassanādayo anupassanādhammā pubbe vibhūtā hutvā upaṭṭhahantāpi idāni mayhaṃ pākaṭā na honti.

'Having been sick, then risen again': previously having been sick and then having arisen from that state of sickness. 'Sweetness of body' means stiffness of the body; it is said to be preceded by heaviness: 'Heaviness has arisen, stiffness has arisen.' 'They do not attend in various ways': this shows that even disorientation arose in me due to the power of grief. 'The phenomena of the foundations of mindfulness, etc.': the contemplations such as contemplation of the body, etc., which, although having been clear and attending previously, are now not apparent to me.

165. Abbhantaraṃ karoti nāma attaniyeva ṭhapanato. Puggalaṃ abbhantaraṃ karoti nāma samānattatāvasena dhammena pubbe tassa saṅgaṇhato. Daharakāleti attano daharakāle. Kassaci akathetvāti kassaci attano antevāsikassa upanigūhabhūtaṃ ganthaṃ akathetvā. Muṭṭhiṃ katvāti muṭṭhigataṃ viya rahasibhūtaṃ katvā. Yasmiṃ vā naṭṭhe sabbo taṃmūlako dhammo vinassati, so ādito mūlabhūto dhammo, mussati vinassati dhammo etena naṭṭhenāti muṭṭhi, taṃ tathārūpaṃ muṭṭhiṃ katvā pariharitvā ṭhapitaṃ kiñci natthīti dasseti.

165. 'Makes internal' means because of establishing it in oneself. 'Makes a person internal' means previously gathering that person with the Dhamma through a quality of similarity. 'In youth': in one's own youth. 'Without telling anyone': without telling a text that was kept hidden from any of one's own resident disciples. 'Making a fist': making it like something held in a closed fist, having made it secret. 'When what is lost, all the Dhamma rooted in it is destroyed'—that Dhamma, being the root from the beginning, is the 'fist'; when this is lost, the Dhamma is destroyed—this shows that there is nothing at all that was made into such a 'fist', preserved, and kept.

Ahamevāti [V 2.0131] avadhāraṇaṃ bhikkhusaṅghapariharaṇassa aññasādhāraṇicchādassanatthaṃ, avadhāraṇena pana vinā “ahaṃ bhikkhusaṅgha”ntiādi bhikkhusaṅghapariharaṇe ahaṃkāramamaṃkārābhāvadassananti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Uddisitabbaṭṭhenāti “satthā”ti uddisitabbaṭṭhena. Mā vā [P 2.0188] ahesuṃ bhikkhūti adhippāyo. “Mā vā ahosī”ti vā pāṭho. Evaṃ na hotīti “ahaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharissāmī”tiādi ākārena cittappavatti na hoti. “Pacchimavayaanuppattabhāvadīpanatthaṃ vutta”nti iminā vayo viya buddhakiccampi pariyositakammanti dīpeti. Sakaṭassa bāhappadese daḷhībhāvāya veṭhadānaṃ bāhabandho. Cakkanemisandhīnaṃ daḷhībhāvāya veṭhadānaṃ cakkabandho.

‘Ahameva’ (only I) is an emphatic particle used to show that sustaining the Saṅgha is not common to others. However, it should be understood that even without this emphatic particle, in sustaining the Saṅgha, as in ‘I sustain the Saṅgha’ and so on, there is an absence of ‘I-making’ and ‘mine-making’. ‘Uddisitabbaṭṭhena’: by way of what is to be designated, such as ‘the Teacher.’ The intention is, ‘May there not be such monks,’ or alternatively, the reading may be ‘May it not be so.’ Thus, it does not happen: meaning there is no mental activity in the form of ‘I will sustain the Saṅgha’ and so on. ‘Said to indicate the state of having reached the final age’: this reveals that just as his age is advanced, the Buddha’s task is also a completed action. The wrapping around the shaft-area of a cart for firmness is called ‘bāhabandho’ (shaft-binding). The wrapping around the joints of the wheel-rim for firmness is called ‘cakkabandho’ (wheel-binding).

Tamatthanti veṭhamissakena maññeti vuttamatthaṃ. Rūpādayo eva dhammā saviggaho viya upaṭṭhānato rūpanimittādayo, tesaṃ rūpanimittādīnaṃ. Lokiyānaṃ vedanānanti yāsaṃ nirodhanena phalasamāpatti samāpajjitabbā, tāsaṃ nirodhā phāsu hoti, tathā bāḷhavedanābhitunnasarīrassāpi. Tadatthāyāti phalasamāpattivihāratthāya. Dvīhi bhāgehi āpo gato etthāti dīpo, oghena parigato hutvā anajjhotthaṭo bhūmibhāgo, idha pana catūhipi oghehi, saṃsāramahogheneva vā anajjhotthaṭo attā “dīpo”ti adhippeto. Tenāha “mahāsamuddagatā”tiādi. Attassaraṇāti attappaṭisaraṇā. Attagatikā vāti attaparāyaṇāva[M 2.0147]. Mā aññagatikāti aññaṃ kiñci gatiṃ paṭisaraṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ mā cintayittha. Kasmā? Attā nāmettha paramatthato dhammo abbhantaraṭṭhena, so evaṃ sampādito tumhākaṃ dīpaṃ tāṇaṃ gati parāyaṇanti. Tena vuttaṃ “dhammadīpā”tiādi. Tathā cāha “attā hi attano nātho, ko hi nātho paro siyā”ti (dha. pa. 160, 380) upadesamattameva [P 2.0189] hi parasmiṃ paṭibaddhaṃ, aññā sabbā sampatti purisassa attādhīnā eva. Tenāha bhagavā “tumhehi kiccaṃ ātappaṃ, akkhātāro tathāgatā”ti (dha. pa. 276). Tamaggeti tamayogassa agge tassa atikkantābhāvato. Tenevāha “ime aggatamā”tiādi. Mamāti mama sāsane. Sabbepi te catusatipaṭṭhānagocarā vāti catubbidhaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ bhāvetvā brūhetvā tadeva gocaraṃ attano pavattiṭṭhānaṃ katvā ṭhitā eva bhikkhū agge bhavissanti.

That meaning: the meaning stated in the phrase, 'one thinks it is kept going with wrappings.' The phenomena such as form, etc., are called 'signs of form' and so on because they appear as if with substance. Regarding 'worldly feelings': the cessation of those feelings by which fruition attainment is to be attained brings ease, just as it does for one whose body is tormented by severe pain. 'For that purpose': for the purpose of dwelling in the fruition attainment. 'An island' (dīpo): this is an etymological explanation where water (āpo) has gone on two (dvi) sides, a piece of land surrounded and not submerged by a flood; but here, 'island' refers to the self, not submerged by the four floods or by the great flood of saṃsāra. Hence, it is said, 'like an island in the great ocean,' etc. 'Self as refuge': self as resort. 'Self as destination' (attagatikā): devoted to oneself. 'Do not have another destination': do not consider anything else as a destination, resort, or final support. Why? Because, in the ultimate sense, the self here is the internal Dhamma. When it is thus accomplished, it becomes your island, shelter, destination, and final support. Therefore, it is said, 'with the Dhamma as an island,' etc. Similarly, it is said: 'One is indeed one’s own refuge, for who else could be a refuge?' (Dhammapada 160, 380). For instruction is all that depends on another; all other accomplishment depends solely on oneself. Hence, the Blessed One said: 'You yourselves must strive; the Tathāgatas are only proclaimers' (Dhammapada 276). 'At the peak of darkness' (tamagge): at the peak of connection with darkness, because it is not surpassed. Therefore, it is said, 'these are the foremost,' etc. 'My': in my dispensation. 'All those who have the four establishments of mindfulness as their pasture': those monks who, having developed and cultivated the fourfold establishment of mindfulness, making that very thing their pasture and abiding place—they will be the foremost.

Dutiyabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the second recitation section is concluded.

Nimittobhāsakathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Discourse on the Manifestation of Signs

166. Anekavāraṃ [V 2.0132] bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati, tasmā imaṃ vesālippavesanaṃ niyametvā dassetuṃ “kadā pāvisī”ti pucchitvā āgamanato paṭṭhāya taṃ dassento “bhagavā kirā”tiādimāha. Āgatamaggenevāti pubbe yāva veḷuvagāmakā āgatamaggeneva paṭinivattento. Yathāparicchedenāti yathāparicchinnakālena. Tatoti phalasamāpattito. Ayanti idāni vuccamānākāro. Divāṭṭhānolokanādi parinibbānassa ekantikabhāvadassanaṃ. Ossaṭṭhoti vissaṭṭho āyusaṅkhāro “sattāhameva mayā jīvitabba”nti.

166. The Blessed One dwelt in Vesālī many times. Therefore, to specify and show this entry into Vesālī, having asked, 'When did he enter?', and then, showing it from the time of his arrival, he said, 'The Blessed One, it is said,' and so on. 'By the very path he had come' means turning back by the very path he had come as far as the village of Veḷuva. 'According to the fixed time' means according to the predetermined time. 'From that' means from the fruition attainment. 'This' refers to the manner now being stated. The inspection of the daytime dwelling place and so on shows the certainty of his final passing away. 'Relinquished' means the life-formation was released, with the thought, 'I must live for only seven more days.'

Jeṭṭhakaniṭṭhabhātikānanti sabbeva sabrahmacārino sandhāya vadati.

'Of elder and younger brothers' means he speaks referring to all fellow practitioners of the holy life.

Paṭipādessāmīti maggapaṭipattiyā niyojessāmi. Maṇiphalaketi maṇikhacite pamukhe atthataphalake. Taṃ paṭhamaṃ [P 2.0190] dassananti yaṃ veḷuvane paribbājakarūpena āgatassa siddhaṃ dassanaṃ, taṃ paṭhamadassanaṃ. Yaṃ vā anomadassissa bhagavato vacanaṃ saddahantena tadā abhinīhārakāle paccakkhato [M 2.0148] viya tumhākaṃ dassanaṃ siddhaṃ, taṃ paṭhamadassanaṃ. Paccāgamanacārikanti paccāgamanatthaṃ cārikaṃ.

'I will instruct' means I will engage them in the practice of the path. 'On a jeweled slab' means on a spread-out slab inlaid with jewels in a prominent place. 'That first sight' refers to the successful vision when he came to the Veḷuvana in the guise of a wanderer—that was the first vision. Or, it refers to the successful vision you had at the time of making the aspiration, as if seeing directly, when you had faith in the words of the Blessed One Anomadassī—that was the first vision. 'A journey of return' means a journey for the purpose of returning.

Sattāhanti accantasaṃyoge upayogavacanaṃ. Therassa jātovarakagehaṃ kira itaragehato vivekaṭṭhaṃ, vivaṭaṅgaṇañca, tasmā devabrahmānaṃ upasaṅkamanayogyanti “jātovarakaṃ paṭijaggathā”ti vuttaṃ. Soti uparevato. Taṃ pavattinti tattha vasitukāmatāya vuttaṃ taṃ.

'For seven days' is a usage in the sense of continuous duration. It is said that the elder's jātovaraka house was a place of seclusion from other houses and had an open courtyard, thus being suitable for the approach of devas and Brahmās—hence it was said, 'Attend to the jātovaraka.' 'He' refers to Uparevata. 'That statement' means it was said because of his desire to dwell there.

“Jānantāpi tathāgatā pucchantī”ti (pārā. 16, 165) iminā nīhārena thero “ke tumhe”ti pucchi. “Tvaṃ catūhi mahārājehi mahantataro”ti puṭṭho attano mahattaṃ satthu upari pakkhipanto “ārāmikasadisā ete upāsike amhākaṃ satthuno”ti āha. Sāvakasampattikittanampi hi atthato satthu sampattiṃyeva vibhāveti.

In accordance with the principle, 'Tathāgatas ask, even though they know' (Pārā. 16, 165), the elder asked, 'Who are you?' When asked, 'Are you greater than the four great kings?', attributing his own greatness to the Teacher, he said, 'These laywomen are like monastery attendants to our Teacher.' For praising the disciples’ attainments also, in essence, reveals the Teacher’s attainments.

Sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhāyāti therassa desanānubhāvena, attano ca upanissayasampattiyā ñāṇassa paripakkattā sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhahitvā.

'Having been established in the fruit of stream-entry' means: having become established in the fruit of stream-entry through the power of the Elder’s teaching and the fulfillment of his own supporting conditions, due to the ripening of his knowledge.

Ayanti [V 2.0133] yathāvuttā. Etthāti “vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisī”ti etasmiṃ vesālīpavese. Anupubbīkathāti anupubbadīpanī kathā.

'This' refers to what was said earlier. 'Here' refers to the phrase 'he entered Vesālī for alms,' that is, this entering of Vesālī. 'Gradual discourse' means a discourse that unfolds step by step.

167. Udenayakkhassa cetiyaṭṭhāneti udenassa nāma yakkhassa āyatanabhāvena iṭṭhakāhi cite mahājanassa cittīkataṭṭhāne. Katavihāroti bhagavantaṃ uddissa katavihāro. Vuccatīti purimavohārena “udenacetiya”nti vuccati. Gotamakādīsupīti “gotamakacetiya”nti evaṃ ādīsupi. Eseva nayoti cetiyaṭṭhāne katavihārabhāvaṃ atidisati. Vaḍḍhitāti [P 2.0191] bhāvanāpāripūrivasena paribrūhitā. Punappunaṃ katāti bhāvanāya bahulīkaraṇena aparāparaṃ pavattitā. Yuttayānaṃ viya katāti yathā yuttaṃ ājaññayānaṃ chekena sārathinā adhiṭṭhitaṃ yathāruci pavattati, evaṃ yathārucipavattirahataṃ gamitā. Patiṭṭhānaṭṭhenāti adhiṭṭhānaṭṭhena. Vatthu viya katāti sabbaso upakkilesavisodhanena iddhivisayatāya pavattiṭṭhānabhāvato suvisodhitaparissayavatthu viya katā. Adhiṭṭhitāti paṭipakkhadūrībhāvato subhāvitabhāvena taṃtaṃadhiṭṭhānayogyatāya ṭhapitā[M 2.0149]. Samantato citāti sabbabhāgena bhāvanupacayaṃ gamitā. Tenāha “suvaḍḍhitā”ti. Suṭṭhu samāraddhāti iddhibhāvanāya sikhāppattiyā sammadeva saṃsevitā.

167. 'At the shrine of the yakkha Udena' means at the place revered by the populace, built up with bricks as a dwelling for the yakkha named Udena. 'A dwelling was made' means a dwelling was made dedicated to the Blessed One. 'It is called' means by former usage it is called the 'Udena shrine.' 'In the case of Gotamaka and others as well' means 'Gotamaka shrine,' and so on. 'This is the same method' extends the principle of a dwelling being made at a shrine site. 'Well-developed' means augmented by way of the perfection of cultivation. 'Repeatedly done' means made to occur repeatedly by the frequent practice of cultivation. 'Made like a yoked vehicle' means just as a yoked thoroughbred vehicle, controlled by a skilled charioteer, proceeds as desired, so too it is brought to a state of proceeding as desired, free from hindrance. 'In the sense of a foundation' means in the sense of a determination. 'Made like a basis' means made like a well-purified basis free from dangers, because of being a place for the occurrence of the sphere of psychic power through the complete purification of defilements. 'Determined' means established in its suitability for this or that determination because of being well-developed through the removal of opposing factors. 'Accumulated on all sides' means brought to an accumulation of cultivation in every part. Therefore he said, 'well-developed.' 'Well undertaken' means properly practiced by means of the cultivation of psychic power that has reached its peak.

Aniyamenāti “yassa kassacī”ti aniyamavacanena. Niyametvāti “tathāgatassā”ti sarūpadassanena niyametvā. Āyuppamāṇanti paramāyuppamāṇaṃ vadati, tasseva gahaṇe kāraṇaṃ brahmajālasuttavaṇṇanāyaṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.40; dī. ni. ṭī. 1.40) vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Mahāsivatthero pana “mahābodhisattānaṃ carimabhave paṭisandhidāyino kammassa asaṅkhyeyyāyukatāsaṃvattanasamatthataṃ hadaye ṭhapetvā buddhānaṃ āyusaṅkhārassa parissayavikkhambhanasamatthatā pāḷiyaṃ āgatā evāti imaṃ bhaddakappameva tiṭṭheyyā”ti avoca. “Khaṇḍiccādīhi abhibhuyyatī”ti etena yathā iddhibalena jarāya na paṭighāto, evaṃ tena maraṇassapi na paṭighātoti atthato āpannamevāti. “Kva saro khitto, kva ca nipatito”ti aññathā vuṭṭhitenāpi theravādena aṭṭhakathāvacanameva samatthitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ[P 2.0192]. Tenāha “so na ruccati…pe… niyamita”nti.

'Without restriction' means by the unrestricted statement 'for anyone.' 'Having restricted' means having restricted by showing the specific form with 'for the Tathāgata.' 'The measure of life' refers to the maximum measure of life; the reason for taking it as such should be understood in the same way as explained in the commentary on the Brahmajāla Sutta (Dī. Ni. Aṭṭha. 1.40; Dī. Ni. Ṭī. 1.40). However, the Elder Mahāsiva said, 'Keeping in mind that the kamma giving rebirth for great bodhisattvas in their final existence is capable of bringing about an incalculable lifespan, and that the power of a Buddha's life-formation to suppress dangers is indeed stated in the Pāli, he could remain for this entire auspicious aeon.' By this 'is overcome by broken teeth, etc.', it is in effect implied that just as psychic power cannot counteract old age, so too it cannot counteract death. 'Where was the arrow shot, and where did it fall?'—it should be seen that even though the elder's view arose otherwise, only the statement of the commentary is supported. Therefore it is said, 'That is not acceptable... (etc.)... restricted.'

Pariyuṭṭhitacittoti yathā kiñci atthānatthaṃ sallakkhetuṃ na sakkā, evaṃ abhibhūtacitto. So pana abhibhavo mahatā udakoghena appakassa udakassa ajjhottharaṇaṃ viya ahosīti vuttaṃ “ajjhotthaṭacitto”ti. Aññopīti therato, ariyehi vā aññopi yo koci puthujjano. Puthujjanaggahaṇañcettha yathā sabbena sabbaṃ appahīnavipallāso mārena pariyuṭṭhitacitto kiñci [V 2.0134] atthaṃ sallakkhetuṃ na sakkoti, evaṃ thero bhagavatā kataṃ nimittobhāsaṃ sabbaso na sallakkhesīti dassanatthaṃ. Tenāha “māro hī”tiādi. Cattāro vipallāsāti asubhe “subha”nti saññāvipallāso, cittavipallāso, dukkhe “sukha”nti saññāvipallāso, cittavipallāsoti ime cattāro vipallāsā. Tenāti yadipi itare aṭṭha vipallāsā pahīnā, tathāpi yathāvuttānaṃ catunnaṃ vipallāsānaṃ appahīnabhāvena. Assāti therassa. Maddatīti phusanamattena maddanto viya hoti, aññathā tena maddite sattānaṃ maraṇameva siyā. Kiṃ sakkhissati, na sakkhissatīti adhippāyo. Kasmā [M 2.0150] na sakkhissati, nanu esa aggasāvakassa kucchiṃ paviṭṭhoti? Saccaṃ paviṭṭho, tañca kho attano ānubhāvadassanatthaṃ, na vibādhanādhippāyena. Vibādhanādhippāyena pana idha “kiṃ sakkhissatī”ti vuttaṃ hadayamaddanassa adhigatattā. Nimittobhāsanti ettha “tiṭṭhatu bhagavā kappa”nti sakalakappaṃ avaṭṭhānayācanāya “yassa kassaci ānanda cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā”tiādinā aññāpadesena attano caturiddhipādabhāvanānubhāvena kappaṃ avaṭṭhānasamatthatāvasena saññuppādanaṃ nimittaṃ, tathā pana pariyāyaṃ muñcitvā ujukaṃyeva attano adhippāyavibhāvanaṃ obhāso. Jānantoyeva vāti mārena pariyuṭṭhitabhāvaṃ jānanto eva. Attano aparādhahetuto [P 2.0193] sattānaṃ soko tanuko hoti, na balavāti āha “dosāropanena sokatanukaraṇattha”nti. Kiṃ pana thero mārena pariyuṭṭhitacittakāle pavattiṃ pacchā jānātīti? Na jānāti sabhāvena, buddhānubhāvena pana anujānāti.

'The mind is overwhelmed' means that one cannot discern what is beneficial or harmful; thus, the mind is overpowered. This overpowering was like a small amount of water being submerged by a great flood; hence, it is said, 'the mind is submerged.' 'Another' refers to any ordinary person other than the Elder or the Noble Ones. The inclusion of 'ordinary person' is to show that just as one whose distortions are entirely unabandoned has their mind overwhelmed by Māra and cannot discern any benefit, so too the Elder did not at all discern the sign and manifestation made by the Blessed One. This is the meaning to be shown. Therefore, it is said, 'For Māra…' and so on. 'The four distortions' are: the distortion of perception and the distortion of mind in perceiving the unattractive as 'attractive,' and the distortion of perception and the distortion of mind in perceiving suffering as 'pleasure'—these are the four distortions. 'Therefore' means: even if the other eight distortions are abandoned, it is due to the non-abandonment of these four distortions as described. 'Of him' means of the Elder. 'Crushes' means it is as if crushing by mere touch; otherwise, if beings were truly crushed by him, death would result. 'What will he be able to do?' The intention is: 'He will not be able to do anything.' Why will he not be able to do anything? Did he not enter the belly of the chief disciple? It is true he entered, but that was to display his own power, not with the intent to harm. Here, however, 'What will he be able to do?' is said because the crushing of the heart is what is meant. Regarding 'sign and manifestation': here, the 'sign' is the creation of an awareness of his capability to remain for an aeon through the power of having developed the four bases of psychic power, indicated indirectly by the statement beginning, 'Ānanda, for whomever the four bases of psychic power have been developed…' as a way of inviting the request, 'Let the Blessed One remain for an aeon.' The 'manifestation,' however, is the direct revelation of his own intention, setting aside such indirect phrasing. 'Or, though knowing' means knowing that he was overwhelmed by Māra. It is said 'for the purpose of lessening grief by assigning blame' because the grief of beings on account of their own fault is slight, not strong. But does the Elder afterwards know what occurred when his mind was overwhelmed by Māra? He does not know by his own nature, but through the Buddha's power, he comes to understand.

Mārayācanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Māra's Request

168. Anatthe niyojento guṇamāraṇena māreti, virāgavibandhanena vā jātinimittatāya tattha tattha jātaṃ jātaṃ mārento viya hotīti “māretīti māro”ti vuttaṃ. Ativiya pāpatāya pāpimā. Kaṇhadhammehi samannāgato kaṇho. Virāgādiguṇānaṃ antakaraṇato antako. Sattānaṃ anatthāvahapaṭipattiṃ na muccatīti namuci. Attano mārapāsena pamatte bandhati, pamattā vā bandhū etassāti pamattabandhu. Sattamasattāhato paraṃ satta ahāni sandhāyāha “aṭṭhame sattāhe”ti na pana pallaṅkasattāhādi viya niyatakiccassa aṭṭhamasattāhassa nāma labbhanato. Sattamasattāhassa hi parato ajapālanigrodhamūle mahābrahmuno, sakkassa ca devarañño paṭiññātadhammadesanaṃ bhagavantaṃ ñatvā “idāni satte dhammadesanāya mama visayaṃ atikkamāpessatī”ti sañjātadomanasso hutvā ṭhito cintesi “handa dānāhaṃ naṃ upāyena parinibbāpessāmi, evamassa manoratho aññathattaṃ gamissati, mama ca manoratho ijjhissatī”ti[V 2.0135]. Evaṃ pana cintetvā bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃ antaṃ ṭhito “parinibbātu dāni bhante bhagavā”tiādinā parinibbānaṃ yāci, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “aṭṭhame sattāhe”tiādi. Tattha ajjāti āyusaṅkhārossajjanadivasaṃ sandhāyāha. Bhagavā cassa abhisandhiṃ jānantopi [M 2.0151] taṃ anāvikatvā parinibbānassa akālabhāvameva pakāsento yācanaṃ paṭikkhipi. Tenāha “na tāvāha”ntiādi.

168. He is called 'Māra' because 'he kills' (`māreti`), by engaging beings in what is unbeneficial, by destroying their wholesome qualities, or by obstructing dispassion; or, because he is like one who kills whatever is born here and there, due to birth being his mark. Due to his excessive evil, he is Pāpimā, 'the Evil One.' Endowed with dark qualities, he is Kaṇha, 'the Dark One.' Because he makes an end (`antakaraṇato`) of virtues such as dispassion, he is Antaka, 'the Ender.' Because he does not release (`na muccati`) beings from the practice that brings them disadvantage, he is Namuci. Because he binds the heedless with his snare, or because the heedless are his kinsmen, he is Pamattabandhu, 'the Kinsman of the Heedless.' Regarding 'in the eighth week,' this refers to the seven days after the seventh week; it is not that an 'eighth week' with a fixed duty, like the weeks at the Bodhi-seat, is found by that name. For after the seventh week, at the foot of the Ajapāla Banyan Tree, Māra learned that the Blessed One had assented to teach the Dhamma to Mahābrahmā and Sakka, king of the devas. He became distressed and stood there thinking, 'Now, by teaching the Dhamma, he will cause beings to transcend my domain.' He pondered, 'Come now, I shall by some means cause him to attain final Nibbāna. In this way, his aspiration will be altered, and my own aspiration will succeed.' Having thought thus, he approached the Blessed One, stood to one side, and requested his final Nibbāna, saying, 'Venerable sir, let the Blessed One now attain final Nibbāna,' and so on. It is with reference to this that it is said, 'in the eighth week,' and so on. Therein, 'today' refers to the day of relinquishing the life-force. And the Blessed One, though knowing his intention, did not reveal it but rejected the request, making it clear that it was not the time for his final Nibbāna. Therefore, he said, 'Not yet shall I…' and so on.

Maggavasena viyattāti saccasampaṭivedhaveyyattiyena byattā. Tatheva vinītāti maggavasena kilesānaṃ samucchedavinayanena vinītā. Tathā visāradāti ariyamaggādhigameneva satthusāsane vesārajjappattiyā visāradā[P 2.0194], sārajjakarānaṃ diṭṭhivicikicchādipāpadhammānaṃ vigamena visāradabhāvaṃ pattāti attho. Yassa sutassa vasena vaṭṭadukkhato nissaraṇaṃ sambhavati, taṃ idha ukkaṭṭhaniddesena “suta”nti adhippetanti āha “tepiṭakavasenā”ti. Tiṇṇaṃ piṭakānaṃ samūho tepiṭakaṃ, tīṇi vā piṭakāni tipiṭakaṃ, tipiṭakameva tepiṭakaṃ, tassa vasena. Tamevāti yaṃ taṃ tepiṭakaṃ sotabbabhāvena “suta”nti vuttaṃ, tameva. Dhammanti pariyattidhammaṃ. Dhārentīti suvaṇṇabhājane pakkhittasīhavasaṃ viya avinassantaṃ katvā suppaguṇasuppavattibhāvena dhārenti hadaye ṭhapenti. Iti pariyattidhammavasena bahussutadhammadharabhāvaṃ dassetvā idāni paṭivedhadhammavasenapi taṃ dassetuṃ “atha vā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ariyadhammassāti maggaphaladhammassa, navavidhassāpi vā lokuttaradhammassa. Anudhammabhūtanti adhigamāya anurūpadhammabhūtaṃ. Anucchavikapaṭipadanti ca tameva vipassanādhammamāha, chabbidhā visuddhiyo vā. Anudhammanti tassā yathāvuttapaṭipadāya anurūpaṃ abhisallekhitaṃ appicchatādidhammaṃ. Caraṇasīlāti samādāya pavattanasīlā. Anu maggaphaladhammo etissāti vā anudhammā, vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanā, tassā caraṇasīlā. Attano ācariyavādanti attano ācariyassa sammāsambuddhassa vādaṃ. Sadevakassa lokassa ācārasikkhāpanena ācariyo, bhagavā. Tassa vādo, catusaccadesanā.

'Skilled' (`viyattā`) means skilled by means of the path, that is, accomplished through the dexterity of penetrating the truths. Likewise, 'trained' (`vinītā`) means trained by means of the path, that is, through the removal of defilements by eradication. Similarly, 'confident' (`visāradā`) means they have attained confidence through the very attainment of the noble path, having reached fearlessness in the Teacher’s dispensation; the meaning is that they have attained a state of confidence through the removal of evil states that cause diffidence, such as wrong views and doubt. That 'learning' (`suta`) by means of which escape from the suffering of the cycle of existence is possible is here intended in its highest sense; thus, it is said, 'by means of the Tipiṭaka.' The Tipiṭaka is the collection of the three Piṭakas, or the three Piṭakas are the Tipiṭaka, or the Tipiṭaka is simply the Tipiṭaka; by means of it. 'That very thing' means that very Tipiṭaka which is called 'learning' because it is to be heard. 'Dhamma' means the textual Dhamma. 'They bear it' means they bear it in their hearts, making it imperishable like lion’s fat placed in a golden vessel, by being well-versed and proficient in it. Having thus shown the state of being learned and a bearer of the Dhamma by way of the textual Dhamma, now to show it also by way of the realized Dhamma, it is said, 'Or else…' and so on. 'Of the noble Dhamma' means of the Dhamma of the path and fruition, or of the ninefold supramundane Dhamma. 'Being in conformity with the Dhamma' means being the Dhamma that is suitable for attainment. And 'suitable practice' refers to that very insight-Dhamma, or the six kinds of purification. 'In conformity with the Dhamma' means the austere qualities, such as fewness of wishes, that are in accordance with the aforesaid practice. 'Of the nature of practicing' means of the nature of undertaking and practicing it. Or alternatively, `anudhammā` is that which is followed by (`anu`) the Dhamma of the path and fruition; this is insight leading to emergence. 'Of the nature of practicing it' refers to that. 'Their own teacher’s doctrine' means the doctrine of their own teacher, the Perfectly Enlightened One. The Blessed One is the teacher (`ācariya`) because he instructs the world with its gods in proper conduct. His doctrine is the teaching of the Four Truths.

Ācikkhissantīti ādito kathessanti, attanā uggahitaniyāmena pare uggaṇhāpessantīti attho. Desessantīti vācessanti, pāḷiṃ sammā pabodhessantīti attho. Paññāpessantīti pajānāpessanti, saṅkāpessantīti attho. Paṭṭhapessantīti pakārehi ṭhapessanti, pakāsessantīti attho. Vivarissantīti vivaṭaṃ karissanti. Vibhajissantīti vibhattaṃ karissanti. Uttāniṃ karissantīti [P 2.0195] anuttānaṃ gambhīraṃ uttānaṃ pākaṭaṃ karissanti. Saha dhammenāti ettha dhamma-saddo kāraṇapariyāyo “hetumhi ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā”tiādīsu [M 2.0152] (vibha. 270) viyāti āha “sahetukena sakāraṇena vacanenā”ti. Sappāṭihāriyanti sanissaraṇaṃ[V 2.0136], yathā paravādaṃ bhañjitvā sakavādo patiṭṭhahati, evaṃ hetudāharaṇehi yathādhigatamatthaṃ sampādetvā dhammaṃ kathessanti. Tenāha “niyyānikaṃ katvā dhammaṃ desessantī”ti, navavidhaṃ lokuttaradhammaṃ pabodhessantīti attho. Ettha ca “paññāpessantī”tiādīhi chahi padehi cha atthapadāni dassitāni, ādito pana dvīhi padehi cha byañjanapadāni. Ettāvatā tepiṭakaṃ buddhavacanaṃ saṃvaṇṇanānayena saṅgahetvā dassitaṃ hoti. Vuttañhetaṃ nettiyaṃ “dvādasapadāni suttaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ byañjanañca attho cā”ti (netti. saṅkhāre).

They will declare: they will speak from the beginning; the meaning is that they will cause others to learn according to the method they themselves have learned. They will teach: they will recite; the meaning is that they will rightly awaken to the Pāli. They will make known: they will cause to understand; the meaning is that they will cause to comprehend. They will establish: they will set forth with explanations; the meaning is that they will make manifest. They will open: they will make it open. They will analyze: they will make it distinct. They will make plain: they will make what is not plain and is deep, plain and evident. With the Dhamma: here, the term 'Dhamma' is a synonym for cause, as in 'knowledge in cause is the analytical knowledge of Dhamma' (Vibh. 270), etc. Thus it is said: 'with reasoned and causative speech.' With a marvel means leading to liberation, just as after refuting another's doctrine, one's own doctrine is established. Thus, with reasons and examples, having accomplished the meaning as they have understood it, they will teach the Dhamma. Therefore, it is said: 'Having made it lead to liberation, they will teach the Dhamma'; the meaning is that they will awaken to the ninefold supramundane Dhamma. And here, by the six terms beginning with 'they will make known,' six terms of meaning are shown; but from the beginning, by two terms, six terms of wording are shown. By this much, the Tipiṭaka, the Buddha's word, is shown, having been summarized by the method of commentary. For this is said in the Netti: 'The twelve terms are the teaching; all of that is both wording and meaning' (Netti. Saṅkhāre).

Sikkhattayasaṅgahitanti adhisīlasikkhādisikkhattayasaṅgahaṇaṃ. Sakalaṃ sāsanabrahmacariyanti anavasesaṃ satthusāsanabhūtaṃ seṭṭhacariyaṃ. Samiddhanti sammadeva vaḍḍhitaṃ. Jhānassādavasenāti tehi tehi bhikkhūhi samadhigatajhānasukhavasena. Vuddhippattanti uḷārapaṇītabhāvagamanena sabbaso parivuddhiṃ upagataṃ. Sabbapāliphullaṃ viya abhiññāsampattivasena abhiññāsampadāhi sāsanābhivuddhiyā matthakappattito. Patiṭṭhitavasenāti patiṭṭhānavasena, patiṭṭhappattiyāti attho. Paṭivedhavasena bahuno janassa hitanti bāhujaññaṃ. Tenāha “bahujanābhisamayavasenā”ti. Puthu puthulaṃ bhūtaṃ jātaṃ, puthu vā puthuttaṃ bhūtaṃ pattanti [P 2.0196] puthubhūtaṃ. Tenāha “sabbākāra…pe… patta”nti. Suṭṭhu pakāsitanti suṭṭhu sammadeva ādikalyāṇādibhāvena paveditaṃ.

'Embraced by the threefold training' means the embracing of the threefold training, beginning with the training in higher virtue. 'The entire holy life of the dispensation' means the complete, excellent conduct that is the Teacher's dispensation. 'Flourished' means rightly increased. 'Through the delight in jhāna' means by the power of the bliss of jhāna attained by those various monks. 'Reached growth' means having in every way attained complete growth through reaching a state of excellence and refinement. 'Like a fully blossomed tree' means because of reaching the peak of the dispensation's growth through the accomplishments of direct knowledge, by the power of the attainment of direct knowledge. 'By being established' means by the basis of establishment; the meaning is having reached stability. 'For the welfare of many people through penetration' is for the benefit of the multitude. Therefore, it is said: 'by the power of the realization of many.' 'Widespread' means having become extensive, having arisen; or having become, having attained, extensiveness. Therefore, it is said: 'attained in every way….' 'Well proclaimed' means well and rightly made known through being good in the beginning, etc.

Āyusaṅkhāraossajjanavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Relinquishing of the Life-Formation

169. Satiṃ sūpaṭṭhitaṃ katvāti ayaṃ kāyādivibhāgo attabhāvasaññito dukkhabhāro mayā ettakaṃ kālaṃ vahito, idāni pana na vahitabbo, etassa avahanatthaṃ cirataraṃ kālaṃ ariyamaggasambhāro sambhato, svāyaṃ ariyamaggo paṭividdho, yato ime kāyādayo asubhādito sammadeva pariññātā, catubbidhampi sammāsatiṃ yathātathaṃ visaye suṭṭhu upaṭṭhitaṃ katvā. Ñāṇena paricchinditvāti yasmā imassa attabhāvasaññitassa dukkhabhārassa vahane payojanabhūtaṃ attahitaṃ tāva mahābodhimūle eva parisamāpitaṃ, parahitaṃ pana buddhaveneyyavinayanaṃ parisamāpitabbaṃ, taṃ [M 2.0153] idāni māsattayeneva parisamāpanaṃ pāpuṇissati, tasmā abhāsi “visākhapuṇṇamāyaṃ parinibbāyissāmī”ti, evaṃ buddhañāṇena paricchinditvā sabbabhāgena nicchayaṃ katvā. Āyusaṅkhāraṃ vissajjīti āyuno jīvitassa abhisaṅkhārakaṃ phalasamāpattidhammaṃ “na samāpajjissāmī”ti vissajji taṃvissajjaneneva tena abhisaṅkhariyamānaṃ jīvitasaṅkhāraṃ “nappavattessāmī”ti vissajji. Tenāha “tatthā”tiādi. Ṭhānamahantatāyapi pavattiākāramahantatāyapi mahanto pathavīkampo. Tattha ṭhānamahantatāya bhūmicālassa mahattaṃ dassetuṃ [V 2.0137] “tadā kira…pe… kampitthā”ti vuttaṃ. Sā pana jātikkhettabhūtā dasasahassī lokadhātu eva, na yā kāci, yā mahābhinīhāramahājātiādīsupi kampittha. Tadāpi tattikāya eva kampane kiṃ kāraṇaṃ[P 2.0197]? Jātikkhettabhāvena tasseva ādito pariggahassa katattā. Pariggahakaraṇaṃ cassa dhammatāvasena veditabbaṃ. Tathā hi purimabuddhānampi tāvatakameva jātikkhettaṃ ahosi. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “dasasahassī lokadhātū, nissaddā honti nirākulā…pe… mahāsamuddo ābhujati, dasasahassī pakampatī”ti ca ādi (bu. vaṃ. 84-91). Udakapariyantaṃ katvā chappakārapavedhanena avītarāge bhiṃsetīti bhiṃsano, so eva bhiṃsanakoti āha “bhayajanako”ti. Devabheriyoti devadundubhisaddassa pariyāyavacanamattaṃ. Na cettha kāci bherī “devadundubhī”ti adhippetā, atha kho uppātabhāvena labbhamāno ākāsagato nigghosasaddo. Tenāha “devo”tiādi. Devoti megho. Tassa hi acchabhāvena ākāsassa vassābhāvena sukkhagajjitasaññite sadde niccharante devadundubhisamaññā. Tenāha “devo sukkhagajjitaṃ gajjī”ti.

169. Having established mindfulness well: this division of the body, etc., designated as the individual existence, a burden of suffering, has been carried by me for such a long time, but now it is not to be carried. For the purpose of not carrying it, the requisites of the noble path have been accumulated for a very long time. That noble path has been penetrated, whereby this body, etc., have been fully and rightly understood as unattractive, etc. Thus, having established the fourfold right mindfulness well in its object, in accordance with reality. Having delimited with knowledge: because his own welfare, which was the purpose in carrying this burden of suffering designated as the individual existence, was already completed at the foot of the great Bodhi tree, but the welfare of others, the training of those to be tamed by the Buddha, was to be completed, and that would now reach completion in just three months. Therefore, he declared, 'On the full moon day of Visākha, I will attain final Nibbāna.' Thus, having delimited with the Buddha's knowledge, he made a decision in every way. He relinquished the life-formation: he relinquished the state of fruit-attainment which forms life, thinking, 'I will not attain it.' By that very relinquishment, he relinquished the life-formation that was being formed by it, thinking, 'I will not cause it to continue.' Therefore, it is said, 'Therein,' etc. The earthquake was great due to the greatness of the place and also due to the greatness of the manner of its occurrence. Therein, to show the greatness of the earth's shaking due to the greatness of the place, it is said, 'At that time, indeed… it shook.' That was the ten-thousandfold world-sphere, which was the birthplace, and not just any other, which also shook during the great resolve, the great birth, etc. Even then, what was the reason for the shaking of only that much? Because of its being the birthplace, it was taken as such from the beginning. And the taking of it should be understood as being by the nature of things. For even the previous Buddhas had only that much as their birthplace. Thus, it is said: 'The ten-thousandfold world-sphere becomes silent, undisturbed… the great ocean surges, the ten-thousandfold world-sphere shakes,' etc. (Bu.va. 1.84–91). Making the water its limit, with six kinds of trembling, it terrifies those not free from lust, thus it is terrifying (bhiṃsano); that very thing is terrifying (bhiṃsanako), so he says 'fear-producing.' The divine drum is merely a synonym for the sound of the divine drum. Here, no actual drum called 'divine drum' is intended, but rather the resounding sound in the sky which is obtained due to the portentous event. Therefore, it is said, 'The deva,' etc. Deva means a cloud. For when the sky is clear and there is no rain, the sound that issues forth, known as dry thunder, is designated as the 'divine drum.' Therefore, it is said, 'The deva roared with dry thunder.'

Pītivegavissaṭṭhanti “evaṃ cirataraṃ kālaṃ vahito ayaṃ attabhāvasaññito dukkhabhāro, idāni na cirasseva nikkhipissatī”ti sañjātasomanasso bhagavā sabhāveneva pītivegavissaṭṭhaṃ udānaṃ udānesi. Evaṃ pana udānentena ayampi attho sādhito hotīti dassanatthaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “kasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Released by the force of joy: The Blessed One, in whom delight had arisen thinking, 'For such a long time this burden of suffering, designated as the individual existence, has been carried; now, before long, it will be laid down,' naturally uttered an inspired utterance released by the force of joy. To show that by uttering it thus this meaning too is accomplished, in the commentary it is said, 'Why,' etc.

Tulīyatīti tulanti tula-saddo kammasādhanoti dassetuṃ “tulita”nti vuttaṃ. Appānubhāvatāya paricchinnaṃ. Tathā hi taṃ parito khaṇḍitabhāvena “paritta”nti vuccati. Paṭipakkhavikkhambhanato dīghasantānatāya, vipulaphalatāya [M 2.0154] ca na tulaṃ na paricchinnaṃ. Yehi kāraṇehi pubbe avisesato mahaggataṃ “atula”nti vuttaṃ, tāni kāraṇāni [P 2.0198] rūpāvacarato āruppassa sātisayāni vijjantīti “arūpāvacaraṃ atula”nti vuttaṃ, itarañca “tula”nti, appavipākaṃ tīsupi kammesu yaṃ tanuvipākaṃ hīnaṃ, taṃ tulaṃ.
